١١٩٢٤ — عن أبي هريرة قال: كان أهل الكتاب يقرؤون التوراة بالعبرانية، ويفسرونها بالعربية لأهل الإسلام.
فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((لا تصدقوا أهل الكتاب ولا تكذبوهم، وقولوا: ﴿آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْنَا﴾)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٤٤٨٥).
هذا الحديث أصل في وجوب التوقف عما يشكل من الأمور والعلوم؛ فلا يقضى عليه بجواز أو بطلان، ولا بتحليل ولا تحريم.
وقد أمرنا أن نؤمن بالكتب المنزلة على الأنبياء، إلا أن قراء الكتب من اليهود والنصارى قد حرفوا وبدلوا، ولا سبيل لنا إلى العلم بما هو صحيح منها، وأن ما يحكونه عن تلك الكتب هل هو مستقيم.
فأمرنا بالتوقف فيه؛ فلا نصدقهم لئلا نكون شركاء معهم فيما حرفوه وبدلوه، ولا نكذب به؛ فلعله يكون صحيحًا، فنكون منكرين لما أمرنا أن نؤمن به.
ونقول: آمنا بما أنزل اللّٰه من كتاب. أفاده الخطابي في أعلام الحديث (٣/١٨٠١).

11924 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
The People of the Scripture used to recite the Torah in Hebrew and explain it in Arabic to the Muslims.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Do not affirm what the People of the Scripture tell you, and do not declare it false. Rather, say:
‘We believe in Allah and in what was revealed to us.’”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4485).
This hadith establishes the principle that one must refrain from issuing a judgment concerning matters and reports whose truth is uncertain.
Such matters should not be conclusively judged valid or false, lawful or unlawful, without evidence.
We have been commanded to believe in the scriptures revealed to the prophets.
However, the Jewish and Christian custodians of those books altered and changed them. We therefore have no certain way of knowing which of their reports are authentic or whether what they relate from those books is accurate.
We were therefore commanded to withhold judgment.
We do not affirm their reports, lest we agree with them concerning what they altered and changed.
Nor do we reject them outright, because the report may be true, in which case we would be denying something we were commanded to believe.
We therefore say:
“We believe in whatever scripture Allah revealed.”
Al-Khaṭṭābī explained this in Aʿlām al-Ḥadīth (3/1801).

هذا الحديث أصل في وجوب التوقف عما يشكل من الأمور والعلوم؛ فلا يقضى عليه بجواز أو بطلان، ولا بتحليل ولا تحريم.
وقد أمرنا أن نؤمن بالكتب المنزلة على الأنبياء، إلا أن قراء الكتب من اليهود والنصارى قد حرفوا وبدلوا، ولا سبيل لنا إلى العلم بما هو صحيح منها، وأن ما يحكونه عن تلك الكتب هل هو مستقيم.
فأمرنا بالتوقف فيه؛ فلا نصدقهم لئلا نكون شركاء معهم فيما حرفوه وبدلوه، ولا نكذب به؛ فلعله يكون صحيحًا، فنكون منكرين لما أمرنا أن نؤمن به.
ونقول: آمنا بما أنزل اللّٰه من كتاب. أفاده الخطابي في أعلام الحديث (٣/١٨٠١).
11924 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
The People of the Scripture used to recite the Torah in Hebrew and explain it in Arabic to the Muslims.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Do not affirm what the People of the Scripture tell you, and do not declare it false. Rather, say:
‘We believe in Allah and in what was revealed to us.’”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4485).
This hadith establishes the principle that one must refrain from issuing a judgment concerning matters and reports whose truth is uncertain.
Such matters should not be conclusively judged valid or false, lawful or unlawful, without evidence.
We have been commanded to believe in the scriptures revealed to the prophets.
However, the Jewish and Christian custodians of those books altered and changed them. We therefore have no certain way of knowing which of their reports are authentic or whether what they relate from those books is accurate.
We were therefore commanded to withhold judgment.
We do not affirm their reports, lest we agree with them concerning what they altered and changed.
Nor do we reject them outright, because the report may be true, in which case we would be denying something we were commanded to believe.
We therefore say:
“We believe in whatever scripture Allah revealed.”
Al-Khaṭṭābī explained this in Aʿlām al-Ḥadīth (3/1801).

١١٩٢٥ — عن البراء أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ صلى إلى بيت المقدس ستة عشر شهرًا، أو سبعة عشر شهرًا، وكان يعجبه أن تكون قبلته قبل البيت.
وأنه صلى، أو صلاها، صلاة العصر، وصلى معه قوم.
فخرج رجل ممن كان صلى معه، فمر على أهل مسجد وهم راكعون، فقال: أشهد باللّٰه، لقد صليت مع النبي ﷺ قبل مكة.
فداروا كما هم قبل البيت.
وكان الذين ماتوا على القبلة قبل أن تحول قبل البيت رجالًا قتلوا، فلم ندر ما نقول فيهم.
فأنزل اللّٰه:
﴿وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَانَكُمْ، إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِالنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٤٨٦)، ومسلم (٥٢٥)، واللفظ للبخاري.
وقوله: ﴿إِيمَانَكُمْ﴾، أي: صلاتكم.

11925 — Al-Barāʾ narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed facing Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months.
He desired that his qiblah be directed toward the Sacred House.
He performed the afternoon prayer—or one of the prayers—with a group of people.
A man who had prayed with him then left and passed by the people of another mosque while they were bowing in prayer.
He said:
“I testify by Allah that I have just prayed with the Prophet ﷺ facing Makkah.”
They immediately turned while remaining in prayer and faced the Sacred House.
Some men had died or been killed while praying toward the former qiblah before it was changed toward the Sacred House, and we did not know what to say concerning them.
Allah then revealed:
“Allah would never allow your faith to be lost. Allah is indeed Most Kind and Most Merciful to mankind.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4486) and Muslim (525). The wording cited here is that of al-Bukhārī.
The word:
“Your faith”
means your prayers.

١١٩٢٦ — عن ابن عباس قال: لما وجه النبي ﷺ إلى الكعبة قالوا: يا رسول اللّٰه، كيف بإخواننا الذين ماتوا وهم يصلون إلى بيت المقدس؟
فأنزل اللّٰه تعالى:
﴿وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَانَكُمْ﴾.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٤٦٨٠)، والترمذي (٢٩٦٤)، وأحمد (٢٦٩١)، وصححه ابن حبان (١٧١٧)، والحاكم (٢/٢٦٩).

11926 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
When the Prophet ﷺ was directed to face the Kaʿbah, the Companions asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, what will happen to our brothers who died while praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis?”
Allah, the Exalted, then revealed:
“Allah would never allow your faith to be lost.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4680), al-Tirmidhī (2964), Aḥmad (2691), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (1717) and al-Ḥākim (2/269).

١١٩٢٨ — عن أنس أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ كان يصلي نحو بيت المقدس، فنزلت:
﴿قَدْ نَرَىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِي السَّمَاءِ، فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ قِبْلَةً تَرْضَاهَا، فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ، وَحَيْثُ مَا كُنْتُمْ فَوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُ، وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ لَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ، وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾.
فمر رجل من بني سلمة، وهم ركوع في صلاة الفجر، وقد صلوا ركعة، فنادى: ألا إن القبلة قد حولت. فمالوا كما هم نحو القبلة.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٥٢٧).
وقوله تعالى:
﴿وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلْنَاكُمْ أُمَّةً وَسَطًا لِتَكُونُوا شُهَدَاءَ عَلَى النَّاسِ، وَيَكُونَ الرَّسُولُ عَلَيْكُمْ شَهِيدًا﴾.

english_source:
11928 — Anas narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray facing Bayt al-Maqdis. Then the following verse was revealed:
“We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the sky. We will therefore surely turn you toward a direction of prayer that pleases you. So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque, and wherever you may be, turn your faces toward it. Those who were given the Scripture certainly know that this is the truth from their Lord, and Allah is not unaware of what they do.”
A man from Banū Salamah passed by some people while they were bowing in the dawn prayer, after they had completed one rakʿah.
He called out:
“The direction of prayer has now been changed.”
They immediately turned, while remaining in prayer, toward the new qiblah.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (527).
The words of Allah, the Exalted:
“Thus We have made you a balanced and just nation, so that you may be witnesses over mankind and the Messenger may be a witness over you.”

١١٩٢٩ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((يدعى نوح يوم القيامة، فيقول: لبيك وسعديك يا رب.
فيقول: هل بلغت؟
فيقول: نعم.

﴿وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلْنَاكُمْ أُمَّةً وَسَطًا لِتَكُونُوا شُهَدَاءَ عَلَى النَّاسِ، وَيَكُونَ الرَّسُولُ عَلَيْكُمْ شَهِيدًا﴾.
والوسط: العدل)).

11929 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Noah will be summoned on the Day of Resurrection, and he will say, ‘Here I am at Your service, my Lord.’
Allah will ask, ‘Did you convey the message?’
He will reply, ‘Yes.’
His nation will then be asked, ‘Did he convey the message to you?’
They will reply, ‘No warner came to us.’
Allah will ask Noah, ‘Who will testify for you?’
He will reply, ‘Muḥammad and his nation.’
They will testify that he conveyed the message, and the Messenger will be a witness over you. This is the meaning of the words of Allah, Glorious is His mention:
‘Thus We have made you a balanced and just nation, so that you may be witnesses over mankind and the Messenger may be a witness over you.’
The word ‘balanced’ means just.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4487).

١١٩٣٠ — عن أبي هريرة قال: كان أهل الكتاب يقرؤون التوراة بالعبرانية، ويفسرونها بالعربية لأهل الإسلام.
فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((لا تصدقوا أهل الكتاب ولا تكذبوهم، وقولوا: ﴿آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْنَا﴾)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٤٤٨٥).

11930 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
The People of the Scripture used to recite the Torah in Hebrew and explain it in Arabic to the Muslims.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Do not affirm what the People of the Scripture tell you, and do not declare it false. Rather, say:
‘We believe in Allah and in what was revealed to us.’”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4485).

١١٩٣١ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال: ((يقول اللّٰه تعالى: أنا عند ظن عبدي بي، وأنا معه إذا ذكرني.
فإن ذكرني في نفسه ذكرته في نفسي، وإن ذكرني في ملأ ذكرته في ملأ خير منه.
وإن تقرب إلي شبرًا تقربت إليه ذراعًا، وإن تقرب إلي ذراعًا تقربت إليه باعًا، وإن أتاني يمشي أتيته هرولة)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧٤٠٥)، ومسلم (٢٦٧٥).

١١٩٣٢ — عن أم سلمة زوج النبي ﷺ قالت: إنها سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول: ((ما من مسلم تصيبه مصيبة، فيقول ما أمره اللّٰه: إنا للّٰه وإنا إليه راجعون، اللهم أجرني في مصيبتي، واخلف لي خيرًا منها، إلا أخلف اللّٰه له خيرًا منها)).
قالت: فلما مات أبو سلمة قلت: أي المسلمين خير من أبي سلمة؟ أول بيت هاجر إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ. ثم إني قلتها، فأخلف اللّٰه لي رسول اللّٰه ﷺ.
قالت: أرسل إلي رسول اللّٰه ﷺ حاطب بن أبي بلتعة يخطبني له. فقلت: إن لي بنتًا، وأنا غيور.
فقال: ((أما ابنتها فندعو اللّٰه أن يغنيها عنها، وأدعو اللّٰه أن يذهب بالغيرة)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٩١٨).
ورواه مسلم من وجه آخر، وفيه: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول:
((ما من عبد تصيبه مصيبة، فيقول: إنا للّٰه وإنا إليه راجعون، اللهم أجرني في مصيبتي، وأخلف لي خيرًا منها، إلا أجره اللّٰه في مصيبته، وأخلف له خيرًا منها)).
قالت أم سلمة: فلما توفي أبو سلمة قلت كما أمرني رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فأخلف اللّٰه لي خيرًا منه: رسول اللّٰه ﷺ.

11932 — Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, narrated that she heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“No Muslim is afflicted by a calamity and then says what Allah commanded:
‘Indeed, we belong to Allah and to Him we will return. O Allah, reward me for my calamity and replace it for me with something better,’
except that Allah replaces it for him with something better.”
She said:
When Abū Salamah died, I said to myself:
“Which Muslim could be better than Abū Salamah, from the first household to migrate to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?”
Nevertheless, I recited the supplication, and Allah replaced him for me with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
She continued:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿah to propose marriage to me on his behalf.
I said:
“I have a daughter, and I am a woman who experiences jealousy.”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“As for her daughter, we will supplicate to Allah to make her independent of her, and I will supplicate to Allah to remove her jealousy.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (918).
Muslim narrated it through another route with the wording:
Umm Salamah said:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“No servant is afflicted by a calamity and says:
‘Indeed, we belong to Allah and to Him we will return. O Allah, reward me for my calamity and replace it for me with something better,’
except that Allah rewards him for his calamity and replaces it for him with something better.”
Umm Salamah said:
When Abū Salamah died, I said what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had commanded me to say. Allah then replaced him for me with someone better than him: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

١١٩٣٣ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((من يرد اللّٰه به خيرًا يصب منه)).
صحيح: رواه مالك في الموطأ (١٧٥٢)، والبخاري (٥٦٤٥).
وقوله: «يصب منه»، قال أبو عبيد الهروي: معناه يبتليه بالمصائب ليثيبه عليها.

11933 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“When Allah intends good for someone, He afflicts him with trials.”
Authentic: Narrated by Mālik in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ (1752) and al-Bukhārī (5645).
Concerning the words “He afflicts him,” Abū ʿUbayd al-Harawī said:
“It means that Allah tests him with calamities in order to reward him for enduring them.”

11934 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī and Abū Hurayrah narrated that they heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“No fatigue, illness, anxiety, sorrow, harm, or distress afflicts a Muslim—even the prick of a thorn—except that Allah expiates some of his sins through it.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5641–5642) and Muslim (2573). The wording cited here is that of al-Bukhārī.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٦٤١-٥٦٤٢)، ومسلم (٢٥٧٣)، واللفظ للبخاري.
11934 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī and Abū Hurayrah narrated that they heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“No fatigue, illness, anxiety, sorrow, harm, or distress afflicts a Muslim—even the prick of a thorn—except that Allah expiates some of his sins through it.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5641–5642) and Muslim (2573). The wording cited here is that of al-Bukhārī.

١١٩٣٥ — عن عروة بن الزبير أنه سأل عائشة فقال: أرأيت قول اللّٰه تعالى:
﴿إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ مِنْ شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ، فَمَنْ حَجَّ الْبَيْتَ أَوِ اعْتَمَرَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَا﴾،
فواللّٰه ما على أحد جناح أن لا يطوف بالصفا والمروة.
قالت: بئس ما قلت يا ابن أختي! إن هذه لو كانت كما أولتها عليه، كانت: لا جناح عليه أن لا يتطوف بهما.
ولكنها أنزلت في الأنصار، كانوا قبل أن يسلموا يهلون لمناة الطاغية التي كانوا يعبدونها عند المشلل، فكان من أهل لها يتحرج أن يطوف بالصفا والمروة.
فلما أسلموا سألوا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ عن ذلك، فقالوا: يا رسول اللّٰه، إنا كنا نتحرج أن نطوف بين الصفا والمروة.
فأنزل اللّٰه تعالى:
﴿إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ مِنْ شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ﴾ الآية.
قالت عائشة رضي اللّٰه عنها: وقد سن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ الطواف بينهما، فليس لأحد أن يترك الطواف بينهما.
ثم أخبرت أبا بكر بن عبد الرحمن، فقال: إن هذا لعلم ما كنت سمعته.
ولقد سمعت رجالًا من أهل العلم يذكرون أن الناس، إلا من ذكرت عائشة ممن كان يهل بمناة، كانوا يطوفون كلهم بالصفا والمروة.
فلما ذكر اللّٰه تعالى الطواف بالبيت، ولم يذكر الصفا والمروة في القرآن، قالوا: يا رسول اللّٰه، كنا نطوف بالصفا والمروة، وإن اللّٰه أنزل الطواف بالبيت، فلم يذكر الصفا، فهل علينا من حرج أن نطوف بالصفا والمروة؟
فأنزل اللّٰه تعالى:
﴿إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ مِنْ شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ﴾ الآية.
قال أبو بكر: فأسمع هذه الآية نزلت في الفريقين كليهما: في الذين كانوا يتحرجون أن يطوفوا في الجاهلية بالصفا والمروة، والذين كانوا يطوفون ثم تحرجوا أن يطوفوا بهما في الإسلام من أجل أن اللّٰه تعالى أمر بالطواف بالبيت، ولم يذكر الصفا والمروة، حتى ذكر ذلك بعد ما ذكر الطواف بالبيت.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٦٤٣)، ومسلم (١٢٧٧/٢٦١).

11935 — ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr narrated that he asked ʿĀʾishah:
“What do you think about the words of Allah, the Exalted:
‘Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. Whoever performs Ḥajj or ʿUmrah at the House incurs no sin by going between them’?
By Allah, it would appear that there is no sin upon anyone who does not go between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah.”
She replied:
“What a terrible interpretation you have made, son of my sister! Had the verse meant what you understood, it would have said: ‘There is no sin upon him if he does not go between them.’
Rather, it was revealed concerning the Anṣār. Before accepting Islam, they used to enter the state of pilgrimage devotion in the name of the idol Manāt, which they worshipped near al-Mushallal. Those who had entered pilgrimage devotion for Manāt considered it sinful to go between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah.
After embracing Islam, they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about this, saying, ‘O Messenger of Allah, we used to consider it sinful to go between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah.’
Allah, the Exalted, then revealed:
‘Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah…’”
ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said:
“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ established going between them as a religious practice, so no one is permitted to abandon going between them.”
ʿUrwah continued:
I informed Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān of this, and he said:
“This is knowledge I had not previously heard.
I have heard learned men mention that all people used to go between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, except those whom ʿĀʾishah mentioned who had entered pilgrimage devotion for Manāt.
When Allah mentioned circumambulation of the House in the Qur’an but did not mention al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, they asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, we used to go between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. Allah has revealed the command to circumambulate the House but has not mentioned al-Ṣafā. Is there any sin upon us if we go between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah?’
Allah, the Exalted, then revealed:
‘Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah…’”
Abū Bakr said:
“It appears that this verse was revealed concerning both groups:
Those who, during the pre-Islamic period, considered it sinful to go between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah;
and those who had previously gone between them but later hesitated to do so after accepting Islam, because Allah had commanded circumambulation of the House without initially mentioning al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, until He mentioned them afterward.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1643) and Muslim (1277/261).

قال أبو بكر: فأسمع هذه الآية نزلت في الفريقين كليهما: في الذين كانوا يتحرجون أن يطوفوا في الجاهلية بالصفا والمروة، والذين كانوا يطوفون ثم تحرجوا أن يطوفوا بهما في الإسلام من أجل أن اللّٰه تعالى أمر بالطواف بالبيت، ولم يذكر الصفا والمروة، حتى ذكر ذلك بعد ما ذكر الطواف بالبيت.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٦٤٣)، ومسلم (١٢٧٧/٢٦١).
11935 — ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr narrated that he asked ʿĀʾishah:
“What do you think about the words of Allah, the Exalted:
‘Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. Whoever performs Ḥajj or ʿUmrah at the House incurs no sin by going between them’?
By Allah, it would appear that there is no sin upon anyone who does not go between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah.”
She replied:
“What a terrible interpretation you have made, son of my sister! Had the verse meant what you understood, it would have said: ‘There is no sin upon him if he does not go between them.’
Rather, it was revealed concerning the Anṣār. Before accepting Islam, they used to enter the state of pilgrimage devotion in the name of the idol Manāt, which they worshipped near al-Mushallal. Those who had entered pilgrimage devotion for Manāt considered it sinful to go between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah.
After embracing Islam, they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about this, saying, ‘O Messenger of Allah, we used to consider it sinful to go between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah.’
Allah, the Exalted, then revealed:
‘Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah…’”
ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said:
“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ established going between them as a religious practice, so no one is permitted to abandon going between them.”
ʿUrwah continued:
I informed Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān of this, and he said:
“This is knowledge I had not previously heard.
I have heard learned men mention that all people used to go between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, except those whom ʿĀʾishah mentioned who had entered pilgrimage devotion for Manāt.
When Allah mentioned circumambulation of the House in the Qur’an but did not mention al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, they asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, we used to go between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. Allah has revealed the command to circumambulate the House but has not mentioned al-Ṣafā. Is there any sin upon us if we go between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah?’
Allah, the Exalted, then revealed:
‘Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah…’”
Abū Bakr said:
“It appears that this verse was revealed concerning both groups:
Those who, during the pre-Islamic period, considered it sinful to go between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah;
and those who had previously gone between them but later hesitated to do so after accepting Islam, because Allah had commanded circumambulation of the House without initially mentioning al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, until He mentioned them afterward.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1643) and Muslim (1277/261).

١١٩٣٧ — عن جابر قال في حجة النبي ﷺ في حديث طويل: ثم خرج من الباب إلى الصفا، فلما دنا من الصفا قرأ:
﴿إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ مِنْ شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ﴾.
وقال: ((أبدأ بما بدأ اللّٰه به)).
فبدأ بالصفا، فرقي عليه حتى رأى البيت، فاستقبل القبلة، فوحد اللّٰه وكبره، وقال:
((لا إله إلا اللّٰه وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد، وهو على كل شيء قدير. لا إله إلا اللّٰه وحده، أنجز وعده، ونصر عبده، وهزم الأحزاب وحده)).
ثم دعا بين ذلك، قال مثل هذا ثلاث مرات.
ثم نزل إلى المروة، حتى إذا انصبت قدماه في بطن الوادي سعى، حتى إذا صعدتا مشى، حتى أتى المروة، ففعل على المروة كما فعل على الصفا… الحديث.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٢١٨).

11937 — Jābir narrated in the lengthy hadith describing the pilgrimage of the Prophet ﷺ:
The Prophet ﷺ then went out through the gate toward al-Ṣafā.
When he approached al-Ṣafā, he recited:
“Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah.”
He then said:
“I begin with that which Allah mentioned first.”
He began with al-Ṣafā and climbed it until he could see the Sacred House.
He faced the qiblah, declared Allah’s oneness and greatness, and said:
“There is no deity except Allah alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise, and He has power over all things.
There is no deity except Allah alone. He fulfilled His promise, granted victory to His servant, and defeated the confederate armies by Himself.”
He then supplicated between these declarations and repeated this three times.
He afterward descended toward al-Marwah. When his feet reached the bottom of the valley, he ran. When he began ascending, he walked until he reached al-Marwah.
There he performed the same acts that he had performed upon al-Ṣafā.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1218).

arabic_source:
١١٩٣٨ — عن ابن مسعود قال: قال النبي ﷺ كلمة، وقلت أخرى.
قال النبي ﷺ: ((من مات وهو يدعو من دون اللّٰه ندًا دخل النار)).
وقلت أنا: من مات وهو لا يدعو للّٰه ندًا دخل الجنة.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٤٩٧)، ومسلم (٩٢/١٥٠).
وهذا الذي قاله عبد اللّٰه بن مسعود، فإنه من المعروف أنه كان يحتاط في رفع الحديث إلى النبي ﷺ.
ولذلك قيل: إنه سمع الحديثين جميعًا من النبي ﷺ، فرفع منهما ما كان حافظًا له، ووقف الذي شك فيه؛ لأن اللفظين ثابتان عن النبي ﷺ في حديث جابر الآتي.

11938 — Ibn Masʿūd narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ made one statement, and I made another.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Whoever dies while calling upon a rival besides Allah will enter the Fire.”
I said:
“Whoever dies without calling upon any rival besides Allah will enter Paradise.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4497) and Muslim (92/150).
This second statement was made by ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd.
It is well known that he exercised great caution before attributing statements directly to the Prophet ﷺ.
It has therefore been said that he heard both statements from the Prophet ﷺ. He explicitly attributed the one he remembered with certainty to him, while leaving the other as his own statement because he was uncertain about its precise attribution.
Both statements are, however, authentically established from the Prophet ﷺ in the following hadith of Jābir.

11938 — Ibn Masʿūd narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ made one statement, and I made another.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Whoever dies while calling upon a rival besides Allah will enter the Fire.”
I said:
“Whoever dies without calling upon any rival besides Allah will enter Paradise.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4497) and Muslim (92/150).
This second statement was made by ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd.
It is well known that he exercised great caution before attributing statements directly to the Prophet ﷺ.
It has therefore been said that he heard both statements from the Prophet ﷺ. He explicitly attributed the one he remembered with certainty to him, while leaving the other as his own statement because he was uncertain about its precise attribution.
Both statements are, however, authentically established from the Prophet ﷺ in the following hadith of Jābir.

١١٩٤٠ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((أيها الناس، إن اللّٰه طيب لا يقبل إلا طيبًا، وإن اللّٰه أمر المؤمنين بما أمر به المرسلين، فقال:
﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الرُّسُلُ كُلُوا مِنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ وَاعْمَلُوا صَالِحًا، إِنِّي بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ عَلِيمٌ﴾ [المؤمنون: ٥١].
وقال:
﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ﴾.
ثم ذكر الرجل يطيل السفر، أشعث أغبر، يمد يديه إلى السماء: يا رب، يا رب، ومطعمه حرام، ومشربه حرام، وملبسه حرام، وغذي بالحرام، فأنى يستجاب لذلك؟)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٠١٥).

11940 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“O people, Allah is pure and accepts only what is pure. Allah has commanded the believers with the same command He gave to the messengers.
He said:
‘O messengers, eat from the good and lawful things and perform righteous deeds. I am fully aware of what you do.’
 [Sūrat al-Muʾminūn 23:51]
And He said:
‘O you who believe, eat from the good things We have provided for you.’
He then mentioned a man who travels for a long time, disheveled and covered in dust, raising his hands toward heaven and saying, ‘My Lord! My Lord!’
Yet his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and he has been nourished with what is unlawful. How, then, could his supplication be answered?”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1015).

١١٩٤١ — عن ابن عمر قال: أُحِلَّت لنا ميتتان ودمان: الجراد والحيتان، والكبد والطحال.
صحيح: رواه البيهقي (١/٢٥٤).
قال ابن القيم في زاد المعاد (٣/٣٩٢): «هذا حديث حسن، وهذا الموقوف في حكم المرفوع؛ لأن قول الصحابي: أُحِلَّ لنا كذا، وحُرِّم علينا، ينصرف إلى إحلال النبي ﷺ وتحريمه». انتهى.

english_source:
11941 — Ibn ʿUmar said:
“Two kinds of carrion and two kinds of blood have been made lawful for us: locusts and fish, and the liver and spleen.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bayhaqī (1/254).
Ibn al-Qayyim said in Zād al-Maʿād (3/392):
“This is a ḥasan hadith. Although it is formally a statement of a Companion, it carries the ruling of a prophetic report, because when a Companion says, ‘Such-and-such was made lawful for us,’ or, ‘Such-and-such was forbidden to us,’ this refers to the declaration of lawfulness or prohibition by the Prophet ﷺ.”
End quote.

11942 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, which charity brings the greatest reward?”
He replied:
“That you give charity while you are healthy and reluctant to part with your wealth, fearing poverty and hoping for wealth. Do not delay until your soul reaches your throat and then say, ‘So-and-so should receive this much, and so-and-so should receive this much,’ when it has already become the property of so-and-so.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1419) and Muslim (1032). The wording cited here is that of al-Bukhārī.
The Words of Allah: “And Those Who Ask”
This contains encouragement not to send a person who asks away empty-handed, as stated in the following hadith.

١١٩٤٣ — عن عبد الرحمن بن بجيد، عن جدته أم بجيد، وكانت ممن بايع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، أنها قالت: يا رسول اللّٰه، إن المسكين ليقوم على بابي، فما أجد شيئًا أعطيه إياه.
فقال لها رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((إن لم تجدي شيئًا تعطينه إياه إلا ظلفًا محرقًا، فادفعيه إليه في يده)).
حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٦٦٦)، والترمذي (٦٦٥)، والنسائي (٢٥٧٤)، وابن خزيمة (٢٤٧٣).

11943 — ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Bujayd narrated from his grandmother, Umm Bujayd, who was among the women who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
She said:
“O Messenger of Allah, a poor person may stand at my door, but I find nothing to give him.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:
“Even if you find nothing to give him except a burned hoof, place it in his hand.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1666), al-Tirmidhī (665), al-Nasāʾī (2574), and Ibn Khuzaymah (2473).
The Words of Allah: “And Those Who Remain Patient during Hardship, Affliction, and at the Time of Battle”

١١٩٤٥ — عن أنس أن الربيع، وهي ابنة النضر، كسرت ثنية جارية، فطلبوا الأرش وطلبوا العفو، فأبوا. فأتوا النبي ﷺ، فأمرهم بالقصاص.
فقال أنس بن النضر: أتكسر ثنية الربيع يا رسول اللّٰه؟ لا، والذي بعثك بالحق، لا تكسر ثنيتها.
فقال: ((يا أنس، كتاب اللّٰه القصاص)).
فرضي القوم وعفوا، فقال النبي ﷺ: ((إن من عباد اللّٰه من لو أقسم على اللّٰه لأبره)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٧٠٣).

english_source:
11945 — Anas narrated:
Al-Rubayyiʿ, the daughter of al-Naḍr, broke the front tooth of a young woman.
Her family offered financial compensation and asked the injured party to pardon her, but they refused. They came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he ordered legal retaliation.
Anas ibn al-Naḍr said:
“O Messenger of Allah, will al-Rubayyiʿ’s tooth be broken? No, by the One who sent you with the truth, her tooth will not be broken.”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“Anas, the ruling of Allah is legal retaliation.”
The injured family then became satisfied and granted pardon.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Among the servants of Allah are those who, if they swear by Allah that something will occur, Allah fulfills their oath.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2703).

١١٩٤٦ — عن أبي هريرة أنه عام فتح مكة قتلت خزاعة رجلًا من بني ليث بقتيل لهم في الجاهلية، فقام رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال:
((إن اللّٰه حبس عن مكة الفيل، وسلط عليها رسوله والمؤمنين. ألا وإنها لم تحل لأحد قبلي، ولا تحل لأحد بعدي. ألا وإنها أحلت لي ساعة من نهار، ألا وإنها ساعتي هذه حرام.
لا يختلى شوكها، ولا يعضد شجرها، ولا يلتقط ساقطتها إلا منشد. ومن قتل له قتيل فهو بخير النظرين: إما يودى، وإما يقاد))… الحديث.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٨٨٠)، ومسلم (١٣٥٥)، واللفظ للبخاري.

11946 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
During the year of the conquest of Makkah, the tribe of Khuzāʿah killed a man from Banū Layth in retaliation for one of their men who had been killed during the pre-Islamic period.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood and said:
“Allah restrained the elephant from Makkah and gave authority over it to His Messenger and the believers. It was not made lawful for anyone before me, and it will not be made lawful for anyone after me. It was made lawful for me only for one hour of one day, and at this very hour it has returned to being sacred.
Its thorny plants may not be cut, its trees may not be felled, and its lost property may not be picked up except by one who will publicly announce it. Whoever has a relative murdered has the choice between two options: either blood money is paid to him or the killer is subjected to legal retaliation.”
The remainder of the hadith follows.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6880) and Muslim (1355). The wording cited here is that of al-Bukhārī.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٨٨٠)، ومسلم (١٣٥٥)، واللفظ للبخاري.
11946 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
During the year of the conquest of Makkah, the tribe of Khuzāʿah killed a man from Banū Layth in retaliation for one of their men who had been killed during the pre-Islamic period.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood and said:
“Allah restrained the elephant from Makkah and gave authority over it to His Messenger and the believers. It was not made lawful for anyone before me, and it will not be made lawful for anyone after me. It was made lawful for me only for one hour of one day, and at this very hour it has returned to being sacred.
Its thorny plants may not be cut, its trees may not be felled, and its lost property may not be picked up except by one who will publicly announce it. Whoever has a relative murdered has the choice between two options: either blood money is paid to him or the killer is subjected to legal retaliation.”
The remainder of the hadith follows.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6880) and Muslim (1355). The wording cited here is that of al-Bukhārī.

١١٩٤٧ — عن ابن عباس قال: كان في بني إسرائيل القصاص، ولم تكن فيهم الدية، فقال اللّٰه تعالى لهذه الأمة:
﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِصَاصُ فِي الْقَتْلَى﴾.
فالعفو أن يقبل الدية في العمد.
﴿فَاتِّبَاعٌ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَأَدَاءٌ إِلَيْهِ بِإِحْسَانٍ﴾، يتبع بالمعروف ويؤدى إليه بإحسان.
﴿ذَٰلِكَ تَخْفِيفٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَرَحْمَةٌ﴾، مما كتب على من كان قبلكم.
﴿فَمَنِ اعْتَدَىٰ بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ فَلَهُ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾، أي: قتل بعد قبول الدية.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٤٤٩٨).

11947 — Ibn ʿAbbās said:
Among the Children of Israel, there was legal retaliation, but there was no provision for blood money.
Allah, the Exalted, therefore said to this nation:
“O you who believe, legal retaliation has been prescribed for you concerning those murdered.”
The meaning of pardon is that blood money is accepted in a case of intentional killing.
The words:
“Then there should be a fair demand and payment made with kindness”
mean that the victim’s family should seek payment reasonably and the offender should pay it graciously.
The words:
“That is a concession and mercy from your Lord”
refer to a concession from what had been prescribed for those before you.
The words:
“Whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment”
refer to one who kills the offender after having already accepted the blood money.
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4498).

١١٩٤٨ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمر أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال: ((ما حق امرئ مسلم له شيء يوصي فيه، يبيت ليلتين إلا ووصيته عنده مكتوبة)).
متفق عليه: رواه مالك في الوصية (١)، والبخاري (٢٧٣٨)، ومسلم (١٦٢٧).

11948 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“It is not proper for a Muslim who has something concerning which he should make a bequest to spend two nights without having his will written and kept with him.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Mālik in al-Waṣiyyah (1), al-Bukhārī (2738), and Muslim (1627).

١١٩٤٩ — عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال: جاء النبي ﷺ يعودني وأنا بمكة، وهو يكره أن يموت بالأرض التي هاجر منها.
قال: ((يرحم اللّٰه ابن عفراء)).
قلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، أوصي بمالي كله؟
قال: ((لا)).
قلت: فالشطر؟
قال: ((لا)).
قلت: فالثلث؟
قال: ((الثلث، والثلث كثير. إنك أن تدع ورثتك أغنياء خير من أن تدعهم عالة يتكففون الناس في أيديهم.
وإنك مهما أنفقت من نفقة فإنها صدقة، حتى اللقمة التي ترفعها إلى في امرأتك. وعسى اللّٰه أن يرفعك، فينتفع بك ناس ويضر بك آخرون)).
ولم يكن له يومئذ إلا ابنة.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٧٤٢)، ومسلم (١٦٢٨)، واللفظ للبخاري.

english_source:
11949 — Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ came to visit me while I was ill in Makkah. Saʿd disliked the possibility of dying in the land from which he had migrated.
He said:
“May Allah have mercy upon Ibn ʿAfrāʾ.”
I asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, may I bequeath all my wealth?”
He replied:
“No.”
I asked:
“Then half of it?”
He replied:
“No.”
I asked:
“Then one-third?”
He replied:
“One-third, and one-third is a great deal. It is better for you to leave your heirs wealthy than to leave them poor and begging from people.
Whatever you spend is charity for you, even the morsel of food you place in your wife’s mouth. Perhaps Allah will preserve you so that some people benefit through you while others are harmed through you.”
At that time, Saʿd had only one daughter.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2742) and Muslim (1628). The wording cited here is that of al-Bukhārī.

١١٩٥٠ — عن عائشة قالت: كان رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أمر بصيام يوم عاشوراء، فلما فرض رمضان كان من شاء صام، ومن شاء أفطر.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٠٠١)، ومسلم (١١٢٥/١١٥).

11950 — ʿĀʾishah narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had commanded the people to fast on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ.
When fasting Ramadan was made obligatory, whoever wished continued fasting ʿĀshūrāʾ, and whoever wished left it.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2001) and Muslim (1125/115).

﴿وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُ فِدْيَةٌ طَعَامُ مِسْكِينٍ﴾،
كان من أراد أن يفطر ويفتدي، حتى نزلت الآية التي بعدها فنسختها.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٥٠٧)، ومسلم (١١٤٥/١٤٩).
ومعنى الحديث أنه لما نزل قوله تعالى:
﴿وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُ فِدْيَةٌ طَعَامُ مِسْكِينٍ﴾،
كان من شاء صام، ومن شاء أطعم مسكينًا.
ثم إن اللّٰه عز وجل أنزل الآية الأخرى، وهي قوله:
﴿شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ فِيهِ الْقُرْآنُ﴾، إلى قوله: ﴿فَمَنْ شَهِدَ مِنْكُمُ الشَّهْرَ فَلْيَصُمْهُ﴾.

11951 — Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ narrated:
When the verse:
“Those who are able to fast only with great difficulty may give a ransom by feeding a poor person”
was revealed, whoever wished could refrain from fasting and instead offer the ransom.
This remained the case until the following verse was revealed and abrogated that option.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4507) and Muslim (1145/149).
The meaning of the hadith is that when Allah revealed:
“Those who are able to fast only with great difficulty may give a ransom by feeding a poor person,”
whoever wished could fast, and whoever wished could instead feed a poor person.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then revealed the following verse:
“The month of Ramadan is that in which the Qur’an was revealed,”
continuing until His words:
“Whoever among you witnesses the month must fast it.”
Allah thereby made fasting obligatory upon the healthy resident, permitted the ill person and traveler to make up the fast later, and retained the provision of feeding a poor person for the elderly person who is unable to fast.

١١٩٥٢ — عن عطاء أنه سمع ابن عباس يقرأ:
﴿وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُ فِدْيَةٌ طَعَامُ مِسْكِينٍ﴾.
قال ابن عباس: ليست منسوخة، هو الشيخ الكبير والمرأة الكبيرة لا يستطيعان أن يصوما، فيطعمان مكان كل يوم مسكينًا.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٤٥٠٥).
فالنسخ الثابت هو في حق الصحيح المقيم، بإيجاب الصوم عليه بقوله تعالى:
﴿فَمَنْ شَهِدَ مِنْكُمُ الشَّهْرَ فَلْيَصُمْهُ﴾.
وأما الشيخ الفاني الذي لا يستطيع الصيام، فله أن يفطر، ولا قضاء عليه.
وقوله: «فيطعمان مكان كل يوم مسكينًا»، هذا رأي ابن عباس، وبه قال أكثر العلماء. وكان أنس بعدما كبر يطعم كل يوم مسكينًا خبزًا ولحمًا، ويفطر.
والقول الآخر، وهو أحد قولي الشافعي: لا يجب عليه إطعام، كما لا يجب على الصبي الذي لم يبلغ؛ لأن اللّٰه لا يكلف نفسًا إلا وسعها.
انظر مزيدًا من التفصيل في كتاب الصيام.

11952 — ʿAṭāʾ narrated that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās recite:
“Those who are able to fast only with great difficulty may give a ransom by feeding a poor person.”
Ibn ʿAbbās said:
“This verse has not been abrogated. It applies to an elderly man and an elderly woman who are unable to fast. They must feed one poor person for each day.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4505).
The established abrogation applies to a healthy resident, upon whom fasting became obligatory through the words of Allah:
“Whoever among you witnesses the month must fast it.”
As for a very elderly person who is unable to fast, he may refrain from fasting and is not required to make up the days.
The statement:
“They must feed one poor person for each day”
is the opinion of Ibn ʿAbbās and the majority of scholars.
When Anas became elderly, he would refrain from fasting and feed a poor person bread and meat for each day.
Another opinion, which is one of the two views attributed to al-Shāfiʿī, holds that feeding is not obligatory upon such a person, just as no obligation applies to a child who has not reached puberty, because Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity.
Refer to the Book of Fasting for further details.

١١٩٥٣ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري وجابر بن عبد اللّٰه قالا: سافرنا مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فيصوم الصائم ويفطر المفطر، فلا يعيب بعضهم على بعض.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١١١٧).
قوله تعالى: ﴿وَلِتُكْمِلُوا الْعِدَّةَ﴾

11953 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī and Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh said:
We traveled with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Some of us fasted and others did not fast, and neither group criticized the other.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1117).
The Words of Allah: “So That You May Complete the Prescribed Number”

١١٩٥٦ — عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال: كنا مع النبي ﷺ في سفر، فجعل الناس يجهرون بالتكبير.
فقال النبي ﷺ: ((أيها الناس، اربعوا على أنفسكم؛ إنكم لا تدعون أصم ولا غائبًا، إنكم تدعون سميعًا قريبًا، وهو معكم))… الحديث.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٧٠٤).

11956 — Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī narrated:
We were traveling with the Prophet ﷺ, and the people began raising their voices while declaring Allah’s greatness.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“O people, be gentle with yourselves. You are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent. You are calling upon One who is All-Hearing and Near, and He is with you.”
The remainder of the hadith follows.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2704).

﴿عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَخْتَانُونَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَعَفَا عَنْكُمْ﴾.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٤٥٠٨).

When fasting Ramadan was first prescribed, the Muslims would not approach their wives throughout the entire month of Ramadan.
Some men nevertheless betrayed themselves, so Allah revealed:
“Allah knew that you were betraying yourselves, so He accepted your repentance and pardoned you.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4508).

arabic_source:
١١٩٥٨ — عن البراء قال: كان أصحاب محمد ﷺ إذا كان الرجل صائمًا، فحضر الإفطار فنام قبل أن يفطر، لم يأكل ليلته ولا يومه حتى يمسي.
وإن قيس بن صرمة الأنصاري كان صائمًا، فلما حضر الإفطار أتى أهله فقال لها: أعندك طعام؟
قالت: لا، ولكن أنطلق فأطلب لك.
وكان يومه يعمل، فغلبته عيناه. فجاءت امرأته، فلما رأته قالت: خيبة لك.
فلما انتصف النهار غشي عليه، فذكر ذلك للنبي ﷺ، فنزلت هذه الآية:
﴿أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ الصِّيَامِ الرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَائِكُمْ﴾.
ففرحوا بها فرحًا شديدًا، ونزلت:
﴿وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ الْخَيْطِ الْأَسْوَدِ﴾.
صحيح: رواه البخاري في الصوم (١٩١٥)، عن عبيد اللّٰه بن موسى، عن إسرائيل، عن أبي إسحاق، عن البراء.

11958 — Al-Barāʾ narrated:
When one of the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ was fasting and the time for breaking the fast arrived, if he fell asleep before eating, he would not eat during that night or the following day until sunset.
Qays ibn Ṣirmah al-Anṣārī was fasting. When the time of breaking the fast came, he went to his wife and asked:
“Do you have any food?”
She replied:
“No, but I will go and look for some for you.”
He had been working throughout the day, and sleep overcame him.
When his wife returned and saw him asleep, she said:
“What a loss for you!”
By midday the following day, he lost consciousness.
The matter was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and this verse was revealed:
“It has been made lawful for you to be intimate with your wives during the nights of fasting.”
The Muslims rejoiced greatly at its revelation.
The following words were also revealed:
“Eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī in the Book of Fasting (1915), through ʿUbaydullāh ibn Mūsā, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Barāʾ.

١١٩٥٨ — عن البراء قال: كان أصحاب محمد ﷺ إذا كان الرجل صائمًا، فحضر الإفطار فنام قبل أن يفطر، لم يأكل ليلته ولا يومه حتى يمسي.
وإن قيس بن صرمة الأنصاري كان صائمًا، فلما حضر الإفطار أتى أهله فقال لها: أعندك طعام؟
قالت: لا، ولكن أنطلق فأطلب لك.
وكان يومه يعمل، فغلبته عيناه. فجاءت امرأته، فلما رأته قالت: خيبة لك.

﴿أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ الصِّيَامِ الرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَائِكُمْ﴾.

١١٩٥٩ — عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى:
﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾،
قال: فكان الناس على عهد رسول اللّٰه ﷺ إذا صلوا العتمة حرم عليهم الطعام والشراب والنساء، وصاموا إلى القابلة.
فاختان رجل نفسه، فجامع امرأته وقد صلى العشاء ولم يفطر. فأراد اللّٰه عز وجل أن يجعل ذلك يسرًا لمن بقي، ورخصة ومنفعة، فقال سبحانه:
﴿عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَخْتَانُونَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾.
وكان هذا مما نفع اللّٰه به الناس، ورخص لهم ويسر.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٢٣١٣).

11959 — Ibn ʿAbbās said concerning the words of Allah:
“O you who believe, fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you”:
During the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, once the people performed the night prayer, food, drink, and marital relations became forbidden to them, and they continued fasting until the following night.
A man betrayed himself by having relations with his wife after performing the night prayer, even though he had not yet broken his fast.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wished to make the matter easy for those who remained, as a concession and a benefit, so He said:
“Allah knew that you were betraying yourselves.”
This was among the things through which Allah benefited the people, granted them a concession, and made matters easy for them.
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (2313).

١١٩٦٠ — عن ابن عباس قال: إن الناس كانوا قبل أن ينزل في الصوم ما نزل، يأكلون ويشربون، ويحل لهم إتيان النساء، فإذا نام أحدهم لم يطعم ولم يشرب ولم يأت أهله حتى يفطر من القابلة.
فبلغنا أن عمر بن الخطاب بعدما نام، ووجب عليه الصوم، وقع على أهله، ثم جاء إلى النبي ﷺ فقال: أشكو إلى اللّٰه وإليك الذي صنعت.
قال: ((وماذا صنعت؟)).
قال: سولت لي نفسي، فوقعت على أهلي بعدما نمت، وأنا أريد الصوم.
فزعموا أن النبي ﷺ قال: ((ما كنت خليقًا أن تفعل)).
فنزل الكتاب:
﴿أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ الصِّيَامِ الرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَائِكُمْ﴾.
صحيح: رواه موسى بن عقبة، كما ذكره الحافظ ابن كثير في تفسيره (١/٥١١)، وإسناده صحيح، إلا قوله: «ما كنت خليقًا أن تفعل»، ففيه غرابة.

11960 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
Before the relevant ruling concerning fasting was revealed, people were permitted to eat, drink, and approach their wives. However, once one of them fell asleep, he could no longer eat, drink, or approach his wife until breaking the fast on the following night.
It reached us that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, after falling asleep and thereby entering the state in which fasting became binding upon him, had relations with his wife.
He then came to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“I complain to Allah and to you about what I have done.”
The Prophet ﷺ asked:
“What did you do?”
He replied:
“My soul enticed me, and I approached my wife after I had slept, even though I intended to fast.”
They claimed that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“It was not fitting for you to do that.”
Then the following revelation came:
“It has been made lawful for you to be intimate with your wives during the nights of fasting.”
Authentic: Narrated by Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, as mentioned by al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr (1/511). Its chain is authentic, except for the wording, “It was not fitting for you to do that,” which is unusual.

١١٩٦١ — عن موسى بن جبير مولى بني سلمة، أنه سمع عبد اللّٰه بن كعب بن مالك يحدث عن أبيه قال: كان الناس في رمضان إذا صام الرجل فأمسى فنام، حرم عليه الطعام والشراب والنساء حتى يفطر من الغد.
فرجع عمر بن الخطاب من عند النبي ﷺ ذات ليلة، وقد سهر عنده، فوجد امرأته قد نامت، فأرادها.
فقالت: إني قد نمت.
قال: ما نمت.
ثم وقع بها. وصنع كعب بن مالك مثل ذلك.
فغدا عمر إلى النبي ﷺ فأخبره، فأنزل اللّٰه تعالى:
﴿عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَخْتَانُونَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَعَفَا عَنْكُمْ﴾.
حسن: رواه أحمد (١٥٧٩٥).

١١٩٦٢ — عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى:
﴿أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ الصِّيَامِ الرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَائِكُمْ﴾،
قال: وذلك أن المسلمين كانوا في شهر رمضان إذا صلوا العشاء حرم عليهم النساء والطعام إلى مثلها من القابلة.
ثم إن أناسًا من المسلمين أصابوا الطعام والنساء في رمضان بعد العشاء، منهم عمر بن الخطاب، فشكوا ذلك إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ.
فأنزل اللّٰه:
﴿عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَخْتَانُونَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَعَفَا عَنْكُمْ فَالْآنَ بَاشِرُوهُنَّ﴾،
يعني: جامعوهن.
﴿وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ الْخَيْطِ الْأَسْوَدِ مِنَ الْفَجْرِ﴾.
حسن: رواه ابن جرير الطبري (٣/٢٣٥-٢٣٦).

11962 — Ibn ʿAbbās said concerning the words of Allah:
“It has been made lawful for you to be intimate with your wives during the nights of fasting”:
During Ramadan, once the Muslims performed the night prayer, women and food became forbidden to them until the same time on the following night.
Some Muslims nevertheless ate food and approached their wives after the night prayer during Ramadan. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was among them.
They complained about this to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so Allah revealed:
“Allah knew that you were betraying yourselves, so He accepted your repentance and pardoned you. Now, therefore, approach them,”
meaning: have marital relations with them.
And He revealed:
“Eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of dawn.”
Good: Narrated by Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī (3/235–236).

١١٩٦٣ — عن عدي بن حاتم قال: لما نزلت:
﴿حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ الْخَيْطِ الْأَسْوَدِ مِنَ الْفَجْرِ﴾،
عمدت إلى عقال أسود وإلى عقال أبيض، فجعلتهما تحت وسادتي، فجعلت أنظر في الليل فلا يستبين لي.
فغدوت على رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فذكرت له ذلك، فقال: ((إنما ذلك سواد الليل وبياض النهار)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٩١٦)، ومسلم (١٠٩٠)، واللفظ للبخاري.
وفي رواية عندهما قال له رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((إن وسادتك إذًا لعريض، إن كان الخيط الأبيض والخيط الأسود تحت وسادتك)).
رواه البخاري (٤٥٠٩)، ومسلم (١٠٩٠).
وفي لفظ عند البخاري (٤٥١٠): ((إنك لعريض القفا إن أبصرت الخيطين)). ثم قال: ((لا، بل هو سواد الليل وبياض النهار)).

11963 — ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim narrated:
When the verse was revealed:
“Until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of dawn,”
I took a black cord and a white cord and placed them beneath my pillow.
I continued looking at them during the night, but I could not distinguish one from the other.
The following morning, I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned this to him.
He said:
“It refers only to the darkness of the night and the whiteness of the day.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1916) and Muslim (1090). The wording cited here is that of al-Bukhārī.
In another narration recorded by both of them, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
“Your pillow must indeed be very broad if the white thread and black thread are beneath it.”
Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4509) and Muslim (1090).
In another wording narrated by al-Bukhārī (4510), he said:
“You must indeed have a very broad neck if you can see the two threads.”
He then explained:
“No. Rather, it means the darkness of the night and the whiteness of the day.”

﴿حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ الْخَيْطِ الْأَسْوَدِ مِنَ الْفَجْرِ﴾،
عمدت إلى عقال أسود وإلى عقال أبيض، فجعلتهما تحت وسادتي، فجعلت أنظر في الليل فلا يستبين لي.
فغدوت على رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فذكرت له ذلك، فقال: ((إنما ذلك سواد الليل وبياض النهار)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٩١٦)، ومسلم (١٠٩٠)، واللفظ للبخاري.
وفي رواية عندهما قال له رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((إن وسادتك إذًا لعريض، إن كان الخيط الأبيض والخيط الأسود تحت وسادتك)).
رواه البخاري (٤٥٠٩)، ومسلم (١٠٩٠).
وفي لفظ عند البخاري (٤٥١٠): ((إنك لعريض القفا إن أبصرت الخيطين)). ثم قال: ((لا، بل هو سواد الليل وبياض النهار)).
11963 — ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim narrated:
When the verse was revealed:
“Until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of dawn,”
I took a black cord and a white cord and placed them beneath my pillow.
I continued looking at them during the night, but I could not distinguish one from the other.
The following morning, I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned this to him.
He said:
“It refers only to the darkness of the night and the whiteness of the day.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1916) and Muslim (1090). The wording cited here is that of al-Bukhārī.
In another narration recorded by both of them, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
“Your pillow must indeed be very broad if the white thread and black thread are beneath it.”
Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4509) and Muslim (1090).
In another wording narrated by al-Bukhārī (4510), he said:
“You must indeed have a very broad neck if you can see the two threads.”
He then explained:
“No. Rather, it means the darkness of the night and the whiteness of the day.”

١١٩٦٤ — عن سهل بن سعد قال: أنزلت:
﴿وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ الْخَيْطِ الْأَسْوَدِ﴾،
ولم ينزل: ﴿مِنَ الْفَجْرِ﴾.
فكان رجال إذا أرادوا الصوم ربط أحدهم في رجليه الخيط الأبيض والخيط الأسود، ولم يزل يأكل حتى يتبين له رؤيتهما.
فأنزل اللّٰه بعد: ﴿مِنَ الْفَجْرِ﴾، فعلموا أنه إنما يعني الليل والنهار.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري في الصوم (١٩١٧)، ومسلم (١٠٩١/٣٥).
قوله تعالى: ﴿ثُمَّ أَتِمُّوا الصِّيَامَ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ﴾

11964 — Sahl ibn Saʿd narrated:
The following words were first revealed:
“Eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread,”
but the words:
“Of dawn”
had not yet been revealed.
When some men intended to fast, they would tie a white thread and a black thread to their legs and continue eating until they could distinguish between them.
Allah later revealed the words:
“Of dawn,”
and they then understood that the verse referred to the night and the day.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī in the Book of Fasting (1917) and Muslim (1091/35).
The Words of Allah: “Then Complete the Fast until Nightfall”

١١٩٦٥ — عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((إذا أقبل الليل من ها هنا، وأدبر النهار من ها هنا، وغربت الشمس، فقد أفطر الصائم)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٩٥٤)، ومسلم (١١٠٠)، واللفظ للبخاري.
قوله تعالى: ﴿وَلَا تُبَاشِرُوهُنَّ وَأَنْتُمْ عَاكِفُونَ فِي الْمَسَاجِدِ﴾

11965 — ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“When the night approaches from this direction, the day withdraws from that direction, and the sun has set, the fasting person has reached the time of breaking his fast.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1954) and Muslim (1100). The wording cited here is that of al-Bukhārī.
The Words of Allah: “Do Not Approach Them while You Are Remaining in Seclusion in the Mosques”

١١٩٦٦ — عن عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ قالت: إن كنت لأدخل البيت للحاجة، والمريض فيه، فما أسأل عنه إلا وأنا مارة.
وإن كان رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ليدخل علي رأسه وهو في المسجد فأرجله، وكان لا يدخل البيت إلا لحاجة إذا كان معتكفًا.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٠٢٩)، ومسلم (٢٩٧/٧)، واللفظ لمسلم.

11966 — ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, narrated:
I would enter the house only for a necessary purpose. If there was an ill person inside, I would not ask about him except while passing by.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would extend his head to me while he remained in the mosque, and I would comb his hair.
When he was observing iʿtikāf, he would not enter the house except for a necessary purpose.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2029) and Muslim (297/7). The wording cited here is that of Muslim.

١١٩٦٧ — عن أم سلمة، عن النبي ﷺ قال: ((إنما أنا بشر، وإنكم تختصمون إلي، ولعل بعضكم أن يكون ألحن بحجته من بعض، فأقضي له على نحو ما أسمع. فمن قضيت له من حق أخيه شيئًا فلا يأخذه؛ فإنما أقطع له قطعة من النار)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٩٦٧)، ومسلم (١٧١٣)، واللفظ للبخاري.

11967 — Umm Salamah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“I am only a human being, and you bring your disputes before me. Perhaps one of you is more eloquent and persuasive in presenting his argument than another, so I judge in his favor according to what I hear.
If I award someone anything that rightfully belongs to his brother, he must not take it, for I have only cut out for him a piece of the Fire.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6967) and Muslim (1713). The wording cited here is that of al-Bukhārī.

١١٩٦٩ — عن جابر بن عبد اللّٰه قال: كانت قريش يدعون الحمس، وكانوا يدخلون من الأبواب في الإحرام، وكانت الأنصار وسائر العرب لا يدخلون من الأبواب في الإحرام.
فبينما رسول اللّٰه ﷺ في بستان، فخرج من بابه، وخرج معه قطبة بن عامر الأنصاري.
فقالوا: يا رسول اللّٰه، إن قطبة بن عامر رجل فاجر، إنه خرج معك من الباب.
فقال: ((ما حملك على ذلك؟)).
قال: رأيتك فعلت ففعلت.
فقال: ((إني أحمسي)).
فقال: إن ديني دينك.
فأنزل اللّٰه عز وجل:
﴿وَلَيْسَ الْبِرُّ بِأَنْ تَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهَا وَلَٰكِنَّ الْبِرَّ مَنِ اتَّقَىٰ وَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ مِنْ أَبْوَابِهَا﴾.
صحيح: رواه الحاكم (١/٤٨٣)، والواحدي في أسباب النزول (ص ٤٨).
ثم قال الواحدي: «وقال المفسرون: كان الناس في الجاهلية وفي أول الإسلام إذا أحرم الرجل منهم بالحج أو العمرة، لم يدخل حائطًا ولا بيتًا ولا دارًا من بابه.
فإن كان من أهل المدينة نقب نقبًا في ظهر بيته، منه يدخل ويخرج، أو اتخذ سلمًا فصعد فيه.
وإن كان من أهل الوبر خرج من خلف الخيمة والفسطاط، ولا يدخل من الباب حتى يحل من إحرامه، ويرون ذلك دينًا.
إلا أن يكون من الحمس، وهم قريش، وكنانة، وخزاعة، وثقيف، وخثعم، وبنو عامر بن صعصعة، وبنو النضر بن معاوية. سموا حمسًا لشدتهم في دينهم.
قالوا: فدخل رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ذات يوم بيتًا لبعض الأنصار، فدخل رجل من الأنصار على أثره من الباب وهو محرم، فأنكروا عليه.
فقال له رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((لم دخلت من الباب وأنت محرم؟)).
فقال: رأيتك دخلت من الباب، فدخلت على أثرك.
فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((إني أحمسي)).
قال الرجل: إن كنت أحمسيًا فإني أحمسي، ديننا واحد، رضيت بهديك وسمتك ودينك.
فأنزل اللّٰه هذه الآية». انتهى.

11969 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated:
Quraysh were known as al-Ḥums, and while in the state of iḥrām they would enter houses through their doors.
The Anṣār and the other Arabs, however, would not enter through doors while in iḥrām.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was once inside a garden and came out through its gate. Quṭbah ibn ʿĀmir al-Anṣārī came out through the gate with him.
The people said:
“O Messenger of Allah, Quṭbah ibn ʿĀmir is a sinful man. He came out through the gate with you.”
The Prophet ﷺ asked him:
“What caused you to do that?”
He replied:
“I saw you do it, so I did the same.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“I am from al-Ḥums.”
The man replied:
“Your religion is my religion.”
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then revealed:
“Righteousness is not that you enter houses from the rear, but righteousness belongs to the one who fears Allah. Enter houses through their doors.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Ḥākim (1/483) and al-Wāḥidī in Asbāb al-Nuzūl (p. 48).
Al-Wāḥidī then said:
“The commentators said that during the pre-Islamic period and at the beginning of Islam, when a man entered the state of iḥrām for Ḥajj or ʿUmrah, he would not enter an enclosure, house, or dwelling through its door.
If he was from the people of Madinah, he would make an opening in the rear of his house through which he entered and exited, or he would set up a ladder and climb over it.
If he lived in tents, he would leave from the rear of his tent or pavilion and would not enter through the front opening until he completed his state of iḥrām. They considered this a religious practice.
The only exception was one of al-Ḥums. These included Quraysh, Kinānah, Khuzāʿah, Thaqīf, Khathʿam, Banū ʿĀmir ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿah, and Banū al-Naḍr ibn Muʿāwiyah. They were called al-Ḥums because of their strictness in religion.
They said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ once entered a house belonging to one of the Anṣār. A man from the Anṣār followed him through the door while in iḥrām, and the people objected to him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked him, ‘Why did you enter through the door while in iḥrām?’
He replied, ‘I saw you enter through the door, so I followed you.’
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, ‘I am from al-Ḥums.’
The man replied, ‘If you are from al-Ḥums, then I am also from al-Ḥums. Our religion is one. I am pleased with your guidance, manner, and religion.’
Allah then revealed this verse.”
End quote.

﴿وَلَيْسَ الْبِرُّ بِأَنْ تَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهَا وَلَٰكِنَّ الْبِرَّ مَنِ اتَّقَىٰ وَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ مِنْ أَبْوَابِهَا﴾.
صحيح: رواه الحاكم (١/٤٨٣)، والواحدي في أسباب النزول (ص ٤٨).
ثم قال الواحدي: «وقال المفسرون: كان الناس في الجاهلية وفي أول الإسلام إذا أحرم الرجل منهم بالحج أو العمرة، لم يدخل حائطًا ولا بيتًا ولا دارًا من بابه.
فإن كان من أهل المدينة نقب نقبًا في ظهر بيته، منه يدخل ويخرج، أو اتخذ سلمًا فصعد فيه.
وإن كان من أهل الوبر خرج من خلف الخيمة والفسطاط، ولا يدخل من الباب حتى يحل من إحرامه، ويرون ذلك دينًا.
إلا أن يكون من الحمس، وهم قريش، وكنانة، وخزاعة، وثقيف، وخثعم، وبنو عامر بن صعصعة، وبنو النضر بن معاوية. سموا حمسًا لشدتهم في دينهم.
قالوا: فدخل رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ذات يوم بيتًا لبعض الأنصار، فدخل رجل من الأنصار على أثره من الباب وهو محرم، فأنكروا عليه.
فقال له رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((لم دخلت من الباب وأنت محرم؟)).
فقال: رأيتك دخلت من الباب، فدخلت على أثرك.
فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((إني أحمسي)).
قال الرجل: إن كنت أحمسيًا فإني أحمسي، ديننا واحد، رضيت بهديك وسمتك ودينك.
فأنزل اللّٰه هذه الآية». انتهى.
11969 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated:
Quraysh were known as al-Ḥums, and while in the state of iḥrām they would enter houses through their doors.
The Anṣār and the other Arabs, however, would not enter through doors while in iḥrām.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was once inside a garden and came out through its gate. Quṭbah ibn ʿĀmir al-Anṣārī came out through the gate with him.
The people said:
“O Messenger of Allah, Quṭbah ibn ʿĀmir is a sinful man. He came out through the gate with you.”
The Prophet ﷺ asked him:
“What caused you to do that?”
He replied:
“I saw you do it, so I did the same.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“I am from al-Ḥums.”
The man replied:
“Your religion is my religion.”
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then revealed:
“Righteousness is not that you enter houses from the rear, but righteousness belongs to the one who fears Allah. Enter houses through their doors.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Ḥākim (1/483) and al-Wāḥidī in Asbāb al-Nuzūl (p. 48).
Al-Wāḥidī then said:
“The commentators said that during the pre-Islamic period and at the beginning of Islam, when a man entered the state of iḥrām for Ḥajj or ʿUmrah, he would not enter an enclosure, house, or dwelling through its door.
If he was from the people of Madinah, he would make an opening in the rear of his house through which he entered and exited, or he would set up a ladder and climb over it.
If he lived in tents, he would leave from the rear of his tent or pavilion and would not enter through the front opening until he completed his state of iḥrām. They considered this a religious practice.
The only exception was one of al-Ḥums. These included Quraysh, Kinānah, Khuzāʿah, Thaqīf, Khathʿam, Banū ʿĀmir ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿah, and Banū al-Naḍr ibn Muʿāwiyah. They were called al-Ḥums because of their strictness in religion.
They said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ once entered a house belonging to one of the Anṣār. A man from the Anṣār followed him through the door while in iḥrām, and the people objected to him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked him, ‘Why did you enter through the door while in iḥrām?’
He replied, ‘I saw you enter through the door, so I followed you.’
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, ‘I am from al-Ḥums.’
The man replied, ‘If you are from al-Ḥums, then I am also from al-Ḥums. Our religion is one. I am pleased with your guidance, manner, and religion.’
Allah then revealed this verse.”
End quote.

١١٩٧٠ — عن بريدة قال:
كان رسول الله ﷺ إذا أمّر أميرًا على جيش أو سرية أوصاه في خاصته بتقوى الله، ومن معه من المسلمين خيرًا، ثم قال:
«اغْزُوا بِاسْمِ اللَّهِ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ، قَاتِلُوا مَنْ كَفَرَ بِاللَّهِ. اغْزُوا، وَلَا تَغُلُّوا، وَلَا تَغْدِرُوا، وَلَا تُمَثِّلُوا، وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا وَلِيدًا…».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٧٣١/٣).

11970 — Buraydah reported:
Whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed a commander over an army or military detachment, he would specifically advise him to fear Allah and to treat the Muslims accompanying him well.
He would then say:
“Fight in the name of Allah, in the path of Allah. Fight those who disbelieve in Allah. Go forth, but do not misappropriate the spoils, do not act treacherously, do not mutilate, and do not kill a child…”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1731/3).

١١٩٧١ — عن نافع، عن ابن عمر، قال: أتاه رجلان في فتنة ابن الزبير، فقالا: إن الناس ضيعوا، وأنت ابن عمر وصاحب النبي ﷺ، فما يمنعك أن تخرج؟
قال: يمنعني أن اللّٰه حرم دم أخي.
قالا: ألم يقل اللّٰه:
﴿وَقَاتِلُوهُمْ حَتَّىٰ لَا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ﴾؟
قال: قاتلنا حتى لم تكن فتنة، وكان الدين للّٰه، وأنتم تريدون أن تقاتلوا حتى تكون فتنة ويكون الدين لغير اللّٰه.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٤٥١٣).
قال البخاري (٤٥١٤): وزاد عثمان بن صالح، عن وهب، قال: أخبرني فلان وحيوة بن شريح، عن بكر بن عمرو المعافري، أن بكير بن عبد اللّٰه حدثه، عن نافع:
أن رجلًا أتى ابن عمر، فقال له: يا أبا عبد الرحمن، ما حملك على أن تحج عامًا وتعتمر عامًا، وتترك الجهاد في سبيل اللّٰه، وقد علمت ما رغب اللّٰه فيه؟
فقال: يا ابن أخي، بني الإسلام على خمس: الإيمان باللّٰه ورسوله، والصلوات الخمس، وصيام رمضان، وأداء الزكاة، وحج البيت.
قال: يا أبا عبد الرحمن، ألا تسمع ما ذكر اللّٰه في كتابه:
﴿وَإِنْ طَائِفَتَانِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ اقْتَتَلُوا فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُمَا، فَإِنْ بَغَتْ إِحْدَاهُمَا عَلَى الْأُخْرَىٰ فَقَاتِلُوا الَّتِي تَبْغِي حَتَّىٰ تَفِيءَ إِلَىٰ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ [الحجرات: ٩]،
و﴿وَقَاتِلُوهُمْ حَتَّىٰ لَا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ﴾؟
قال: فعلنا على عهد النبي ﷺ، وكان الإسلام قليلًا، وكان الرجل يفتن في دينه: إما قتلوه أو عذبوه، حتى كثر الإسلام فلم تكن فتنة.
قال: فما قولك في علي وعثمان؟
قال: أما عثمان، فكان اللّٰه عفا عنه، وأما أنتم فكرهتم أن تعفوا عنه. وأما علي، فابن عم رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وختنه.
وأشار بيده فقال: هذا بيته حيث ترون. انتهى.

11971 — Nāfiʿ narrated from Ibn ʿUmar:
Two men came to him during the turmoil involving Ibn al-Zubayr and said:
“The people have fallen into disorder. You are Ibn ʿUmar and a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ. What prevents you from going out to fight?”
He replied:
“What prevents me is that Allah has forbidden me from shedding the blood of my Muslim brother.”
They said:
“Did Allah not say:
‘Fight them until there is no more persecution’?”
He replied:
“We fought until there was no more persecution and religion belonged to Allah. You wish to fight until persecution returns and religion belongs to other than Allah.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4513).
Al-Bukhārī (4514) said:
ʿUthmān ibn Ṣāliḥ added, narrating from Wahb, who said: So-and-so and Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ informed me, from Bakr ibn ʿAmr al-Maʿāfirī, that Bukayr ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated to him from Nāfiʿ:
A man came to Ibn ʿUmar and asked:
“Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, what causes you to perform Ḥajj one year and ʿUmrah another year while abandoning fighting in the cause of Allah, although you know the encouragement Allah has given concerning it?”
He replied:
“Son of my brother, Islam is built upon five: belief in Allah and His Messenger, the five prayers, fasting Ramadan, paying zakāh, and pilgrimage to the House.”
The man said:
“Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, do you not hear what Allah mentioned in His Book:
‘If two groups of believers fight one another, reconcile between them. If one of them transgresses against the other, fight the transgressing group until it returns to Allah’s command’
 [Sūrat al-Ḥujurāt 49:9],
and:
‘Fight them until there is no more persecution’?”
Ibn ʿUmar replied:
“We did that during the time of the Prophet ﷺ, when Islam was weak in numbers. A man would be persecuted because of his religion: they would either kill or torture him. When Islam became widespread, there was no longer persecution.”
The man asked:
“What is your opinion concerning ʿAlī and ʿUthmān?”
He replied:
“As for ʿUthmān, Allah pardoned him, but you disliked pardoning him. As for ʿAlī, he was the cousin and son-in-law of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”
He pointed with his hand and said:
“That is his house, where you can see it.”
End of the report.

﴿وَإِنْ طَائِفَتَانِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ اقْتَتَلُوا فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُمَا، فَإِنْ بَغَتْ إِحْدَاهُمَا عَلَى الْأُخْرَىٰ فَقَاتِلُوا الَّتِي تَبْغِي حَتَّىٰ تَفِيءَ إِلَىٰ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ [الحجرات: ٩]،
و﴿وَقَاتِلُوهُمْ حَتَّىٰ لَا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ﴾؟
قال: فعلنا على عهد النبي ﷺ، وكان الإسلام قليلًا، وكان الرجل يفتن في دينه: إما قتلوه أو عذبوه، حتى كثر الإسلام فلم تكن فتنة.
قال: فما قولك في علي وعثمان؟
قال: أما عثمان، فكان اللّٰه عفا عنه، وأما أنتم فكرهتم أن تعفوا عنه. وأما علي، فابن عم رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وختنه.

11971 — Nāfiʿ narrated from Ibn ʿUmar:
Two men came to him during the turmoil involving Ibn al-Zubayr and said:
“The people have fallen into disorder. You are Ibn ʿUmar and a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ. What prevents you from going out to fight?”
He replied:
“What prevents me is that Allah has forbidden me from shedding the blood of my Muslim brother.”
They said:
“Did Allah not say:
‘Fight them until there is no more persecution’?”
He replied:
“We fought until there was no more persecution and religion belonged to Allah. You wish to fight until persecution returns and religion belongs to other than Allah.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4513).
Al-Bukhārī (4514) said:
ʿUthmān ibn Ṣāliḥ added, narrating from Wahb, who said: So-and-so and Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ informed me, from Bakr ibn ʿAmr al-Maʿāfirī, that Bukayr ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated to him from Nāfiʿ:
A man came to Ibn ʿUmar and asked:
“Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, what causes you to perform Ḥajj one year and ʿUmrah another year while abandoning fighting in the cause of Allah, although you know the encouragement Allah has given concerning it?”
He replied:
“Son of my brother, Islam is built upon five: belief in Allah and His Messenger, the five prayers, fasting Ramadan, paying zakāh, and pilgrimage to the House.”
The man said:
“Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, do you not hear what Allah mentioned in His Book:
‘If two groups of believers fight one another, reconcile between them. If one of them transgresses against the other, fight the transgressing group until it returns to Allah’s command’
 [Sūrat al-Ḥujurāt 49:9],
and:
‘Fight them until there is no more persecution’?”
Ibn ʿUmar replied:
“We did that during the time of the Prophet ﷺ, when Islam was weak in numbers. A man would be persecuted because of his religion: they would either kill or torture him. When Islam became widespread, there was no longer persecution.”
The man asked:
“What is your opinion concerning ʿAlī and ʿUthmān?”
He replied:
“As for ʿUthmān, Allah pardoned him, but you disliked pardoning him. As for ʿAlī, he was the cousin and son-in-law of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”
He pointed with his hand and said:
“That is his house, where you can see it.”
End of the report.

١١٩٧٣ — عن أسلم أبي عمران التجيبي قال: كنا بمدينة الروم، فأخرجوا إلينا صفًا عظيمًا من الروم، فخرج إليهم من المسلمين مثلهم أو أكثر.
وعلى أهل مصر عقبة بن عامر، وعلى الجماعة فضالة بن عبيد.
فحمل رجل من المسلمين على صف الروم حتى دخل فيهم، فصاح الناس وقالوا: سبحان اللّٰه، يلقي بيديه إلى التهلكة!
فقام أبو أيوب الأنصاري فقال: يا أيها الناس، إنكم لتؤولون هذه الآية هذا التأويل، وإنما أنزلت هذه الآية فينا معشر الأنصار.
لما أعز اللّٰه الإسلام وكثر ناصروه، فقال بعضنا لبعض سرًا دون رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: إن أموالنا قد ضاعت، وإن اللّٰه قد أعز الإسلام وكثر ناصروه، فلو أقمنا في أموالنا فأصلحنا ما ضاع منها.
فأنزل اللّٰه على نبيه ﷺ يرد علينا ما قلنا:
﴿وَأَنْفِقُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلَا تُلْقُوا بِأَيْدِيكُمْ إِلَى التَّهْلُكَةِ﴾.
فكانت التهلكة الإقامة على الأموال وإصلاحها وتركنا الغزو.
فما زال أبو أيوب شاخصًا في سبيل اللّٰه حتى دفن بأرض الروم.
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٢٥١٢)، والترمذي (٢٩٧٢)، وابن أبي حاتم (١/٣٣٠-٣٣١)، وصححه ابن حبان (٤٧١١).

11973 — Aslam Abū ʿImrān al-Tujībī narrated:
We were in a city of the Byzantine lands. The Byzantines brought out against us an enormous battle formation, and an equal or larger number of Muslims advanced against them.
ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir commanded the troops from Egypt, while Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd commanded the entire force.
A Muslim man charged into the Byzantine ranks until he entered among them.
The people shouted:
“Glory be to Allah! He is throwing himself into destruction!”
Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī stood and said:
“People, you are interpreting this verse in this manner, but it was revealed concerning us, the Anṣār.
When Allah strengthened Islam and increased its supporters, some of us secretly said to one another, without the Messenger of Allah ﷺ being present:
‘Our wealth has been neglected. Allah has strengthened Islam and increased its supporters. Perhaps we should remain with our property and repair what has been lost.’
Allah then revealed to His Prophet ﷺ, refuting what we had said:
‘Spend in the cause of Allah and do not throw yourselves into destruction.’
Destruction meant remaining with our property, restoring it, and abandoning military expeditions.”
Abū Ayyūb continued going forth in the cause of Allah until he was buried in Byzantine territory.
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (2512), al-Tirmidhī (2972), Ibn Abī Ḥātim (1/330–331), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (4711).

لما أعز اللّٰه الإسلام وكثر ناصروه، فقال بعضنا لبعض سرًا دون رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: إن أموالنا قد ضاعت، وإن اللّٰه قد أعز الإسلام وكثر ناصروه، فلو أقمنا في أموالنا فأصلحنا ما ضاع منها.
فأنزل اللّٰه على نبيه ﷺ يرد علينا ما قلنا:
﴿وَأَنْفِقُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلَا تُلْقُوا بِأَيْدِيكُمْ إِلَى التَّهْلُكَةِ﴾.
فكانت التهلكة الإقامة على الأموال وإصلاحها وتركنا الغزو.
فما زال أبو أيوب شاخصًا في سبيل اللّٰه حتى دفن بأرض الروم.
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٢٥١٢)، والترمذي (٢٩٧٢)، وابن أبي حاتم (١/٣٣٠-٣٣١)، وصححه ابن حبان (٤٧١١).
11973 — Aslam Abū ʿImrān al-Tujībī narrated:
We were in a city of the Byzantine lands. The Byzantines brought out against us an enormous battle formation, and an equal or larger number of Muslims advanced against them.
ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir commanded the troops from Egypt, while Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd commanded the entire force.
A Muslim man charged into the Byzantine ranks until he entered among them.
The people shouted:
“Glory be to Allah! He is throwing himself into destruction!”
Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī stood and said:
“People, you are interpreting this verse in this manner, but it was revealed concerning us, the Anṣār.
When Allah strengthened Islam and increased its supporters, some of us secretly said to one another, without the Messenger of Allah ﷺ being present:
‘Our wealth has been neglected. Allah has strengthened Islam and increased its supporters. Perhaps we should remain with our property and repair what has been lost.’
Allah then revealed to His Prophet ﷺ, refuting what we had said:
‘Spend in the cause of Allah and do not throw yourselves into destruction.’
Destruction meant remaining with our property, restoring it, and abandoning military expeditions.”
Abū Ayyūb continued going forth in the cause of Allah until he was buried in Byzantine territory.
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (2512), al-Tirmidhī (2972), Ibn Abī Ḥātim (1/330–331), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (4711).

arabic_source:
١١٩٧٤ — عن أبي جبيرة بن الضحاك قال: كانت الأنصار يتصدقون، يعطون ما شاء اللّٰه، فأصابتهم سنة فأمسكوا، فأنزل اللّٰه عز وجل:
﴿وَأَنْفِقُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلَا تُلْقُوا بِأَيْدِيكُمْ إِلَى التَّهْلُكَةِ وَأَحْسِنُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾.
حسن: رواه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره (١/٣٣٢)، والطبراني في الكبير (٢٢/٣٩٠).
وقد فسر جمهور أهل العلم التهلكة هنا بترك النفقة في سبيل اللّٰه.
والمعنى الثاني للتهلكة هو ظن المذنب بأنه لا توبة له، وفي ذلك أحاديث.

english_source:
11974 — Abū Jabīrah ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk narrated:
The Anṣār used to give charity and spend whatever Allah willed.
When a year of hardship afflicted them, they withheld their spending.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then revealed:
“Spend in the cause of Allah and do not throw yourselves into destruction. Do good, for Allah loves those who do good.”
Good: Narrated by Ibn Abī Ḥātim in his Tafsīr (1/332) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (22/390).
The majority of scholars interpreted destruction in this verse as abandoning expenditure in the cause of Allah.
A second meaning of destruction is that a sinner assumes there can be no repentance for him. Reports have also been transmitted concerning this interpretation.

arabic_source:
١١٩٧٧ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن معقل قال: قعدت إلى كعب بن عجرة في هذا المسجد، يعني مسجد الكوفة، فسألته عن فدية من صيام.
فقال: حملت إلى النبي ﷺ والقمل يتناثر على وجهي.
فقال: ((ما كنت أرى أن الجهد قد بلغ بك هذا، أما تجد شاة؟)).
قلت: لا.
قال: ((صم ثلاثة أيام، أو أطعم ستة مساكين، لكل مسكين نصف صاع من طعام، واحلق رأسك)).
فنزلت في خاصة، وهي لكم عامة.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٥١٧)، ومسلم (١٢٠١/٨٥).
قوله تعالى: ﴿فَمَنْ تَمَتَّعَ بِالْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ﴾

english_source:
11977 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Maʿqil narrated:
I sat beside Kaʿb ibn ʿUjrah in this mosque—meaning the mosque of Kūfah—and asked him about the compensation involving fasting.
He replied:
I was carried to the Prophet ﷺ while lice were falling across my face.
He said:
“I did not realize that your suffering had reached this degree. Can you find a sheep?”
I replied:
“No.”
He said:
“Fast for three days, or feed six poor people, giving each poor person half a ṣāʿ of food, and shave your head.”
This verse was revealed specifically concerning me, but its ruling applies generally to all of you.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4517) and Muslim (1201/85).
The Words of Allah: “Whoever Performs ʿUmrah Followed by Ḥajj…”

The Words of Allah: “Whoever Performs ʿUmrah Followed by Ḥajj…”
full_display_content:
١١٩٧٧ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن معقل قال: قعدت إلى كعب بن عجرة في هذا المسجد، يعني مسجد الكوفة، فسألته عن فدية من صيام.
فقال: حملت إلى النبي ﷺ والقمل يتناثر على وجهي.
فقال: ((ما كنت أرى أن الجهد قد بلغ بك هذا، أما تجد شاة؟)).
قلت: لا.
قال: ((صم ثلاثة أيام، أو أطعم ستة مساكين، لكل مسكين نصف صاع من طعام، واحلق رأسك)).
فنزلت في خاصة، وهي لكم عامة.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٥١٧)، ومسلم (١٢٠١/٨٥).
قوله تعالى: ﴿فَمَنْ تَمَتَّعَ بِالْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ﴾
11977 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Maʿqil narrated:
I sat beside Kaʿb ibn ʿUjrah in this mosque—meaning the mosque of Kūfah—and asked him about the compensation involving fasting.
He replied:
I was carried to the Prophet ﷺ while lice were falling across my face.
He said:
“I did not realize that your suffering had reached this degree. Can you find a sheep?”
I replied:
“No.”
He said:
“Fast for three days, or feed six poor people, giving each poor person half a ṣāʿ of food, and shave your head.”
This verse was revealed specifically concerning me, but its ruling applies generally to all of you.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4517) and Muslim (1201/85).
The Words of Allah: “Whoever Performs ʿUmrah Followed by Ḥajj…”

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٥١٨)، ومسلم (١٢٢٦/١٧٢)، واللفظ للبخاري.

11978 — ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn narrated:
The verse concerning tamattuʿ was revealed in the Book of Allah, and we practiced it with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
No Qur’anic verse was revealed prohibiting it, and the Prophet ﷺ did not forbid it before his death.
A man later expressed whatever opinion he wished concerning it.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4518) and Muslim (1226/172). The wording cited here is that of al-Bukhārī.
The statement:
“A man later expressed whatever opinion he wished”
has been interpreted as referring to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, who discouraged tamattuʿ so that people would continue journeying to the Sacred House separately as pilgrims for Ḥajj and as performers of ʿUmrah.

١١٩٧٩ — عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ في قول اللّٰه عز وجل:
﴿فَلَا رَفَثَ وَلَا فُسُوقَ وَلَا جِدَالَ فِي الْحَجِّ﴾،
قال: ((الرفث الإعرابة والتعرض للنساء بالجماع، والفسوق المعاصي كلها، والجدال جدال الرجل صاحبه)).
حسن: رواه الطبراني في الكبير (١١/٢٢).
قوله تعالى: ﴿وَتَزَوَّدُوا فَإِنَّ خَيْرَ الزَّادِ التَّقْوَىٰ﴾

english_source:
11979 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said concerning the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
“There must be no sexual speech, sin, or quarreling during Ḥajj”:
“Sexual speech means explicit references to intercourse and approaching women concerning it. Sin includes every act of disobedience, and quarreling means a man arguing with his companion.”
Good: Narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (11/22).
The Words of Allah: “Take Provisions, but the Best Provision Is God-Consciousness”

١١٩٨٠ — عن ابن عباس قال: كان أهل اليمن يحجون ولا يتزودون، ويقولون: نحن المتوكلون.
فإذا قدموا مكة سألوا الناس، فأنزل اللّٰه تعالى:
﴿وَتَزَوَّدُوا فَإِنَّ خَيْرَ الزَّادِ التَّقْوَىٰ﴾.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (١٥٢٣).

11980 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
The people of Yemen used to perform Ḥajj without taking provisions, saying:
“We are those who place their trust in Allah.”
When they reached Makkah, they would beg from the people.
Allah, the Exalted, then revealed:
“Take provisions, but the best provision is God-consciousness.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1523).

١١٩٨١ — عن ابن عباس قال: كانت عكاظ، ومجنة، وذو المجاز أسواقًا في الجاهلية، فتأثموا أن يتجروا في المواسم، فنزلت:
﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾،
في مواسم الحج.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٤٥١٩).

11981 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
ʿUkāẓ, Majannah, and Dhū al-Majāz were markets during the pre-Islamic period.
The Muslims later feared that conducting trade during the pilgrimage season might be sinful.
Allah then revealed:
“There is no sin upon you in seeking bounty from your Lord,”
concerning trade during the seasons of Ḥajj.
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4519).
