12916 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd narrated:
I asked—or the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked:
“Which sin is greatest in the sight of Allah?”
He replied:
“That you appoint a rival to Allah even though He created you.”
I asked:
“Then which?”
He replied:
“That you kill your child out of fear that he will share your food.”
I asked:
“Then which?”
He replied:
“That you commit adultery with your neighbor’s wife.”
The following verse was revealed confirming the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
“Those who do not invoke another god alongside Allah, do not kill a soul whom Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit adultery.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4761) and Muslim (86). The wording is that of al-Bukhārī, while Muslim’s wording is similar.

١٢٩١٧ — عن ابن عباس أن ناسًا من أهل الشرك كانوا قد قتلوا فأكثروا، وزنوا فأكثروا، فأتوا محمدًا ﷺ فقالوا: إن الذي تقول وتدعو إليه لحسن، لو تخبرنا أن لما عملنا كفارة.
فنزل: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَدْعُونَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا آخَرَ وَلَا يَقْتُلُونَ النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَلَا يَزْنُونَ﴾.
ونزلت: ﴿قُلْ يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلَىٰ أَنْفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ [الزمر: ٥٣].
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٨١٠)، ومسلم (١٢٢).

english_source:
12917 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
Some polytheists had committed many murders and committed adultery frequently. They came to Muḥammad ﷺ and said:
“What you say and call people toward is certainly good. Could you tell us whether there is any expiation for what we have done?”
Then the following verse was revealed:
“Those who do not invoke another god alongside Allah, do not kill a soul whom Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit adultery.”
The following verse was also revealed:
“Say: ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of Allah’s mercy. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. He is truly the Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful.’”
 [Sūrat al-Zumar 39:53]
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4810) and Muslim (122).

١٢٩١٨ — عن سعيد بن جبير قال: قال ابن أبزى: سل ابن عباس عن قوله تعالى: ﴿وَمَنْ يَقْتُلْ مُؤْمِنًا مُتَعَمِّدًا فَجَزَاؤُهُ جَهَنَّمُ خَالِدًا فِيهَا وَغَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَلَعَنَهُ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُ عَذَابًا عَظِيمًا﴾ [النساء: ٩٣]، وقوله: ﴿وَلَا يَقْتُلُونَ النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ﴾ حتى بلغ: ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ تَابَ﴾.
فسألته، فقال: لما نزلت قال أهل مكة: فقد عدلنا باللّٰه، وقد قتلنا النفس التي حرم اللّٰه إلا بالحق، وأتينا الفواحش.
فأنزل اللّٰه: ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ تَابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلًا صَالِحًا﴾ إلى قوله: ﴿غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا﴾.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٧٦٥)، ومسلم (٣٠٢٣: ١٩). واللفظ للبخاري، ولفظ مسلم نحوه، وزاد في آخره: قال: فأما من دخل في الإسلام وعقله، ثم قتل، فلا توبة له.

12918 — Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated:
Ibn Abzā said to me:
“Ask Ibn ʿAbbās about the words of Allah:
‘Whoever deliberately kills a believer, his recompense is Hell, remaining there, and Allah is angry with him, has cursed him, and has prepared for him a tremendous punishment,’
 [Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:93]
and about His words:
‘They do not kill a soul whom Allah has forbidden except by right,’”
until the verse reaches:
“Except those who repent.”
I asked Ibn ʿAbbās, and he replied:
When this verse was revealed, the people of Makkah said:
“We have associated partners with Allah, killed souls whom Allah had forbidden us to kill, and committed indecent acts.”
Allah therefore revealed:
“Except those who repent, believe, and perform righteous deeds,”
until the words:
“Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4765) and Muslim (3023:19). The wording is that of al-Bukhārī, while Muslim’s wording is similar.

١٢٩١٩ — عن سلمة بن قيس الأشجعي قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ في حجة الوداع:
((إنما هن أربع: لا تشركوا باللّٰه شيئًا، ولا تقتلوا النفس التي حرم اللّٰه إلا بالحق، ولا تزنوا، ولا تسرقوا)).
قال: فما أنا بأشح عليهن مني إذ سمعتهن من رسول اللّٰه ﷺ.
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٨٩٩)، والنسائي في السنن الكبرى (١١٣٠٩)، والحاكم (٤/٣٥١).

12919 — Salamah ibn Qays al-Ashjaʿī narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said during the Farewell Pilgrimage:
“They are only four: do not associate anything with Allah, do not kill a soul whom Allah has forbidden except by right, do not commit adultery, and do not steal.”
Salamah said:
“I have never guarded anything more carefully than these commands since hearing them from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (1899), al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (11309), and al-Ḥākim (4/351).
Regarding the words:
“Except those who repent, believe, and perform righteous deeds”:
The scholars differed over whether deliberate murder can be forgiven through repentance. Ibn ʿAbbās and others held that the deliberate murderer has no repentance, while the majority of scholars held that repentance remains available to him. This issue was previously discussed in detail under verse 93 of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.
Regarding the words:
“For those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds”:

١٢٩٢٠ — عن أبي ذر قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((إني لأعلم آخر أهل الجنة دخولًا الجنة، وآخر أهل النار خروجًا منها. رجل يؤتى به يوم القيامة، فيقال: اعرضوا عليه صغار ذنوبه، وارفعوا عنه كبارها.
فتعرض عليه صغار ذنوبه، فيقال: عملت يوم كذا وكذا، كذا وكذا، وعملت يوم كذا وكذا، كذا وكذا؟
فيقول: نعم، لا يستطيع أن ينكر، وهو مشفق من كبار ذنوبه أن تعرض عليه.
فيقال له: فإن لك مكان كل سيئة حسنة.
فيقول: رب، قد عملت أشياء لا أراها هاهنا)).
فلقد رأيت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ضحك حتى بدت نواجذه.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٩٠).

12920 — Abū Dharr narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“I know the last person to enter Paradise and the last person to emerge from the Fire. A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said: ‘Present his minor sins to him, but conceal his major sins.’
His minor sins will be presented, and he will be asked: ‘Did you do such-and-such on such-and-such a day? And did you do such-and-such on another day?’
He will reply, ‘Yes,’ unable to deny them, while fearing that his major sins will also be presented.
It will then be said to him: ‘In place of every evil deed, you will receive a good deed.’
He will say: ‘My Lord, I committed other deeds that I do not see listed here.’”
Abū Dharr said:
“I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laugh until his molar teeth became visible.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (190).

His minor sins will be presented, and he will be asked: ‘Did you do such-and-such on such-and-such a day? And did you do such-and-such on another day?’
He will reply, ‘Yes,’ unable to deny them, while fearing that his major sins will also be presented.
It will then be said to him: ‘In place of every evil deed, you will receive a good deed.’
He will say: ‘My Lord, I committed other deeds that I do not see listed here.’”
Abū Dharr said:
“I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laugh until his molar teeth became visible.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (190).

١٢٩٢١ — عن أبي طويل شطب الممدود أنه أتى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال: أرأيت رجلًا عمل الذنوب كلها، فلم يترك منها شيئًا، وهو في ذلك لم يترك حاجة ولا داجة إلا أتاها، فهل له من توبة؟
قال:
((فهل أسلمت؟)).
قال: أما أنا فأشهد أن لا إله إلا اللّٰه وحده لا شريك له، وأنك رسول اللّٰه.
قال:
((نعم، تفعل الخيرات، وتترك السيئات، فيجعلهن اللّٰه لك خيرات كلهن)).
قال: وغدراتي وفجراتي؟
قال:
((نعم)).
فقال: اللّٰه أكبر. فما زال يكبر حتى توارى.
صحيح: رواه البزار في كشف الأستار (٣٢٤٤)، والطبراني في الكبير (٧/٣٧٥-٣٧٦)، واللفظ للطبراني.

12921 — Abū Ṭawīl Shaṭab al-Mamdūd came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked:
“What do you say about a man who committed every kind of sin and left none of them undone? He did not leave any minor or major desire without committing it. Is repentance available to him?”
The Prophet ﷺ asked:
“Have you accepted Islam?”
He replied:
“As for me, I testify that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner, and that you are the Messenger of Allah.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Yes. Perform good deeds and abandon evil deeds, and Allah will transform all of them into good deeds for you.”
The man asked:
“Even my acts of betrayal and immorality?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
The man exclaimed:
“Allah is the Greatest!”
He continued proclaiming Allah’s greatness until he disappeared from sight.
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (3244) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (7/375–376). The wording is that of al-Ṭabarānī.

١٢٩٢٢ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((ليتمنين أقوام لو أكثروا من السيئات)).
قالوا: بم يا رسول اللّٰه؟

حسن: رواه الحاكم (٤/٦٣).

12922 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Some people will wish that they had committed even more evil deeds.”
They asked:
“Why, O Messenger of Allah?”
He replied:
“They are those whose evil deeds Allah transformed into good deeds.”
Good: Narrated by al-Ḥākim (4/63).

١٢٩٢٤ — عن أبي بكرة قال: قال النبي ﷺ:
((ألا أنبئكم بأكبر الكبائر؟)).
ثلاثًا.
قال:
((الإشراك باللّٰه، وعقوق الوالدين، وشهادة الزور، أو قول الزور)).
وكان رسول اللّٰه ﷺ متكئًا فجلس، فما زال يكررها حتى قلنا: ليته سكت.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٦٥٤)، ومسلم (٨٧: ١٤٣)، واللفظ لمسلم.

12924 — Abū Bakrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ asked three times:
“Shall I inform you of the gravest major sins?”
He then said:
“Associating partners with Allah, disobedience toward one’s parents, and false testimony—or false speech.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been reclining, but he sat upright and continued repeating it until we thought:
“If only he would stop.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2654) and Muslim (87:143). The wording is that of Muslim.

arabic_source:
١٢٩٢٥ — عن جبير بن نفير قال: جلسنا إلى المقداد بن الأسود يومًا، فمر به رجل فقال: طوبى لهاتين العينين اللتين رأتا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، واللّٰه لوددنا أنا رأينا ما رأيت، وشهدنا ما شهدت.
فاستغضب، فجعلت أعجب، ما قال إلا خيرًا.
ثم أقبل إليه فقال: ما يحمل الرجل على أن يتمنى محضرًا غيبه اللّٰه عنه؟ لا يدري لو شهده كيف كان يكون فيه.
واللّٰه لقد حضر رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أقوام كبهم اللّٰه على مناخرهم في جهنم، لم يجيبوه ولم يصدقوه.
أولا تحمدون اللّٰه إذ أخرجكم لا تعرفون إلا ربكم، مصدقين لما جاء به نبيكم، وقد كفيتم البلاء بغيركم؟
واللّٰه لقد بعث اللّٰه النبي ﷺ على أشد حال بعث عليها فيه نبي من الأنبياء، في فترة وجاهلية، ما يرون أن دينًا أفضل من عبادة الأوثان.
فجاء بفرقان فرق به بين الحق والباطل، وفرق بين الوالد وولده، حتى إن كان الرجل ليرى والده أو ولده أو أخاه كافرًا، وقد فتح اللّٰه قفل قلبه للإيمان، يعلم أنه إن هلك دخل النار، فلا تقر عينه وهو يعلم أن حبيبه في النار.
وإنها للتي قال اللّٰه عز وجل: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ﴾.
صحيح: رواه أحمد (٢٣٨١٠)، والبخاري في الأدب المفرد (٨٧)، وابن حبان (٦٥٥٢).

12925 — Jubayr ibn Nufayr narrated:
One day, we were sitting with al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad when a man passed by and said:
“Blessed are these two eyes that saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. By Allah, we wish that we had seen what you saw and witnessed what you witnessed.”
Al-Miqdād became angry, which surprised me because the man had apparently said nothing but good.
Al-Miqdād then turned toward him and said:
“What causes a man to wish that he had been present at an event from which Allah kept him absent? He does not know how he would have behaved had he witnessed it.
By Allah, many people were present during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whom Allah cast face-first into Hell because they neither responded to him nor believed him.
Do you not praise Allah for bringing you forth knowing no lord except your Lord, affirming what your Prophet brought, while sparing you the trial by means of others?
By Allah, Allah sent the Prophet ﷺ during the most difficult circumstances in which any prophet had ever been sent: during a period without revelation and an age of ignorance in which the people believed that no religion was better than the worship of idols.
He came with a criterion that separated truth from falsehood and even separated a father from his son. A man might see his father, son, or brother as a disbeliever after Allah had opened the lock upon his own heart to faith. He knew that if his relative died in that state, he would enter the Fire. Therefore, his eyes could not be comforted while he knew that his beloved relative would be in the Fire.
This is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, referred to when He said:
‘Those who say: Our Lord, grant us comfort of the eyes in our spouses and descendants.’”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (23810), al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (87), and Ibn Ḥibbān (6552).

١٢٩٢٥ — عن جبير بن نفير قال: جلسنا إلى المقداد بن الأسود يومًا، فمر به رجل فقال: طوبى لهاتين العينين اللتين رأتا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، واللّٰه لوددنا أنا رأينا ما رأيت، وشهدنا ما شهدت.
فاستغضب، فجعلت أعجب، ما قال إلا خيرًا.
ثم أقبل إليه فقال: ما يحمل الرجل على أن يتمنى محضرًا غيبه اللّٰه عنه؟ لا يدري لو شهده كيف كان يكون فيه.
واللّٰه لقد حضر رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أقوام كبهم اللّٰه على مناخرهم في جهنم، لم يجيبوه ولم يصدقوه.
أولا تحمدون اللّٰه إذ أخرجكم لا تعرفون إلا ربكم، مصدقين لما جاء به نبيكم، وقد كفيتم البلاء بغيركم؟

12926 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd said:
“Five signs have already occurred: the smoke, the moon, the Romans, the mighty seizure, and the inevitable punishment referred to in the words:
‘It will soon become inevitable.’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4767) and Muslim (2798:41).

١٢٩٢٧ — عن ابن عباس أن النبي ﷺ لما قدم المدينة وجدهم يصومون يومًا، يعني عاشوراء، فقالوا: هذا يوم عظيم، وهو يوم نجى اللّٰه فيه موسى، وأغرق آل فرعون، فصام موسى شكرًا للّٰه.
فقال:
((أنا أولى بموسى منهم)).
فصامه، وأمر بصيامه.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٣٩٧)، واللفظ له، ومسلم (١١٣٠: ١٢٧).

12927 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
When the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Madinah, he found the Jews fasting on a particular day, meaning the Day of ʿĀshūrāʾ.
They said:
“This is a tremendous day. It is the day upon which Allah saved Moses and drowned Pharaoh’s people. Moses therefore fasted on it in gratitude to Allah.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“I have a greater right to Moses than they do.”
He fasted that day and commanded that it be fasted.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3397), whose wording is given here, and Muslim (1130:127).

١٢٩٢٨ — عن رفاعة الزرقي قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يوم أحد في دعاء طويل:
((اللهم حبب إلينا الإيمان، وزينه في قلوبنا، وكره إلينا الكفر والفسوق والعصيان، واجعلنا من الراشدين. اللهم توفنا مسلمين، وأحينا مسلمين، وألحقنا بالصالحين، غير خزايا ولا مفتونين)).
الحديث.
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٥٤٩٢)، والبخاري في الأدب المفرد (٦٩٩)، والبزار في كشف الأستار (١٨٠٠)، والحاكم (١/٥٠٦-٥٠٧)، والطبراني في الدعاء (١٠٧٥).

12928 — Rifāʿah al-Zuraqī narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said during a lengthy supplication on the Day of Uḥud:
“O Allah, make faith beloved to us and beautify it within our hearts. Make disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience hateful to us, and make us among those who are rightly guided. O Allah, cause us to die as Muslims, keep us alive as Muslims, and join us with the righteous, neither disgraced nor subjected to temptation.”
The hadith continues.
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (15492), al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (699), al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (1800), al-Ḥākim (1/506–507), and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Duʿāʾ (1075).

١٢٩٢٩ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
((يلقى إبراهيم أباه آزر يوم القيامة، وعلى وجه آزر قترة وغبرة، فيقول له إبراهيم: ألم أقل لك لا تعصني؟
فيقول أبوه: فاليوم لا أعصيك.
فيقول إبراهيم: يا رب، إنك وعدتني ألا تخزيني يوم يبعثون، فأي خزي أخزى من أبي الأبعد؟
فيقول اللّٰه تعالى: إني حرمت الجنة على الكافرين.
ثم يقال: يا إبراهيم، ما تحت رجليك؟
فينظر، فإذا هو بذيخ ملتطخ، فيؤخذ بقوائمه، فيلقى في النار)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٣٥٠).

12929 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Abraham will meet his father Āzar on the Day of Resurrection, and Āzar’s face will be covered with darkness and dust. Abraham will say to him, ‘Did I not tell you not to disobey me?’
His father will reply, ‘Today, I will not disobey you.’
Abraham will say, ‘My Lord, You promised me that You would not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected. What disgrace could be greater than the disgrace of my father being kept far from Your mercy?’
Allah, the Exalted, will say, ‘I have forbidden Paradise to the disbelievers.’
It will then be said, ‘Abraham, look beneath your feet.’
He will look and see a bloodstained male hyena. It will be seized by its legs and thrown into the Fire.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3350).

١٢٩٣٠ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((يؤتى بأنعم أهل الدنيا من أهل النار يوم القيامة، فيصبغ في النار صبغة، ثم يقال: يا ابن آدم، هل رأيت خيرًا قط؟ هل مر بك نعيم قط؟
فيقول: لا واللّٰه يا رب.
ويؤتى بأشد الناس بؤسًا في الدنيا من أهل الجنة، فيصبغ صبغة في الجنة، فيقال له: يا ابن آدم، هل رأيت بؤسًا قط؟ هل مر بك شدة قط؟
فيقول: لا واللّٰه يا رب، ما مر بي بؤس قط، ولا رأيت شدة قط)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٨٠٧).

12930 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The person who enjoyed the most luxurious life in this world among the people of the Fire will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and dipped into the Fire once. It will then be said to him, ‘Son of Adam, did you ever experience anything good? Did you ever enjoy any comfort?’
He will reply, ‘No, by Allah, my Lord.’
The person who endured the greatest misery in this world among the people of Paradise will then be brought and dipped into Paradise once. It will be said to him, ‘Son of Adam, did you ever experience any misery? Did you ever endure any hardship?’
He will reply, ‘No, by Allah, my Lord. I never experienced any misery, nor did I ever see any hardship.’”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2807).

١٢٩٣١ — عن ابن عباس قال: انطلق النبي ﷺ في طائفة من أصحابه عامدين إلى سوق عكاظ، وقد حيل بين الشياطين وبين خبر السماء، وأرسلت عليهم الشهب.
فرجعت الشياطين إلى قومهم، فقالوا: ما لكم؟
فقالوا: حيل بيننا وبين خبر السماء، وأرسلت علينا الشهب.
قالوا: ما حال بينكم وبين خبر السماء إلا شيء حدث، فاضربوا مشارق الأرض ومغاربها، فانظروا ما هذا الذي حال بينكم وبين خبر السماء.
فانصرف أولئك الذين توجهوا نحو تهامة إلى النبي ﷺ، وهو بنخلة عامدين إلى سوق عكاظ، وهو يصلي بأصحابه صلاة الفجر.
فلما سمعوا القرآن استمعوا له، فقالوا: هذا واللّٰه الذي حال بينكم وبين خبر السماء.
فهنالك حين رجعوا إلى قومهم، وقالوا: ﴿إِنَّا سَمِعْنَا قُرْآنًا عَجَبًا ۝ يَهْدِي إِلَى الرُّشْدِ فَآمَنَّا بِهِ وَلَنْ نُشْرِكَ بِرَبِّنَا أَحَدًا﴾ [الجن: ١-٢].
فأنزل اللّٰه على نبيه ﷺ: ﴿قُلْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهُ اسْتَمَعَ نَفَرٌ مِنَ الْجِنِّ﴾، وإنما أوحي إليه قول الجن.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧٧٣)، ومسلم (٤٤٩).

12931 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ set out with a group of his Companions, intending to travel to the market of ʿUkāẓ. At that time, the devils had been prevented from receiving news from heaven, and flaming missiles were sent against them.
The devils returned to their people, who asked:
“What has happened to you?”
They replied:
“We have been prevented from receiving news from heaven, and flaming missiles have been sent against us.”
Their people said:
“Nothing could have prevented you from the news of heaven except some new event. Travel throughout the eastern and western regions of the earth and discover what has prevented you from receiving the news of heaven.”
Those who traveled toward Tihāmah came upon the Prophet ﷺ while he was at Nakhlah on his way to the market of ʿUkāẓ, leading his Companions in the dawn prayer.
When they heard the Qur’an, they listened attentively and said:
“By Allah, this is what has prevented you from receiving news from heaven.”
When they returned to their people, they said:
“We have heard a wondrous Qur’an. It guides to sound judgment, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord.”
 [Sūrat al-Jinn 72:1–2]
Allah then revealed to His Prophet ﷺ:
“Say: It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened.”
The Prophet ﷺ was informed through revelation of what the jinn had said.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (773) and Muslim (449).

فلما سمعوا القرآن استمعوا له، فقالوا: هذا واللّٰه الذي حال بينكم وبين خبر السماء.
فهنالك حين رجعوا إلى قومهم، وقالوا: ﴿إِنَّا سَمِعْنَا قُرْآنًا عَجَبًا ۝ يَهْدِي إِلَى الرُّشْدِ فَآمَنَّا بِهِ وَلَنْ نُشْرِكَ بِرَبِّنَا أَحَدًا﴾ [الجن: ١-٢].
فأنزل اللّٰه على نبيه ﷺ: ﴿قُلْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهُ اسْتَمَعَ نَفَرٌ مِنَ الْجِنِّ﴾، وإنما أوحي إليه قول الجن.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧٧٣)، ومسلم (٤٤٩).
12931 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ set out with a group of his Companions, intending to travel to the market of ʿUkāẓ. At that time, the devils had been prevented from receiving news from heaven, and flaming missiles were sent against them.
The devils returned to their people, who asked:
“What has happened to you?”
They replied:
“We have been prevented from receiving news from heaven, and flaming missiles have been sent against us.”
Their people said:
“Nothing could have prevented you from the news of heaven except some new event. Travel throughout the eastern and western regions of the earth and discover what has prevented you from receiving the news of heaven.”
Those who traveled toward Tihāmah came upon the Prophet ﷺ while he was at Nakhlah on his way to the market of ʿUkāẓ, leading his Companions in the dawn prayer.
When they heard the Qur’an, they listened attentively and said:
“By Allah, this is what has prevented you from receiving news from heaven.”
When they returned to their people, they said:
“We have heard a wondrous Qur’an. It guides to sound judgment, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord.”
 [Sūrat al-Jinn 72:1–2]
Allah then revealed to His Prophet ﷺ:
“Say: It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened.”
The Prophet ﷺ was informed through revelation of what the jinn had said.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (773) and Muslim (449).

12932 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
The jinn used to ascend toward heaven to listen to revelation. Whenever they heard a single true statement, they would add nine falsehoods to it. The original statement would be true, while everything they added would be false.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent, they were prevented from occupying their former listening posts. They mentioned this to Iblīs. Before that time, stars had not been used to drive them away.
Iblīs said:
“This can only be because of some event that has occurred upon the earth.”
He dispatched his forces, and they found the Messenger of Allah ﷺ standing in prayer between two mountains—according to the narrator, in Makkah.
They returned and informed Iblīs, who said:
“This is the event that has occurred upon the earth.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (1/274), al-Tirmidhī (3324), whose wording is given here, and al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (11626).

١٢٩٣٣ — عن ابن عباس قال: لما نزلت: ﴿وَأَنْذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ الْأَقْرَبِينَ﴾، صعد النبي ﷺ على الصفا، فجعل ينادي:
((يا بني فهر، يا بني عدي)).
لبطون قريش، حتى اجتمعوا.
فجعل الرجل إذا لم يستطع أن يخرج أرسل رسولًا لينظر ما هو. فجاء أبو لهب وقريش.
فقال:
((أرأيتم لو أخبرتكم أن خيلًا بالوادي تريد أن تغير عليكم، أكنتم مصدقي؟)).
قالوا: نعم، ما جربنا عليك إلا صدقًا.
قال:
((فإني نذير لكم بين يدي عذاب شديد)).
فقال أبو لهب: تبًّا لك سائر اليوم، ألهذا جمعتنا؟
فنزلت: ﴿تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ ۝ مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُ وَمَا كَسَبَ﴾ [المسد: ١-٢].
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٧٧٠)، ومسلم (٢٠٨)، واللفظ للبخاري.

12933 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
When the verse:
“Warn your closest relatives”
was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ climbed Mount al-Ṣafā and began calling out:
“Children of Fihr! Children of ʿAdī!”
He called the various clans of Quraysh until they gathered.
Anyone unable to attend personally sent a representative to learn what was happening. Abū Lahab and the people of Quraysh arrived.
The Prophet ﷺ asked:
“Tell me: if I informed you that cavalry in the valley was preparing to attack you, would you believe me?”
They replied:
“Yes. We have never experienced anything from you except truthfulness.”
He said:
“Then I am a warner to you before the coming of a severe punishment.”
Abū Lahab said:
“May you perish for the rest of this day! Is this why you gathered us?”
The following verses were revealed:
“May the hands of Abū Lahab perish, and may he perish. Neither his wealth nor what he earned benefited him.”
 [Sūrat al-Masad 111:1–2]
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4770) and Muslim (208). The wording is that of al-Bukhārī.

“May the hands of Abū Lahab perish, and may he perish. Neither his wealth nor what he earned benefited him.”

١٢٩٣٥ — عن أبي هريرة قال: لما أنزلت هذه الآية: ﴿وَأَنْذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ الْأَقْرَبِينَ﴾، دعا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قريشًا، فاجتمعوا، فعم وخص، فقال:
((يا بني كعب بن لؤي، أنقذوا أنفسكم من النار.
يا بني مرة بن كعب، أنقذوا أنفسكم من النار.
يا بني عبد شمس، أنقذوا أنفسكم من النار.
يا بني عبد مناف، أنقذوا أنفسكم من النار.
يا بني هاشم، أنقذوا أنفسكم من النار.
يا بني عبد المطلب، أنقذوا أنفسكم من النار.
يا فاطمة، أنقذي نفسك من النار، فإني لا أملك لكم من اللّٰه شيئًا، غير أن لكم رحمًا سأبلها ببلالها)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٠٤).

12935 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
When the verse:
“Warn your closest relatives”
was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned Quraysh. They gathered, and he addressed them both generally and specifically, saying:
“Children of Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy, save yourselves from the Fire.
Children of Murrah ibn Kaʿb, save yourselves from the Fire.
Children of ʿAbd Shams, save yourselves from the Fire.
Children of ʿAbd Manāf, save yourselves from the Fire.
Children of Hāshim, save yourselves from the Fire.
Children of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, save yourselves from the Fire.
Fāṭimah, save yourself from the Fire. I possess no power to protect you from Allah, except that you have ties of kinship with me which I will properly maintain.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (204).

١٢٩٣٧ — عن قبيصة بن المخارق وزهير بن عمرو قالا: لما نزلت: ﴿وَأَنْذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ الْأَقْرَبِينَ﴾، انطلق نبي اللّٰه ﷺ إلى رضمة من جبل، فعلا أعلاها حجرًا، ثم نادى:
((يا بني عبد منافاه، إني نذير. إنما مثلي ومثلكم كمثل رجل رأى العدو، فانطلق يربأ أهله، فخشي أن يسبقوه، فجعل يهتف: يا صباحاه)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٠٧).

12937 — Qabīṣah ibn Mukhāriq and Zuhayr ibn ʿAmr narrated:
When the verse:
“Warn your closest relatives”
was revealed, the Prophet of Allah ﷺ went to a mound upon a mountain, climbed its highest rock, and called out:
“Children of ʿAbd Manāf! I am a warner. My example in relation to you is like that of a man who sees an approaching enemy and rushes to warn his family. Fearing that the enemy will reach them before he does, he cries out: ‘O people, awake! An attack is upon you!’”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (207).

١٢٩٣٧ — عن قبيصة بن المخارق وزهير بن عمرو قالا: لما نزلت: ﴿وَأَنْذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ الْأَقْرَبِينَ﴾، انطلق نبي اللّٰه ﷺ إلى رضمة من جبل، فعلا أعلاها حجرًا، ثم نادى:
((يا بني عبد منافاه، إني نذير. إنما مثلي ومثلكم كمثل رجل رأى العدو، فانطلق يربأ أهله، فخشي أن يسبقوه، فجعل يهتف: يا صباحاه)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٠٧).
12937 — Qabīṣah ibn Mukhāriq and Zuhayr ibn ʿAmr narrated:
When the verse:
“Warn your closest relatives”
was revealed, the Prophet of Allah ﷺ went to a mound upon a mountain, climbed its highest rock, and called out:
“Children of ʿAbd Manāf! I am a warner. My example in relation to you is like that of a man who sees an approaching enemy and rushes to warn his family. Fearing that the enemy will reach them before he does, he cries out: ‘O people, awake! An attack is upon you!’”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (207).

arabic_source:
١٢٩٣٨ — عن عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ قالت: سأل أناس النبي ﷺ عن الكهان، فقال:
((إنهم ليسوا بشيء)).
فقالوا: يا رسول اللّٰه، فإنهم يحدثون بالشيء يكون حقًّا.
قال: فقال النبي ﷺ:
((تلك الكلمة من الحق يخطفها الجني، فيقرقرها في أذن وليه كقرقرة الدجاجة، فيخلطون فيها أكثر من مائة كذبة)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧٥٦١)، ومسلم (٢٢٢٨).

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (7561) and Muslim (2228).

١٢٩٤٠ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: بينا نحن نسير مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بالعرج، إذ عرض شاعر ينشد، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((خذوا الشيطان، أو أمسكوا الشيطان؛ لأن يمتلئ جوف رجل قيحًا خير له من أن يمتلئ شعرًا)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٢٥٩).
هذا الحديث خاص بهذا الرجل الذي لعله كان ينشد في الباطل والفواحش، ويحمل على هذا كل من يفعل ذلك.
لأن قوله تعالى بعد ذلك: ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾ يدل على ذلك، فهو استثناء منه، ويدل عليه قول ابن عباس الآتي:

12940 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrated:
While we were traveling with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-ʿArj, a poet appeared and began reciting poetry.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Seize the devil,”
or:
“Stop the devil. For a man’s body cavity to be filled with pus is better for him than for it to be filled with poetry.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2259).
This hadith applies specifically to this man, who may have been reciting poetry containing falsehood or indecency. The same ruling applies to anyone who uses poetry in this manner.
This is indicated by the words of Allah that follow:
“Except those who believe and perform righteous deeds.”
This is an exception from the general condemnation, as also indicated by the following statement of Ibn ʿAbbās:

arabic_source:
١٢٩٤١ — عن ابن عباس قال: ﴿وَالشُّعَرَاءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ الْغَاوُونَ﴾، فنسخ من ذلك واستثنى فقال: ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا﴾.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٥٠١٦)، والبخاري في الأدب المفرد (٨٧١).
ويدل على قول ابن عباس أن النبي ﷺ أجاز لشعراء الإسلام مدح النبي ﷺ، والدعوة إلى الإسلام، والدفاع عنه.
وقوله: «فنسخ من ذلك»، المراد به التخصيص.
ويفهم من قول ابن عباس أن هذه الآية مدنية، وقد صح أن سورة الشعراء نزلت في مكة.
فقال النحاس في الناسخ والمنسوخ: إن سورة الشعراء مكية إلا هذه الآيات، فإنها نزلت بالمدينة.
ويؤيده ما رواه ابن أبي شيبة في المصنف (٢٦٥٧٤)، عن يحيى بن واضح، عن محمد بن إسحاق، عن يزيد بن عبد اللّٰه بن قسيط، عن أبي الحسن البراد، قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية: ﴿وَالشُّعَرَاءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ الْغَاوُونَ﴾، جاء عبد اللّٰه بن رواحة وكعب بن مالك وحسان بن ثابت إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وهم يبكون، فقالوا: يا رسول اللّٰه، أنزل اللّٰه هذه الآية، وهو يعلم أنا شعراء.
فقال:
((اقرؤوا ما بعدها: ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾ أنتم، ﴿وَانْتَصَرُوا﴾ أنتم)).
وهؤلاء الشعراء من أنصار المدينة، إلا أن إسناده مرسل؛ فإني لم أقف على من ذكر أبا الحسن البراد، وهو مولى تميم الداري، من الصحابة.

12941 — Ibn ʿAbbās said concerning the verse:
“The poets are followed by those who are astray”:
Allah then excluded some of them from this ruling, saying:
“Except those who believe, perform righteous deeds, and remember Allah frequently.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5016) and al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (871).
Supporting the statement of Ibn ʿAbbās is the fact that the Prophet ﷺ permitted Muslim poets to praise the Prophet ﷺ, call people to Islam, and defend the religion.
The phrase:
“He abrogated part of it”
means that Allah restricted and qualified the general ruling through the exception.
The statement of Ibn ʿAbbās may suggest that these verses were revealed in Madinah, even though it is authentically established that Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ was revealed in Makkah.
Al-Naḥḥās stated in al-Nāsikh wa-al-Mansūkh that Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ is Makkan except for these verses, which were revealed in Madinah.
This is supported by what Ibn Abī Shaybah narrated in al-Muṣannaf (26574), through Yaḥyā ibn Wāḍiḥ, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qusayṭ, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Barrād:
When the verse:
“The poets are followed by those who are astray”
was revealed, ʿAbdullāh ibn Rawāḥah, Kaʿb ibn Mālik, and Ḥassān ibn Thābit came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ weeping. They said:
“O Messenger of Allah, Allah has revealed this verse while He knows that we are poets.”
He replied:
“Recite what follows it:
‘Except those who believe and perform righteous deeds’—that refers to you.

حسن: رواه أبو داود (٥٠١٦)، والبخاري في الأدب المفرد (٨٧١).

وقوله: «فنسخ من ذلك»، المراد به التخصيص.
ويفهم من قول ابن عباس أن هذه الآية مدنية، وقد صح أن سورة الشعراء نزلت في مكة.
فقال النحاس في الناسخ والمنسوخ: إن سورة الشعراء مكية إلا هذه الآيات، فإنها نزلت بالمدينة.

١٢٩٤٢ — عن كعب بن مالك أنه قال للنبي ﷺ: إن اللّٰه عز وجل قد أنزل في الشعر ما أنزل.
فقال:
((إن المؤمن يجاهد بسيفه ولسانه، والذي نفسي بيده، لكأن ما ترمونهم به نضح النبل)).
صحيح: رواه أحمد (٢٧١٧٤)، والطبراني في الكبير (١٩/٧٥)، وصححه ابن حبان (٥٧٨٦).

12942 — Kaʿb ibn Mālik said to the Prophet ﷺ:
“Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has revealed concerning poetry what He has revealed.”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“The believer strives with both his sword and his tongue. By the One in Whose hand is my soul, the poetry with which you attack them is like the showering of arrows.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (27174), al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (19/75), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (5786).

12945 — ʿĀʾishah, Mother of the Believers, narrated:
After the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, the wives of the Prophet ﷺ wished to send ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān to Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq to ask him for their inheritance from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

متفق عليه: رواه مالك في الكلام والغيبة والتقى (٢٧)، والبخاري (٦٧٣٠)، ومسلم (١٧٥٨).
12945 — ʿĀʾishah, Mother of the Believers, narrated:
After the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, the wives of the Prophet ﷺ wished to send ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān to Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq to ask him for their inheritance from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
ʿĀʾishah said to them:
“Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not say:
‘We prophets are not inherited from. Whatever we leave behind is charity’?”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Mālik in al-Kalām wa-al-Ghībah wa-al-Tuqā (27), al-Bukhārī (6730), and Muslim (1758).

١٢٩٤٦ — عن أبي ذر، عن النبي ﷺ فيما روى عن اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى أنه قال:
((يا عبادي، إني حرمت الظلم على نفسي، وجعلته بينكم محرمًا، فلا تظالموا.
يا عبادي، كلكم ضال إلا من هديته، فاستهدوني أهدكم.
يا عبادي، كلكم جائع إلا من أطعمته، فاستطعموني أطعمكم.
يا عبادي، كلكم عار إلا من كسوته، فاستكسوني أكسكم.
يا عبادي، إنكم تخطئون بالليل والنهار، وأنا أغفر الذنوب جميعًا، فاستغفروني أغفر لكم.
يا عبادي، إنكم لن تبلغوا ضري فتضروني، ولن تبلغوا نفعي فتنفعوني.
يا عبادي، لو أن أولكم وآخركم، وإنسكم وجنكم، كانوا على أتقى قلب رجل واحد منكم، ما زاد ذلك في ملكي شيئًا.
يا عبادي، لو أن أولكم وآخركم، وإنسكم وجنكم، كانوا على أفجر قلب رجل واحد، ما نقص ذلك من ملكي شيئًا.
يا عبادي، لو أن أولكم وآخركم، وإنسكم وجنكم، قاموا في صعيد واحد فسألوني، فأعطيت كل إنسان مسألته، ما نقص ذلك مما عندي إلا كما ينقص المخيط إذا أدخل البحر.
يا عبادي، إنما هي أعمالكم أحصيها لكم، ثم أوفيكم إياها، فمن وجد خيرًا فليحمد اللّٰه، ومن وجد غير ذلك فلا يلومن إلا نفسه)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٥٧٧).

12946 — Abū Dharr narrated that the Prophet ﷺ related from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, that He said:
“My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and have made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another.
My servants, all of you are astray except those whom I guide, so ask Me for guidance and I will guide you.
My servants, all of you are hungry except those whom I feed, so ask Me for food and I will feed you.
My servants, all of you are unclothed except those whom I clothe, so ask Me for clothing and I will clothe you.
My servants, you commit sins by night and day, and I forgive all sins, so seek My forgiveness and I will forgive you.
My servants, you will never attain the ability to harm Me, nor will you attain the ability to benefit Me.
My servants, if the first and last of you, the humans and jinn among you, were all as pious as the most pious heart of any one man among you, that would not increase My dominion in the slightest.
My servants, if the first and last of you, the humans and jinn among you, were all as wicked as the most wicked heart of any one man, that would not decrease My dominion in the slightest.
My servants, if the first and last of you, the humans and jinn among you, all stood together in one place and asked Me, and I gave every person what he requested, that would decrease what I possess no more than a needle decreases the sea when dipped into it.
My servants, these are only your deeds, which I record for you and then repay you for in full. Whoever finds good should praise Allah, and whoever finds something else should blame no one but himself.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2577).

١٢٩٤٧ — عن رجل من بَلْهُجَيْم قال: قلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، إلام تدعو؟ قال:
((أدعو إلى اللّٰه وحده، الذي إن مسك ضر فدعوته كشف عنك، والذي إن ضللت بأرض قفر دعوته رد عليك، والذي إن أصابتك سنة فدعوته أنبت عليك)).
قال: قلت: فأوصني. قال:
((لا تسبن أحدًا، ولا تزهدن في المعروف، ولو أن تلقى أخاك وأنت منبسط إليه وجهك، ولو أن تفرغ من دلوك في إناء مستسق، وائتزر إلى نصف الساق، فإن أبيت فإلى الكعبين، وإياك وإسبال الإزار، فإن إسبال الإزار من المخيلة، وإن اللّٰه لا يحب المخيلة)).
صحيح: رواه أحمد (٢٠٦٣٦). والرجل المبهم من الصحابة هو جابر بن سليم، كما في الإسناد الذي قبله (٢٠٦٣٥).

12947 — A man from Balhujaym narrated:
I asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, to what are you calling people?”
He replied:
“I call them to Allah alone: the One who, if harm touches you and you call upon Him, removes it from you; the One who, if you become lost in a barren land and call upon Him, returns you safely; and the One who, if a year of drought afflicts you and you call upon Him, causes vegetation to grow for you.”
I said:
“Then advise me.”
He replied:
“Never insult anyone. Do not regard any good deed as insignificant, even if it is meeting your brother with a cheerful face or pouring water from your bucket into the vessel of someone seeking water. Wear your lower garment to the middle of your shin; if you refuse, then down to your ankles. Beware of letting the lower garment hang beneath the ankles, for doing so is an expression of pride, and Allah does not love pride.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (20636). The unnamed Companion was Jābir ibn Sulaym, as identified in the preceding chain (20635).

١٢٩٤٨ — عن أبي هريرة قال: كان النبي ﷺ بارزًا يومًا للناس، فأتاه رجل فقال: ما الإيمان؟ قال:
((الإيمان أن تؤمن باللّٰه، وملائكته، وكتابه، ولقائه، ورسله، وتؤمن بالبعث الآخر)).
قال: يا رسول اللّٰه، ما الإسلام؟ قال:
((الإسلام أن تعبد اللّٰه ولا تشرك به، وتقيم الصلاة المكتوبة، وتؤدي الزكاة المفروضة، وتصوم رمضان)).
قال: يا رسول اللّٰه، ما الإحسان؟ قال:
((أن تعبد اللّٰه كأنك تراه، فإنك إن لا تراه فإنه يراك)).
قال: يا رسول اللّٰه، متى الساعة؟ قال:
((ما المسؤول عنها بأعلم من السائل، ولكن سأحدثك عن أشراطها: إذا ولدت الأمة ربها فذاك من أشراطها، وإذا كانت العراة الحفاة رؤوس الناس فذاك من أشراطها، وإذا تطاول رعاء الإبل البهم في البنيان فذاك من أشراطها، في خمس لا يعلمهن إلا اللّٰه)).
ثم تلا: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ وَيُنَزِّلُ الْغَيْثَ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِي الْأَرْحَامِ وَمَا تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ مَاذَا تَكْسِبُ غَدًا وَمَا تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ بِأَيِّ أَرْضٍ تَمُوتُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ﴾ [لقمان: ٣٤].
ثم أدبر الرجل، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((ردوا علي الرجل)).
فأخذوا ليردوه، فلم يروا شيئًا، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((هذا جبريل، جاء ليعلم الناس دينهم)).

12948 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
One day, the Prophet ﷺ was sitting publicly among the people when a man came and asked:
“What is faith?”
He replied:
“Faith is that you believe in Allah, His angels, His Book, meeting Him, His messengers, and the final resurrection.”
The man asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, what is Islam?”
He replied:
“Islam is that you worship Allah without associating anything with Him, establish the prescribed prayer, pay the obligatory zakāh, and fast Ramadan.”
He asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, what is excellence?”
He replied:
“It is to worship Allah as though you see Him, for although you do not see Him, He certainly sees you.”
He asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, when is the Hour?”
He replied:
“The one being questioned knows no more about it than the questioner. However, I will tell you some of its signs: when a slave woman gives birth to her master, that is among its signs; when the barefoot and unclothed become the leaders of the people, that is among its signs; and when the shepherds of dark-colored camels compete in constructing tall buildings, that is among its signs. It is among five matters known only to Allah.”
He then recited:
“Indeed, Allah alone possesses knowledge of the Hour, sends down the rain, and knows what is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.”
 [Sūrat Luqmān 31:34]
The man then departed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Bring the man back to me.”
They went to bring him back but could not find anyone.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“That was Gabriel. He came to teach the people their religion.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4777) and Muslim (9). The wording is that of Muslim.

١٢٩٤٩ — عن أبي طلحة أن نبي اللّٰه ﷺ أمر يوم بدر بأربعة وعشرين رجلًا من صناديد قريش، فقذفوا في طوي من أطواء بدر خبيث مخبث.
وكان إذا ظهر على قوم أقام بالعرصة ثلاث ليال.
فلما كان ببدر اليوم الثالث، أمر براحلته فشد عليها رحلها، ثم مشى، واتبعه أصحابه، وقالوا: ما نرى ينطلق إلا لبعض حاجته.
حتى قام على شفة الركي، فجعل يناديهم بأسمائهم وأسماء آبائهم:
((يا فلان بن فلان، ويا فلان بن فلان، أيسركم أنكم أطعتم اللّٰه ورسوله؟ فإنا قد وجدنا ما وعدنا ربنا حقًّا، فهل وجدتم ما وعد ربكم حقًّا؟)).
قال: فقال عمر: يا رسول اللّٰه، ما تكلم من أجساد لا أرواح لها؟
فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((والذي نفس محمد بيده، ما أنتم بأسمع لما أقول منهم)).
قال قتادة: أحياهم اللّٰه حتى أسمعهم قوله توبيخًا وتصغيرًا ونقمة وحسرة وندمًا.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٩٧٦)، ومسلم (٢٨٧٥: ٧٨)، والسياق للبخاري.

12949 — Abū Ṭalḥah narrated:
On the Day of Badr, the Prophet of Allah ﷺ ordered that twenty-four leading men of Quraysh be thrown into one of the filthy, abandoned wells of Badr.
Whenever he gained victory over a people, he would remain at the battlefield for three nights.
On the third day at Badr, he ordered that his riding animal be prepared and its saddle secured. He then set out on foot, and his Companions followed him, saying:
“We think he is only going out for some need.”
He reached the edge of the well and began calling the dead by their names and the names of their fathers:
“So-and-so son of so-and-so! So-and-so son of so-and-so! Would it have pleased you if you had obeyed Allah and His Messenger? We have certainly found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true?”
ʿUmar asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, how can you speak to bodies that possess no souls?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied:
“By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, you do not hear what I am saying any better than they do.”
Qatādah said:
“Allah brought them to life so that He caused them to hear his words as rebuke, humiliation, vengeance, grief, and regret.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3976) and Muslim (2875:78). The wording is that of al-Bukhārī.

((يا فلان بن فلان، ويا فلان بن فلان، أيسركم أنكم أطعتم اللّٰه ورسوله؟ فإنا قد وجدنا ما وعدنا ربنا حقًّا، فهل وجدتم ما وعد ربكم حقًّا؟)).
قال: فقال عمر: يا رسول اللّٰه، ما تكلم من أجساد لا أرواح لها؟
فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((والذي نفس محمد بيده، ما أنتم بأسمع لما أقول منهم)).
قال قتادة: أحياهم اللّٰه حتى أسمعهم قوله توبيخًا وتصغيرًا ونقمة وحسرة وندمًا.

12949 — Abū Ṭalḥah narrated:
On the Day of Badr, the Prophet of Allah ﷺ ordered that twenty-four leading men of Quraysh be thrown into one of the filthy, abandoned wells of Badr.
Whenever he gained victory over a people, he would remain at the battlefield for three nights.
On the third day at Badr, he ordered that his riding animal be prepared and its saddle secured. He then set out on foot, and his Companions followed him, saying:
“We think he is only going out for some need.”
He reached the edge of the well and began calling the dead by their names and the names of their fathers:
“So-and-so son of so-and-so! So-and-so son of so-and-so! Would it have pleased you if you had obeyed Allah and His Messenger? We have certainly found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true?”
ʿUmar asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, how can you speak to bodies that possess no souls?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied:
“By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, you do not hear what I am saying any better than they do.”
Qatādah said:
“Allah brought them to life so that He caused them to hear his words as rebuke, humiliation, vengeance, grief, and regret.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3976) and Muslim (2875:78). The wording is that of al-Bukhārī.

١٢٩٥٠ — عن أنس بن مالك أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ترك قتلى بدر ثلاثًا، ثم أتاهم، فقام عليهم فناداهم، فقال:
((يا أبا جهل بن هشام، يا أمية بن خلف، يا عتبة بن ربيعة، يا شيبة بن ربيعة، أليس قد وجدتم ما وعد ربكم حقًّا؟ فإني قد وجدت ما وعدني ربي حقًّا)).
فسمع عمر قول النبي ﷺ فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، كيف يسمعوا، وأنى يجيبوا، وقد جيفوا؟
قال:
((والذي نفسي بيده، ما أنتم بأسمع لما أقول منهم، ولكنهم لا يقدرون أن يجيبوا)).
ثم أمر بهم، فسحبوا، فألقوا في قليب بدر.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٨٧٤: ٧٧).
قوله: «فألقوا في قليب بدر» لم يكن أمية بن خلف في القليب؛ لأنه كان ضخمًا، فانتفخ وتقطعت أوصاله بعد الجر، فألقوا عليه من الحجارة والتراب ما غيبه، لكنه كان قريبًا من القليب، فنودي فيمن نودي.

english_source:
12950 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ left the dead of Badr for three days. He then came to them, stood over them, and called out:
“Abū Jahl ibn Hishām! Umayyah ibn Khalaf! ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah! Shaybah ibn Rabīʿah! Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true? I have certainly found what my Lord promised me to be true.”
ʿUmar heard the words of the Prophet ﷺ and asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, how can they hear, and how could they answer, when their bodies have decomposed?”
He replied:
“By the One in Whose hand is my soul, you do not hear what I am saying any better than they do, but they are unable to respond.”
He then ordered that their bodies be dragged away and thrown into the well of Badr.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2874:77).
Regarding the words:
“They were thrown into the well of Badr”:
Umayyah ibn Khalaf was not actually placed inside the well. Because he was very large, his body became swollen and his limbs came apart when they attempted to drag him. They therefore covered him with stones and earth until his body was concealed. However, he was close to the well and was included among those whom the Prophet ﷺ addressed.

١٢٩٥١ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمر قال: وقف النبي ﷺ على قليب بدر فقال:
((هل وجدتم ما وعد ربكم حقًّا؟)).
ثم قال:
((إنهم الآن يسمعون ما أقول)).
فذكر لعائشة، فقالت: إنما قال النبي ﷺ:
((إنهم الآن ليعلمون أن الذي كنت أقول لهم هو الحق)).
ثم قرأت: ﴿إِنَّكَ لَا تُسْمِعُ الْمَوْتَىٰ﴾ [النمل: ٨٠]، حتى قرأت الآية.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٩٨٠)، ومسلم (٩٣٢: ٢٦).

12951 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ stood over the well of Badr and said:
“Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true?”
He then said:
“They are now hearing what I say.”
When this was mentioned to ʿĀʾishah, she said:
“The Prophet ﷺ only said:
‘They now know that what I used to tell them was the truth.’”
She then recited:
“Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear,”
 [Sūrat al-Naml 27:80]
and continued to the end of the verse.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3980) and Muslim (932:26).

١٢٩٥٢ — عن عائشة قالت: أمر رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بقتلى بدر أن يطرحوا في القليب، فطرحوا فيه، إلا ما كان من أمية بن خلف؛ فإنه انتفخ في درعه فملأها، فذهبوا ليحركوه فتزايل، فأقروه، وألقوا عليه ما غيبه من التراب والحجارة.
فلما ألقاهم في القليب وقف عليهم رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال:
((يا أهل القليب، هل وجدتم ما وعدكم ربكم حقًّا؟ فإني قد وجدت ما وعدني ربي حقًّا)).
قالت: فقال له أصحابه: يا رسول اللّٰه، أتكلم قومًا موتى؟
فقال لهم:
((لقد علموا أن ما وعدتهم حق)).
قالت عائشة: والناس يقولون: لقد سمعوا ما قلت لهم، وإنما قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((لقد علموا)).
حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٦٣٦١)، وابن حبان (٧٠٨٨)، والحاكم (٣/٢٢٤).
قال الحاكم: صحيح على شرط مسلم.

١٢٩٥٣ — عن أنس، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
((العبد إذا وضع في قبره، وتولي وذهب أصحابه، حتى إنه ليسمع قرع نعالهم، أتاه ملكان فأقعداه، فيقولان له: ما كنت تقول في هذا الرجل محمد ﷺ؟
فيقول: أشهد أنه عبد اللّٰه ورسوله.
فيقال: انظر إلى مقعدك من النار، أبدلك اللّٰه به مقعدًا من الجنة)).
قال النبي ﷺ:
((فيراهما جميعًا.
وأما الكافر أو المنافق فيقول: لا أدري، كنت أقول ما يقول الناس.
فيقال: لا دريت ولا تليت.
ثم يضرب بمطرقة من حديد ضربة بين أذنيه، فيصيح صيحة يسمعها من يليه إلا الثقلين)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٣٣٨)، ومسلم (٢٨٧٠).
قوله: «يسمعها من يليه إلا الثقلين»، الثقلان هما الإنس والجن، فإنهما لا يسمعان ماذا يفعل بصاحب القبر، وهذا كله يحصل في عالم غير عالمنا.
ومن قال: فيه دلالة على حياة الميت في القبر، فقد خالف الظاهر المحسوس.
فإن الحياة في العالم الآخر، وهو عالم البرزخ، لا نعلم عنه إلا ما أخبرنا اللّٰه تعالى ورسوله ﷺ، ولا نقيس ذلك على عالمنا الدنيوي.

12953 — Anas narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“When a servant is placed in his grave and his companions turn away and leave, he can hear the sound of their sandals. Two angels then come to him, make him sit, and ask: ‘What did you used to say concerning this man, Muḥammad ﷺ?’
He will reply: ‘I testify that he is the servant and Messenger of Allah.’
It will be said to him: ‘Look at the place you would have occupied in the Fire. Allah has replaced it for you with a place in Paradise.’”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“He will see both places.
As for the disbeliever or hypocrite, he will say: ‘I do not know. I merely used to repeat what the people said.’
It will be said to him: ‘You neither knew nor followed those who knew.’
He will then be struck between his ears with an iron hammer and will scream with a cry heard by everything near him except the two weighty species.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1338) and Muslim (2870).
The words:
“It is heard by everything near him except the two weighty species”
refer to humankind and the jinn. They do not hear what happens to the occupant of the grave. All of this occurs in a realm different from our present world.
Whoever claims that this proves that the deceased possesses ordinary worldly life inside the grave has contradicted what is outwardly and physically observable.
Life in the next realm—the realm of al-Barzakh—is known to us only through what Allah, the Exalted, and His Messenger ﷺ have informed us. It must not be measured according to the conditions of our worldly life.

١٢٩٥٤ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((لقنوا موتاكم لا إله إلا اللّٰه)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٩١٧).

12954 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Prompt your dying people to say: ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah.’”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (917).
The word “deceased” here refers to a person whose death is approaching but who is still alive. For further details, see The Book of Funerals.
As for prompting the deceased after death, this has not been authentically established.
What is authentically established is seeking forgiveness for the deceased after burial and supplicating that Allah keep him firm. Abū Dāwūd (3221) narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān:
When the Prophet ﷺ finished burying a deceased person, he would stand beside the grave and say:
“Seek forgiveness for your brother and ask that he be kept firm, for he is now being questioned.”
Its chain of transmission is good.
For further details, see The Book of Funerals, which contains many issues related to this subject.

١٢٩٥٥ — عن حذيفة بن أسيد الغفاري قال: اطلع النبي ﷺ علينا ونحن نتذاكر، فقال:
((ما تذاكرون؟)).
قالوا: نذكر الساعة.
قال:
((إنها لن تقوم حتى تروا قبلها عشر آيات)).
فذكر الدخان، والدجال، والدابة، وطلوع الشمس من مغربها، ونزول عيسى ابن مريم ﷺ، ويأجوج ومأجوج، وثلاثة خسوف: خسف بالمشرق، وخسف بالمغرب، وخسف بجزيرة العرب، وآخر ذلك نار تخرج من اليمن تطرد الناس إلى محشرهم.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٩٠١).

12955 — Ḥudhayfah ibn Usayd al-Ghifārī narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ looked in upon us while we were discussing something and asked:
“What are you discussing?”
They replied:
“We are discussing the Hour.”
He said:
“It will not occur until you see ten signs before it.”
He then mentioned the smoke, the Antichrist, the Beast, the rising of the sun from the west, the descent of Jesus son of Mary ﷺ, Gog and Magog, and three landslides: one in the east, one in the west, and one in the Arabian Peninsula. The last of these signs will be a fire emerging from Yemen that will drive the people toward their place of gathering.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2901).

١٢٩٥٧ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمرو بن العاص قال: جاء أعرابي إلى النبي ﷺ فقال: ما الصور؟ قال:
((قرن ينفخ فيه)).
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٤٧٤٢)، والترمذي (٢٤٣٠، ٣٢٤٤)، وصححه ابن حبان (٧٣١٢)، والحاكم (٢/٤٣٦).
قوله: ﴿فَفَزِعَ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾، الفزع هو الجزع، يحصل هذا للإنسان من الشيء المخيف.
وقوله: ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ﴾، اختلف في هذا الاستثناء، فذهب كثير من أهل العلم إلى أنهم الشهداء؛ وذلك أنهم أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون، وإن كانوا في عداد الموتى عند أهل الدنيا. ورد ذكرهم في حديث أبي هريرة:

english_source:
12957 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ narrated:
A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked:
“What is the Trumpet?”
He replied:
“It is a horn into which one will blow.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4742), al-Tirmidhī (2430, 3244), authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (7312), and narrated by al-Ḥākim (2/436).
The words:
“Those in the heavens and those on the earth will be terrified”
refer to fear and alarm caused by something terrifying.
The scholars differed concerning those excluded by the words:
“Except whomever Allah wills.”
Many scholars held that they are the martyrs, because they are alive with their Lord and receiving provision, even though the people of this world count them among the dead. They are mentioned in the following narration of Abū Hurayrah:

Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4742), al-Tirmidhī (2430, 3244), authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (7312), and narrated by al-Ḥākim (2/436).
The words:
“Those in the heavens and those on the earth will be terrified”
refer to fear and alarm caused by something terrifying.
The scholars differed concerning those excluded by the words:
“Except whomever Allah wills.”
Many scholars held that they are the martyrs, because they are alive with their Lord and receiving provision, even though the people of this world count them among the dead. They are mentioned in the following narration of Abū Hurayrah:

12958 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ asked Gabriel, peace be upon him, concerning the verse:
“The Trumpet will be blown, and all those in the heavens and on the earth will fall unconscious except whomever Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and suddenly they will be standing, looking on.”
 [Sūrat al-Zumar 39:68]
He asked:
“Who are those whom Allah does not will to fall unconscious?”
Gabriel replied:
“They are the martyrs, wearing their swords around the Throne of the Most Compassionate. On the Day of Resurrection, the angels will receive them and carry them toward the place of gathering upon noble mounts made of ruby. Their saddles will be softer than silk, and the length of each stride will extend as far as a man can see.
They will travel through Paradise and, after a lengthy journey, will say: ‘Come, let us go to our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and observe how He judges between His creation.’
My Lord will laugh toward them, and whenever He laughs toward a servant in any place, that servant will not be called to account.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Yaʿlā in al-Maṭālib al-ʿĀliyah (3702).
As for the words in Sūrat al-Zumar:
“The Trumpet will be blown, and all those in the heavens and on the earth will fall unconscious except whomever Allah wills,”
 [Sūrat al-Zumar 39:68]
the falling unconscious refers to the death that follows the initial terror. If the exception refers to a particular person, then it may refer to Moses, peace be upon him.

“The people will fall unconscious on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first to regain consciousness. I will then see Moses holding one of the supports of the Throne. I do not know whether he regained consciousness before me or whether he was spared in compensation for his falling unconscious at Mount Sinai.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3398) and Muslim (2374:162).

١٢٩٦٠ — عن أبي هريرة قال: استب رجلان: رجل من المسلمين ورجل من اليهود.
قال المسلم: والذي اصطفى محمدًا على العالمين.
فقال اليهودي: والذي اصطفى موسى على العالمين.
فرفع المسلم يده عند ذلك، فلطم وجه اليهودي.
فذهب اليهودي إلى النبي ﷺ، فأخبره بما كان من أمره وأمر المسلم.
فدعا النبي ﷺ المسلم، فسأله عن ذلك، فأخبره.
فقال النبي ﷺ:
((لا تخيروني على موسى، فإن الناس يصعقون يوم القيامة فأصعق معهم، فأكون أول من يفيق، فإذا موسى باطش جانب العرش، فلا أدري أكان فيمن صعق فأفاق قبلي، أو كان ممن استثنى اللّٰه)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٤١١)، ومسلم (٢٣٧٣: ١٦٠).

12960 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
Two men insulted one another: one was a Muslim and the other was a Jew.
The Muslim said:
“By the One who chose Muḥammad above all the worlds.”
The Jew replied:
“By the One who chose Moses above all the worlds.”
The Muslim then raised his hand and slapped the Jew across the face.
The Jew went to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of what had happened between him and the Muslim. The Prophet ﷺ summoned the Muslim and questioned him, and he related what had happened.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Do not declare me superior to Moses in this manner. The people will fall unconscious on the Day of Resurrection, and I will fall unconscious with them. I will be the first to regain consciousness, and Moses will be grasping the side of the Throne. I do not know whether he will have been among those who fell unconscious and regained consciousness before me, or whether he will have been among those whom Allah excluded.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2411) and Muslim (2373:160).

١٢٩٦٠ — عن أبي هريرة قال: استب رجلان: رجل من المسلمين ورجل من اليهود.
قال المسلم: والذي اصطفى محمدًا على العالمين.
فقال اليهودي: والذي اصطفى موسى على العالمين.
فرفع المسلم يده عند ذلك، فلطم وجه اليهودي.
فذهب اليهودي إلى النبي ﷺ، فأخبره بما كان من أمره وأمر المسلم.
فدعا النبي ﷺ المسلم، فسأله عن ذلك، فأخبره.
فقال النبي ﷺ:
((لا تخيروني على موسى، فإن الناس يصعقون يوم القيامة فأصعق معهم، فأكون أول من يفيق، فإذا موسى باطش جانب العرش، فلا أدري أكان فيمن صعق فأفاق قبلي، أو كان ممن استثنى اللّٰه)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٤١١)، ومسلم (٢٣٧٣: ١٦٠).

فقال العباس: يا رسول اللّٰه، إلا الإذخر؛ فإنه لقينهم ولبيوتهم.

((إلا الإذخر)).

12961 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
On the Day of the Conquest of Makkah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“There is no migration after the conquest, but there remains striving and sincere intention. When you are called to mobilize, then go forth.”
He also said on the Day of the Conquest of Makkah:
“Allah made this city sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth. It therefore remains sacred by the sanctity granted to it by Allah until the Day of Resurrection.
Fighting within it was not made lawful for anyone before me, and it was made lawful for me only for a brief period during one day. It remains sacred by the sanctity granted to it by Allah until the Day of Resurrection.
Its thorny plants must not be cut, its game must not be frightened, its lost property must not be picked up except by one who will publicly announce it, and its fresh vegetation must not be cut.”
Al-ʿAbbās said:
“O Messenger of Allah, except for idhkhir grass, because it is needed by their metalworkers and for their houses.”
He replied:
“Except for idhkhir grass.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1834) and Muslim (1353:445). The wording is that of Muslim.

١٢٩٦٢ — عن سعيد بن جبير قال: سألني يهودي من أهل الحيرة: أي الأجلين قضى موسى؟ قلت: لا أدري حتى أقدم على حبر العرب فأسأله.
فقدمت، فسألت ابن عباس، فقال: قضى أكثرهما وأطيبهما، إن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ إذا قال فعل.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٦٨٤).
هذا الذي ذكره ابن عباس لم يكن من اجتهاده، بل جاء أيضًا مرفوعًا، فلعله حدث بذلك في مجلسين.

12962 — Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated:
A Jewish man from al-Ḥīrah asked me:
“Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill?”
I replied:
“I do not know. I will wait until I meet the great scholar of the Arabs and ask him.”
When I arrived, I asked Ibn ʿAbbās. He replied:
“He fulfilled the longer and better of the two terms. When a messenger of Allah gives his word, he fulfills it.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2684).
What Ibn ʿAbbās stated was not merely his own reasoning. It was also narrated as a statement of the Prophet ﷺ. Perhaps he related it on two separate occasions.

arabic_source:
١٢٩٦٤ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري، رفعه إلى النبي ﷺ، قال:
((ما أهلك اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى قومًا بعذاب من السماء ولا من الأرض إلا قبل موسى)).
ثم قال: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا أَهْلَكْنَا الْقُرُونَ الْأُولَىٰ﴾.
صحيح: رواه البزار في كشف الأستار (٢٢٤٨).
وأما الأمم السابقة التي عذبها اللّٰه تعالى قبل إعطاء موسى عليه السلام التوراة فهي:
أولًا: قوم نوح عليه السلام:
قال تعالى: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمْ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمْسِينَ عَامًا فَأَخَذَهُمُ الطُّوفَانُ وَهُمْ ظَالِمُونَ﴾ [العنكبوت: ١٤].
ثانيًا: عاد قوم هود عليه السلام:
قال تعالى: ﴿وَأَمَّا عَادٌ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍ ۝ سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيَالٍ وَثَمَانِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومًا فَتَرَى الْقَوْمَ فِيهَا صَرْعَىٰ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ﴾ [الحاقة: ٦-٧].
ثالثًا: ثمود قوم صالح عليه السلام:
قال تعالى: ﴿فَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِالطَّاغِيَةِ﴾ [الحاقة: ٥].
رابعًا: قوم لوط عليه السلام:
قال تعالى: ﴿فَنَجَّيْنَاهُ وَأَهْلَهُ أَجْمَعِينَ ۝ إِلَّا عَجُوزًا فِي الْغَابِرِينَ ۝ ثُمَّ دَمَّرْنَا الْآخَرِينَ ۝ وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ مَطَرًا فَسَاءَ مَطَرُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ﴾ [الشعراء: ١٧٠-١٧٣].
خامسًا: قوم شعيب عليه السلام:
قال تعالى: ﴿فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ فَأَصْبَحُوا فِي دَارِهِمْ جَاثِمِينَ ۝ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا شُعَيْبًا كَأَنْ لَمْ يَغْنَوْا فِيهَا الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا شُعَيْبًا كَانُوا هُمُ الْخَاسِرِينَ﴾ [الأعراف: ٩١-٩٢].
وقال تعالى: ﴿وَإِذْ فَرَقْنَا بِكُمُ الْبَحْرَ فَأَنْجَيْنَاكُمْ وَأَغْرَقْنَا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَأَنْتُمْ تَنْظُرُونَ﴾ [البقرة: ٥٠].

12964 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī attributed the following statement to the Prophet ﷺ:
“Allah, Blessed and Exalted, did not destroy an entire people with a punishment from the heavens or the earth except before Moses.”
He then recited:
“We certainly gave Moses the Scripture after We had destroyed the earlier generations.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (2248).
The earlier nations whom Allah punished before giving Moses, peace be upon him, the Torah include:
First: The People of Noah, Peace Be upon Him
Allah says:
“We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them for a thousand years minus fifty. Then the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers.”
 [Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt 29:14]
Second: ʿĀd, the People of Hūd, Peace Be upon Him
Allah says:
“As for ʿĀd, they were destroyed by a furious, bitterly cold wind which He imposed upon them for seven nights and eight consecutive days. You would have seen the people lying fallen as though they were hollow trunks of palm trees.”
 [Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah 69:6–7]
Third: Thamūd, the People of Ṣāliḥ, Peace Be upon Him
Allah says:
“As for Thamūd, they were destroyed by the overwhelming blast.”
 [Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah 69:5]
Fourth: The People of Lot, Peace Be upon Him
Allah says:
“We saved him and his entire family, except an old woman who remained behind. Then We utterly destroyed the others and rained upon them a rain of punishment. How terrible was the rain of those who had been warned.”
 [Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ 26:170–173]
Fifth: The People of Shuʿayb, Peace Be upon Him
Allah says:
“The earthquake seized them, and by morning they lay lifeless in their homes. Those who denied Shuʿayb became as though they had never lived there. Those who denied Shuʿayb were themselves the losers.”
 [Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:91–92]
Allah also says:
“Remember when We parted the sea for you, saved you, and drowned Pharaoh’s people while you watched.”
 [Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:50]
All of these peoples were destroyed before the Torah was revealed to Moses, peace be upon him. Allah therefore says:
“We certainly gave Moses the Scripture after We had destroyed the earlier generations, as enlightenment for the people, guidance, and mercy, so that they might take heed.”
 [Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ 28:43]

 [Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah 69:6–7]
Third: Thamūd, the People of Ṣāliḥ, Peace Be upon Him
Allah says:
“As for Thamūd, they were destroyed by the overwhelming blast.”
 [Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah 69:5]
Fourth: The People of Lot, Peace Be upon Him
Allah says:
“We saved him and his entire family, except an old woman who remained behind. Then We utterly destroyed the others and rained upon them a rain of punishment. How terrible was the rain of those who had been warned.”
 [Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ 26:170–173]
Fifth: The People of Shuʿayb, Peace Be upon Him
Allah says:
“The earthquake seized them, and by morning they lay lifeless in their homes. Those who denied Shuʿayb became as though they had never lived there. Those who denied Shuʿayb were themselves the losers.”
 [Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:91–92]
Allah also says:
“Remember when We parted the sea for you, saved you, and drowned Pharaoh’s people while you watched.”
 [Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:50]
All of these peoples were destroyed before the Torah was revealed to Moses, peace be upon him. Allah therefore says:
“We certainly gave Moses the Scripture after We had destroyed the earlier generations, as enlightenment for the people, guidance, and mercy, so that they might take heed.”
 [Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ 28:43]

12965 — Rifāʿah al-Quraẓī said:
“This verse was revealed concerning ten people, and I was one of them:
‘We have repeatedly conveyed the Word to them so that they may take heed. Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it believe in it. When it is recited to them, they say: We believe in it. It is certainly the truth from our Lord. Even before it, we had submitted to Allah. Those will be given their reward twice because of their patience. They repel evil with good, and they spend from what We have provided them.’”
Authentic: Narrated by Ibn Jarīr in his Tafsīr (18/276), Ibn Abī Ḥātim in his Tafsīr (9/2987–2988), and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (5/46–47).
Its chain is authentic.
The words:
“Those will be given their reward twice”
mean that the People of the Scripture who believed in their own prophet and then believed in the Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ receive a double reward, as stated in the authentic hadith:

١٢٩٦٦ — عن أبي موسى قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((ثلاثة لهم أجران: رجل من أهل الكتاب آمن بنبيه وآمن بمحمد ﷺ، والعبد المملوك إذا أدى حق اللّٰه وحق مواليه، ورجل كانت عنده أمة، فأدبها فأحسن تأديبها، وعلمها فأحسن تعليمها، ثم أعتقها فتزوجها، فله أجران)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٩٧)، ومسلم (١٥٤)، واللفظ للبخاري.

12966 — Abū Mūsā narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Three people will receive a double reward: a man from the People of the Scripture who believed in his prophet and then believed in Muḥammad ﷺ; an enslaved servant who fulfills the rights of Allah and the rights of his masters; and a man who possesses a slave woman, educates her well, teaches her well, then emancipates her and marries her. He will receive two rewards.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (97) and Muslim (154). The wording is that of al-Bukhārī.

١٢٩٦٧ — عن أبي أمامة قال: إني لتحت راحلة رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يوم الفتح، فقال قولًا حسنًا جميلًا، وكان فيما قال:
((من أسلم من أهل الكتابين فله أجره مرتين، وله ما لنا، وعليه ما علينا، ومن أسلم من المشركين فله أجره، وله ما لنا، وعليه ما علينا)).
حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٢٢٣٤).
وفي الإسناد ابن لهيعة، وفيه كلام معروف من أجل اختلاطه، لكن رواه الطبري في تفسيره (٢٢/٤٤١)، والطحاوي في شرح مشكل الآثار (٢٥٧١) كلاهما من طريق عبد اللّٰه بن وهب، عن عبد اللّٰه بن لهيعة به.
ورواية ابن وهب عن ابن لهيعة أعدل من غيرها.
وكذلك ابن لهيعة توبع أيضًا، فقد رواه الطبري في تفسيره (٢٢/٤٤١)، والطحاوي في شرح مشكل الآثار (٢٥٧١)، والطبراني في الكبير (٨/٢٢٤) من طريق الليث بن سعد، عن سليمان بن عبد الرحمن به.
وسليمان بن عبد الرحمن وشيخه القاسم، وهو ابن عبد الرحمن الدمشقي، كلاهما حسنا الحديث.

12967 — Abū Umāmah narrated:
I was beneath the riding animal of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Day of the Conquest when he delivered a fine and beautiful address. Among what he said was:
“Whoever accepts Islam from among the two Peoples of the Scripture will receive his reward twice. He will have the same rights as us and bear the same obligations as us. Whoever accepts Islam from among the polytheists will receive his reward, have the same rights as us, and bear the same obligations as us.”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (22234).
The chain contains Ibn Lahīʿah, concerning whom there is well-known criticism because of his later confusion. However, al-Ṭabarī in his Tafsīr (22/441) and al-Ṭaḥāwī in Sharḥ Mushkil al-Āthār (2571) narrated it through ʿAbdullāh ibn Wahb from ʿAbdullāh ibn Lahīʿah with the same chain.
Ibn Wahb’s narration from Ibn Lahīʿah is more reliable than the narrations of others from him.
Ibn Lahīʿah was also corroborated. Al-Ṭabarī in his Tafsīr (22/441), al-Ṭaḥāwī in Sharḥ Mushkil al-Āthār (2571), and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (8/224) narrated it through al-Layth ibn Saʿd from Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān with the same chain.
Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and his shaykh al-Qāsim—namely Ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Dimashqī—are both considered good in hadith.

١٢٩٦٨ — عن سعيد بن المسيب، عن أبيه، قال: لما حضرت أبا طالب الوفاة، جاءه رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فوجد عنده أبا جهل وعبد اللّٰه بن أبي أمية بن المغيرة، فقال:
((أي عم، قل: لا إله إلا اللّٰه، كلمة أحاج لك بها عند اللّٰه)).
فقال أبو جهل وعبد اللّٰه بن أبي أمية: أترغب عن ملة عبد المطلب؟
فلم يزل رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يعرضها عليه، ويعيدان له بتلك المقالة، حتى قال أبو طالب آخر ما كلمهم: على ملة عبد المطلب، وأبى أن يقول: لا إله إلا اللّٰه.
قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((واللّٰه لأستغفرن لك ما لم أنه عنك)).
فأنزل اللّٰه: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ وَلَوْ كَانُوا أُولِي قُرْبَىٰ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُمْ أَصْحَابُ الْجَحِيمِ﴾ [التوبة: ١١٣].
وأنزل اللّٰه في أبي طالب، فقال لرسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ﴿إِنَّكَ لَا تَهْدِي مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ﴾.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٧٧٢)، ومسلم (٢٤)، واللفظ للبخاري، ولفظ مسلم نحوه.

12968 — Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib narrated from his father:
When death approached Abū Ṭālib, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to him and found Abū Jahl and ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Umayyah ibn al-Mughīrah beside him.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Uncle, say: ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah,’ a statement with which I may plead on your behalf before Allah.”
Abū Jahl and ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Umayyah said:
“Will you abandon the religion of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ continued presenting the testimony of faith to him, while the two men continued repeating their statement.
The last words Abū Ṭālib spoke to them were:
“I remain upon the religion of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.”
He refused to say:
“There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“By Allah, I will continue seeking forgiveness for you unless I am forbidden from doing so.”
Allah then revealed:
“It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to seek forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they are close relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are inhabitants of the Blaze.”
 [Sūrat al-Tawbah 9:113]
Allah also revealed concerning Abū Ṭālib, addressing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
“You cannot guide whomever you love, but Allah guides whomever He wills, and He knows best who is rightly guided.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4772) and Muslim (24). The wording is that of al-Bukhārī, while Muslim’s wording is similar.

((قل: لا إله إلا اللّٰه، أشهد لك بها يوم القيامة)).
قال: لولا أن تعيرني قريش، يقولون: إنما حمله على ذلك الجزع، لأقررت بها عينك.
فأنزل اللّٰه: ﴿إِنَّكَ لَا تَهْدِي مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ﴾.

قال: لولا أن تعيرني قريش، يقولون: إنما حمله على ذلك الجزع، لأقررت بها عينك.
فأنزل اللّٰه: ﴿إِنَّكَ لَا تَهْدِي مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ﴾.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٥: ٤٢).

12969 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his uncle:
“Say: ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah,’ and I will testify on your behalf because of it on the Day of Resurrection.”
His uncle replied:
“Were it not that Quraysh would shame me and say that fear at the approach of death caused me to say it, I would certainly comfort your eyes by uttering it.”
Allah then revealed:
“You cannot guide whomever you love, but Allah guides whomever He wills, and He knows best who is rightly guided.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (25:42).

“By Allah, this world in comparison with the Hereafter is only like one of you dipping this finger”—Yaḥyā pointed with his index finger—“into the sea. Let him then observe how much water it brings back.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2858).

١٢٩٧١ — عن عون بن أبي جحيفة، عن أبيه، قال: آخى النبي ﷺ بين سلمان وأبي الدرداء، فزار سلمان أبا الدرداء، فرأى أم الدرداء متبذلة، فقال لها: ما شأنك؟
قالت: أخوك أبو الدرداء ليس له حاجة في الدنيا.
فجاء أبو الدرداء، فصنع له طعامًا، فقال له: كل.
قال: فإني صائم.
قال: ما أنا بآكل حتى تأكل.
قال: فأكل.
فلما كان الليل ذهب أبو الدرداء يقوم، قال: نم، فنام. ثم ذهب يقوم، فقال: نم.
فلما كان من آخر الليل قال سلمان: قم الآن، فصليا.
فقال له سلمان: إن لربك عليك حقًّا، ولنفسك عليك حقًّا، ولأهلك عليك حقًّا، فأعط كل ذي حق حقه.
فأتى النبي ﷺ فذكر ذلك له، فقال له النبي ﷺ:
((صدق سلمان)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (١٩٦٨).

12971 — ʿAwn ibn Abī Juḥayfah narrated from his father:
The Prophet ﷺ established brotherhood between Salmān and Abū al-Dardāʾ.
Salmān visited Abū al-Dardāʾ and saw Umm al-Dardāʾ wearing neglected clothing. He asked her:
“What is the matter with you?”
She replied:
“Your brother Abū al-Dardāʾ has no interest in worldly life.”
Abū al-Dardāʾ arrived and prepared food for Salmān, saying:
“Eat.”
Salmān replied:
“I am fasting.”
Abū al-Dardāʾ said:
“I will not eat until you eat.”
So Salmān ate.
When night came, Abū al-Dardāʾ attempted to stand for prayer. Salmān said:
“Sleep.”
He slept, then later attempted to rise again. Salmān again said:
“Sleep.”
During the final part of the night, Salmān said:
“Rise now.”
They both prayed.
Salmān then said:
“Your Lord has a right over you, your own self has a right over you, and your family has a right over you. Therefore, give everyone who possesses a right his due.”
Abū al-Dardāʾ went to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned this to him.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Salmān has spoken the truth.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1968).

١٢٩٧٢ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال النبي ﷺ، أو قال أبو القاسم ﷺ:
((بينما رجل يمشي في حلة تعجبه نفسه، مرجل جمته، إذ خسف اللّٰه به، فهو يتجلجل إلى يوم القيامة)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٧٨٩)، ومسلم (٢٠٨٨)، واللفظ للبخاري.
وقيل: إن هذا الرجل هو قارون.
وفي معناه أحاديث أخرى ذكرت في مواضعها.

12972 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ—or Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ—said:
“While a man was walking in a fine garment, admiring himself, with his hair neatly combed, Allah caused the earth to swallow him. He will continue sinking into it until the Day of Resurrection.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5789) and Muslim (2088). The wording is that of al-Bukhārī.
It has been said that this man was Qārūn.
Other hadiths with the same meaning have been mentioned in their respective places.

١٢٩٧٣ — عن ابن مسعود قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((إن اللّٰه قسم بينكم أخلاقكم كما قسم بينكم أرزاقكم، وإن اللّٰه يعطي الدنيا من يحب ومن لا يحب، ولا يعطي الإيمان إلا من يحب)).
صحيح: رواه الحاكم (١/٣٣-٣٤).
قال الحاكم: «هذا حديث صحيح».
والكلام عليه مبسوط في كتاب الإيمان.

“No one who has an atom’s weight of arrogance in his heart will enter Paradise.”
A man asked:
“A person likes his clothing and footwear to be beautiful.”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“Allah is Beautiful and loves beauty. Arrogance is rejecting the truth and looking down upon people.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (91).

١٢٩٧٧ — عن مصعب بن سعد، عن أبيه، أنه نزلت فيه آيات من القرآن، قال: حلفت أم سعد ألا تكلمه أبدًا حتى يكفر بدينه، ولا تأكل ولا تشرب.
قالت: زعمت أن اللّٰه وصاك بوالديك، وأنا أمك، وأنا آمرك بهذا.
قال: مكثت ثلاثًا حتى غشي عليها من الجهد، فقام ابن لها يقال له عمارة فسقاها، فجعلت تدعو على سعد.
فأنزل اللّٰه عز وجل في القرآن هذه الآية: ﴿وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ بِوَالِدَيْهِ حُسْنًا﴾ [العنكبوت: ٨]، و﴿وَإِنْ جَاهَدَاكَ عَلَىٰ أَنْ تُشْرِكَ بِي﴾ [لقمان: ١٥]، وفيها: ﴿وَصَاحِبْهُمَا فِي الدُّنْيَا مَعْرُوفًا﴾ [لقمان: ١٥].
قال: وأصاب رسول اللّٰه ﷺ غنيمة عظيمة، فإذا فيها سيف، فأخذته، فأتيت به الرسول ﷺ، فقلت: نفلني هذا السيف، فأنا من قد علمت حاله.
فقال:
((رده من حيث أخذته)).
فانطلقت، حتى إذا أردت أن ألقيه في القبض، لامتني نفسي، فرجعت إليه، فقلت: أعطنيه.
قال: فشد لي صوته:
((رده من حيث أخذته)).
قال: فأنزل اللّٰه عز وجل: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْأَنْفَالِ﴾ [الأنفال: ١].
قال: ومرضت، فأرسلت إلى النبي ﷺ، فأتاني، فقلت: دعني أقسم مالي حيث شئت.
قال: فأبى. قلت: فالنصف. قال: فأبى. قلت: فالثلث. قال: فسكت، فكان بعد الثلث جائزًا.
قال: وأتيت على نفر من الأنصار والمهاجرين، فقالوا: تعال نطعمك ونسقيك خمرًا، وذلك قبل أن تحرم الخمر.
قال: فأتيتهم في حش، والحش البستان، فإذا رأس جزور مشوي عندهم، وزق من خمر.
قال: فأكلت وشربت معهم.
قال: فذكرت الأنصار والمهاجرون عندهم، فقلت: المهاجرون خير من الأنصار.
قال: فأخذ رجل أحد لحيي الرأس، فضربني به، فجرح أنفي.
فأتيت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فأخبرته، فأنزل اللّٰه عز وجل في، يعني نفسه، شأن الخمر: ﴿إِنَّمَا الْخَمْرُ وَالْمَيْسِرُ وَالْأَنْصَابُ وَالْأَزْلَامُ رِجْسٌ مِنْ عَمَلِ الشَّيْطَانِ﴾ [المائدة: ٩٠].
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٧٤٨: ٤٣).
وفي رواية: «فضرب به أنف سعد ففزره»، وكان أنف سعد مفزورًا، أي: مشقوقًا. وأمه هي حمنة بنت أبي سفيان بن أمية بن عبد شمس.

12977 — Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd narrated from his father that several verses of the Qur’an were revealed concerning him.
He said:
My mother swore that she would never speak to me until I rejected my religion, and that she would neither eat nor drink.
She said:
“You claim that Allah has commanded you to treat your parents well. I am your mother, and I command you to abandon this religion.”
She remained in that condition for three days until she lost consciousness from exhaustion. One of her sons, named ʿUmārah, stood and gave her water. She then began supplicating against Saʿd.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed:
“We have instructed the human being to treat his parents well.”
 [Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt 29:8]
And:
“But if they strive to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge…”
 [Sūrat Luqmān 31:15]
The same passage contains:
“Accompany them in this world with kindness.”
 [Sūrat Luqmān 31:15]
Saʿd continued:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ obtained a large amount of war booty, including a sword. I took it and brought it to the Messenger ﷺ, saying:
“Grant me this sword as an additional share, for you know my condition and service.”
He replied:
“Return it to the place from which you took it.”
I went back, but when I was about to place it among the collected spoils, my soul reproached me. I returned to him and said:
“Give it to me.”
He raised his voice and said:
“Return it to the place from which you took it.”
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then revealed:
“They ask you concerning the spoils of war.”
 [Sūrat al-Anfāl 8:1]
Saʿd continued:
I became ill and sent for the Prophet ﷺ. He came to me, and I said:
“Allow me to distribute all my wealth however I wish.”
He refused.
I said:
“Then one half?”
He refused.
I said:
“Then one third?”
He remained silent. Thereafter, bequeathing one third became permissible.
Saʿd continued:
I passed by a group of the Anṣār and Emigrants. They said:
“Come, we will feed you and give you wine to drink.”
This occurred before wine was prohibited.
I joined them in a garden. They had the roasted head of a camel and a wineskin. I ate and drank with them.
The Anṣār and Emigrants were then mentioned, and I said:
“The Emigrants are better than the Anṣār.”
One man picked up one of the jawbones of the camel’s head and struck me with it, injuring my nose.
I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then revealed concerning me and the matter of wine:
“Wine, gambling, stone altars, and divining arrows are only filth from the work of Satan.”
 [Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:90]
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1748:43).
In another narration: “He struck Saʿd’s nose with it and split it.” Saʿd’s nose was therefore mafzūr, meaning split. His mother was Ḥamnah bint Abī Sufyān ibn Umayyah ibn ʿAbd Shams.
