((بعثت أنا والساعة كهاتين)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٩٣٦)، ومسلم (٢٩٥٠).
وقوله: ﴿فَأَنَّىٰ لَهُمْ إِذَا جَاءَتْهُمْ ذِكْرَاهُمْ﴾، أي: من أين لهم إذا جاءتهم الساعة أن يتذكروا؟ فقد فات أوان التذكر وذهب وقته، وهذا مثل قوله تعالى: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسَانُ وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُ الذِّكْرَىٰ﴾ [الفجر: ٢٣].
فتوبتهم وتذكرهم واستعتابهم لا ينفعهم في ذلك اليوم البتة.
13291 — Sahl ibn Saʿd narrated:
I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gesture with these two fingers—the middle finger and the index finger—and say:
“I and the Hour have been sent like these two.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4936) and Muslim (2950).
Regarding the words:
“But how will remembrance benefit them when it comes upon them?”
how will they be able to benefit from remembering and taking heed once the Hour has already arrived?
The proper time for taking heed will have passed.
This resembles Allah’s words:
“On that Day man will remember, but how will remembrance benefit him then?” [Sūrat al-Fajr 89:23]
Their repentance, remembrance, and attempts to seek another opportunity will not benefit them at all on that Day.

١٣٢٩٢ — عن عاصم الأحول، عن عبد اللّٰه بن سرجس قال: رأيت النبي ﷺ، وأكلت معه خبزًا ولحمًا - أو قال: ثريدًا -.
قال: فقلت له: أستغفر لك النبي ﷺ؟
قال: نعم، ولك.
ثم تلا هذه الآية: ﴿وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لِذَنْبِكَ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾.
قال: ثم درت خلفه، فنظرت إلى خاتم النبوة بين كتفيه… الحديث.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٣٤٦).

english_source:
13292 — ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sarjis, who said:
I saw the Prophet ﷺ and ate bread and meat with him—or he said, tharīd.
ʿĀṣim said:
I asked him:
“Did the Prophet ﷺ seek forgiveness for you?”
He replied:
“Yes, and for you as well.”
Then he recited:
“Seek forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women.”
ʿAbdullāh ibn Sarjis continued:
Then I went around behind him and looked at the Seal of Prophethood between his shoulders.
The hadith continues.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2346).

١٣٢٩٣ — عن أبي موسى الأشعري، عن النبي ﷺ أنه كان يدعو بهذا الدعاء:
((رب اغفر لي خطيئتي وجهلي وإسرافي في أمري كله، وما أنت أعلم به مني، اللهم اغفر لي خطاياي، وعمدي، وجهلي، وهزلي، وكل ذلك عندي، اللهم اغفر لي ما قدمت وما أخرت، وما أسررت وما أعلنت، أنت المقدم، وأنت المؤخر، وأنت على كل شيء قدير)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٣٩٨)، ومسلم (٢٧١٩)، واللفظ للبخاري.

english_source:
13293 — Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī narrated that the Prophet ﷺ used to supplicate with the following words:
“My Lord, forgive me my errors, my ignorance, my excesses in all my affairs, and whatever You know better about me than I do.
O Allah, forgive me my sins, those I committed deliberately, those committed through ignorance, and those committed in jest—all of that is found within me.
O Allah, forgive me what I have sent ahead and what I have left behind, what I have concealed and what I have made public. You are the One who brings forward and the One who delays, and You have power over all things.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6398) and Muslim (2719). The wording is that of al-Bukhārī.

((واللّٰه إني لأستغفر اللّٰه وأتوب إليه في اليوم أكثر من سبعين مرة)).

I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“By Allah, I seek Allah’s forgiveness and repent to Him more than seventy times every day.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6307).

١٣٢٩٥ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((إن الشيطان قال: وعزتك يا رب، لا أبرح أغوي عبادك ما دامت أرواحهم في أجسادهم. قال الرب: وعزتي وجلالي، لا أزال أغفر لهم ما استغفروني)).
حسن: رواه أحمد (١١٧٢٩، ١١٢٣٧، ١١٢٤٤).

13295 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Satan said: ‘By Your might, my Lord, I will continue leading Your servants astray for as long as their souls remain in their bodies.’
The Lord said: ‘By My might and My majesty, I will continue forgiving them for as long as they seek My forgiveness.’”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (11729, 11237, 11244).

١٣٢٩٦ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((إن اللّٰه خلق الخلق، حتى إذا فرغ منهم قامت الرحم، فقالت: هذا مقام العائذ من القطيعة. قال: نعم، أما ترضين أن أصل من وصلك، وأقطع من قطعك؟ قالت: بلى. قال: فذاك لك)).
ثم قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((اقرؤوا إن شئتم: ﴿فَهَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ إِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ أَنْ تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَتُقَطِّعُوا أَرْحَامَكُمْ ۝ أُولَٰئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ فَأَصَمَّهُمْ وَأَعْمَىٰ أَبْصَارَهُمْ ۝ أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ الْقُرْآنَ أَمْ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبٍ أَقْفَالُهَا﴾)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٨٣١)، ومسلم (٢٥٥٤)، واللفظ لمسلم.

١٣٢٩٧ — عن أبي بكرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((ما من ذنب أجدر أن يعجل اللّٰه تعالى لصاحبه العقوبة في الدنيا، مع ما يدخر له في الآخرة، مثل البغي وقطيعة الرحم)).
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٤٩٠٢)، والترمذي (٢٥١١)، وابن ماجه (٤٢١١)، وأحمد (٢٠٣٩٨)، وصححه الحاكم (٤/١٦٢).

13297 — Abū Bakrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“There is no sin more deserving that Allah hasten punishment for its perpetrator in this world, in addition to what He stores up for him in the Hereafter, than transgression and severing family ties.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4902), al-Tirmidhī (2511), Ibn Mājah (4211), Aḥmad (20398), and authenticated by al-Ḥākim (4/162).

13301 — ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Kinship is a closely intertwined bond. Whoever maintains it, I maintain ties with him, and whoever cuts it off, I cut him off.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5989) and Muslim (2555). The wording is that of al-Bukhārī.
Muslim’s wording is:
“The bond of kinship is suspended from the Throne, saying: ‘Whoever maintains me, Allah maintains him; and whoever cuts me off, Allah cuts him off.’”

١٣٣٠٤ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ تلا هذه الآية: ﴿وَإِنْ تَتَوَلَّوْا يَسْتَبْدِلْ قَوْمًا غَيْرَكُمْ ثُمَّ لَا يَكُونُوا أَمْثَالَكُمْ﴾.
قالوا: يا رسول اللّٰه، من هؤلاء الذين إن تولينا استبدلوا بنا ثم لا يكونوا أمثالنا؟
فضرب على فخذ سلمان، قال:
((هذا وقومه، ولو كان الدين عند الثريا لتناوله رجال من الفرس)).
حسن: رواه ابن جرير في تفسيره (٢١/٢٣٣-٢٣٤)، والبغوي في تفسيره (٤/١٦٤).

13304 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited the verse:
“If you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and then they will not be like you.”
They asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, who are these people with whom we would be replaced if we turned away, and who would not be like us?”
The Prophet ﷺ struck the thigh of Salmān and said:
“This man and his people. If the religion were as far away as the Pleiades, men from among the Persians would reach it.”
Good: Narrated by Ibn Jarīr in his Tafsīr (21/233–234) and al-Baghawī in his Tafsīr (4/164).

١٣٣٠٥ — عن زيد بن أسلم، عن أبيه، أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ كان يسير في بعض أسفاره، وعمر بن الخطاب يسير معه ليلًا، فسأله عمر بن الخطاب عن شيء فلم يجبه رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، ثم سأله فلم يجبه، ثم سأله فلم يجبه، فقال عمر بن الخطاب: ثكلتك أمك يا عمر، نزرت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ثلاث مرات، كل ذلك لا يجيبك.
قال عمر: فحركت بعيري، ثم تقدمت أمام المسلمين، وخشيت أن ينزل فيَّ قرآن، فما نشبت أن سمعت صارخًا يصرخ بي.
قال: فقلت: لقد خشيت أن يكون قد نزل فيَّ قرآن، وجئت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فسلمت عليه، فقال:
((لقد أنزلت عليَّ الليلة سورة لهي أحب إليَّ مما طلعت عليه الشمس)).
ثم قرأ: ﴿إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ فَتْحًا مُبِينًا﴾.
صحيح: رواه مالك في القرآن (٤٧٦)، والبخاري (٤١٧٧).
قوله: «نزرت» أي: ألححت.

13305 — Zayd ibn Aslam narrated from his father that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was traveling on one of his journeys, while ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was traveling alongside him at night.
ʿUmar asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about something, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not answer him. He asked him again, but he did not answer. Then he asked him a third time, and he still did not answer.
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said to himself:
“May your mother lose you, O ʿUmar! You have persistently questioned the Messenger of Allah ﷺ three times, and each time he has not answered you.”
ʿUmar said:
I urged my camel forward and went ahead of the Muslims, fearing that Qur’an might be revealed concerning me.
It was not long before I heard someone calling out loudly for me.
I said to myself:
“I feared that Qur’an had been revealed concerning me.”
I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and greeted him with salām.
He said:
“Tonight a sūrah has been revealed to me that is more beloved to me than everything upon which the sun rises.”
Then he recited:
“Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory.”
Authentic: Narrated by Mālik in Kitāb al-Qurʾān (476) and al-Bukhārī (4177).
The word “nazarta” means:
“You persisted and pressed repeatedly.”

١٣٣٠٦ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: لما نزلت: ﴿إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ فَتْحًا مُبِينًا ۝ لِيَغْفِرَ لَكَ اللَّهُ﴾ إلى قوله: ﴿فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا﴾ [الفتح: ١-٥] مرجعه من الحديبية، وهم يخالطهم الحزن والكآبة، وقد نحر الهدي بالحديبية، قال:
((لقد أنزلت عليَّ آية هي أحب إليَّ من الدنيا جميعًا)).
متفق عليه: رواه مسلم (١٧٨٦)، والبخاري (٤٨٣٤).

((لقد أنزلت عليَّ آية هي أحب إليَّ من الدنيا جميعًا)).
متفق عليه: رواه مسلم (١٧٨٦)، والبخاري (٤٨٣٤).
english_source:
13306 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
When the verses:
“Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory, so that Allah may forgive you…”
through His words:
“…a tremendous triumph” [Sūrat al-Fatḥ 48:1–5]
were revealed as the Prophet ﷺ was returning from al-Ḥudaybiyyah, the Companions were overcome by sorrow and distress, and the sacrificial animals had already been slaughtered at al-Ḥudaybiyyah.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“A verse has been revealed to me that is more beloved to me than the entire world.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Muslim (1786) and al-Bukhārī (4834).

١٣٣٠٧ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن مغفل المزني قال: رأيت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يوم الفتح على ناقة له يقرأ سورة الفتح - أو من سورة الفتح - قال: فرجَّع فيها.
قال: ثم قرأ معاوية يحكي قراءة ابن مغفل، وقال: لولا أن يجتمع الناس عليكم لرجعت كما رجع ابن مغفل يحكي النبي ﷺ.
قلت لمعاوية: كيف كان ترجيعه؟
قال: آ آ آ، ثلاث مرات.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧٥٤٠)، ومسلم (٧٩٤: ٢٣٧).

13307 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Mughaffal al-Muzanī narrated:
I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Day of the Conquest riding his she-camel and reciting Sūrat al-Fatḥ—or part of Sūrat al-Fatḥ—and he recited it with a melodious, repeated modulation.
Muʿāwiyah then recited in imitation of the recitation of Ibn Mughaffal and said:
“Were it not that the people would gather around you, I would reproduce the modulation just as Ibn Mughaffal reproduced the Prophet’s ﷺ recitation.”
I asked Muʿāwiyah:
“How did he modulate his voice?”
He replied:
“Ā, ā, ā,”
three times.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (7540) and Muslim (794:237).

١٣٣٠٨ — عن أبي وائل قال: قام سهل بن حنيف يوم صفين فقال: أيها الناس، اتهموا أنفسكم. لقد كنا مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يوم الحديبية، ولو نرى قتالًا لقاتلنا، وذلك في الصلح الذي كان بين رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وبين المشركين.
فجاء عمر بن الخطاب، فأتى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، ألسنا على حق وهم على باطل؟
قال: ((بلى)).
قال: أليس قتلانا في الجنة وقتلاهم في النار؟
قال: ((بلى)).
قال: ففيم نعطي الدنية في ديننا، ونرجع ولما يحكم اللّٰه بيننا وبينهم؟
فقال:
((يا ابن الخطاب، إني رسول اللّٰه، ولن يضيعني اللّٰه أبدًا)).
قال: فانطلق عمر فلم يصبر متغيظًا، فأتى أبا بكر، فقال: يا أبا بكر، ألسنا على حق وهم على باطل؟
قال: بلى.
قال: أليس قتلانا في الجنة وقتلاهم في النار؟
قال: بلى.
قال: فعلام نعطي الدنية في ديننا، ونرجع ولما يحكم اللّٰه بيننا وبينهم؟
فقال: يا ابن الخطاب، إنه رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، ولن يضيعه اللّٰه أبدًا.
قال: فنزل القرآن على رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بالفتح، فأرسل إلى عمر فأقرأه إياه.
فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، أوَفتح هو؟
قال: ((نعم)).
فطابت نفسه ورجع.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣١٨٢)، ومسلم (١٧٨٥: ٩٤).

13308 — Abū Wāʾil narrated:
Sahl ibn Ḥunayf stood on the Day of Ṣiffīn and said:
“People, question your own judgment. We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Day of al-Ḥudaybiyyah, and had we seen that fighting was required, we would have fought.”
This concerned the treaty made between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the polytheists.
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, are we not upon the truth while they are upon falsehood?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
ʿUmar asked:
“Are not our dead in Paradise and their dead in the Fire?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
ʿUmar said:
“Then why should we accept humiliation in our religion and turn back before Allah has judged between us and them?”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“O son of al-Khaṭṭāb, I am the Messenger of Allah, and Allah will never abandon me.”
ʿUmar left, but because of his agitation he could not remain patient, so he went to Abū Bakr and said:
“Abū Bakr, are we not upon the truth while they are upon falsehood?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
ʿUmar asked:
“Are not our dead in Paradise and their dead in the Fire?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
ʿUmar said:
“Then why should we accept humiliation in our religion and turn back before Allah has judged between us and them?”
Abū Bakr said:
“O son of al-Khaṭṭāb, he is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah will never abandon him.”
Then the Qur’an announcing the victory was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He sent for ʿUmar and recited it to him.
ʿUmar asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, is this truly a victory?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
Then ʿUmar’s heart became content and he returned.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3182) and Muslim (1785:94).

قال: فانطلق عمر فلم يصبر متغيظًا، فأتى أبا بكر، فقال: يا أبا بكر، ألسنا على حق وهم على باطل؟
قال: بلى.
قال: أليس قتلانا في الجنة وقتلاهم في النار؟
قال: بلى.
قال: فعلام نعطي الدنية في ديننا، ونرجع ولما يحكم اللّٰه بيننا وبينهم؟
فقال: يا ابن الخطاب، إنه رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، ولن يضيعه اللّٰه أبدًا.
قال: فنزل القرآن على رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بالفتح، فأرسل إلى عمر فأقرأه إياه.
فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، أوَفتح هو؟
قال: ((نعم)).
فطابت نفسه ورجع.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣١٨٢)، ومسلم (١٧٨٥: ٩٤).
13308 — Abū Wāʾil narrated:
Sahl ibn Ḥunayf stood on the Day of Ṣiffīn and said:
“People, question your own judgment. We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Day of al-Ḥudaybiyyah, and had we seen that fighting was required, we would have fought.”
This concerned the treaty made between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the polytheists.
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, are we not upon the truth while they are upon falsehood?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
ʿUmar asked:
“Are not our dead in Paradise and their dead in the Fire?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
ʿUmar said:
“Then why should we accept humiliation in our religion and turn back before Allah has judged between us and them?”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“O son of al-Khaṭṭāb, I am the Messenger of Allah, and Allah will never abandon me.”
ʿUmar left, but because of his agitation he could not remain patient, so he went to Abū Bakr and said:
“Abū Bakr, are we not upon the truth while they are upon falsehood?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
ʿUmar asked:
“Are not our dead in Paradise and their dead in the Fire?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
ʿUmar said:
“Then why should we accept humiliation in our religion and turn back before Allah has judged between us and them?”
Abū Bakr said:
“O son of al-Khaṭṭāb, he is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah will never abandon him.”
Then the Qur’an announcing the victory was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He sent for ʿUmar and recited it to him.
ʿUmar asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, is this truly a victory?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
Then ʿUmar’s heart became content and he returned.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3182) and Muslim (1785:94).

١٣٣٠٩ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن مسعود قال: أقبلنا مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ زمن الحديبية، فذكروا أنهم نزلوا دهاسًا من الأرض - يعني بالدهاس: الرمل - فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((من يكلؤنا؟)).
فقال بلال: أنا.
فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((إذن تنم)).
قال: فناموا حتى طلعت الشمس، فاستيقظ الناس، فيهم فلان وفلان، وفيهم عمر.
قال: فقلنا: اهضبوا - يعني تكلموا -.
قال: فاستيقظ النبي ﷺ، فقال:
((افعلوا كما كنتم تفعلون)).
قال: ففعلنا.
قال: وقال:
((كذلك فافعلوا لمن نام أو نسي)).
قال: وضلت ناقة رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فطلبها، فوجدت حبلها قد تعلق بشجرة، فجئت بها إلى النبي ﷺ، فركب مسرورًا.
وكان النبي ﷺ إذا نزل عليه الوحي اشتد ذلك عليه، وعرفنا ذاك فيه.
قال: فتنحى منتبذًا خلفنا، قال: فجعل يغطي رأسه بثوبه، ويشتد ذلك عليه، حتى عرفنا أنه قد أنزل عليه.
فأتانا، فأخبرنا أنه قد أنزل عليه: ﴿إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ فَتْحًا مُبِينًا﴾.
حسن: رواه أحمد (٤٤٢١)، والبزار - كشف الأستار (٤٠٠).

13309 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd narrated:
We were traveling with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the time of al-Ḥudaybiyyah. They mentioned that they stopped on a stretch of dahās land—meaning sandy ground.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked:
“Who will keep watch over us?”
Bilāl said:
“I will.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
“Then you will fall asleep.”
But they slept until the sun had risen.
The people awoke, among them various men, including ʿUmar.
We said:
“Speak aloud.”
The Prophet ﷺ then woke up and said:
“Do as you normally do.”
So we did so.
Then he said:
“Do the same whenever someone sleeps through a prayer or forgets it.”
The she-camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ then became lost, so I went looking for it. I found that its rope had become caught on a tree.
I brought it back to the Prophet ﷺ, and he mounted it happily.
Whenever revelation descended upon the Prophet ﷺ, it weighed heavily upon him, and we could recognize its effect upon him.
He withdrew some distance behind us and began covering his head with his garment. The experience became intense upon him, until we realized that revelation was descending upon him.
Then he came to us and informed us that the following had been revealed to him:
“Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory.”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (4421) and al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (400).

١٣٣١٠ — عن البراء قال: تعدون أنتم الفتح فتح مكة، وقد كان فتح مكة فتحًا، ونحن نعد الفتح بيعة الرضوان يوم الحديبية.
كنا مع النبي ﷺ أربع عشرة مائة، والحديبية بئر، فنزحناها فلم نترك فيها قطرة، فبلغ ذلك النبي ﷺ، فأتاها، فجلس على شفيرها، ثم دعا بإناء من ماء فتوضأ، ثم مضمض ودعا، ثم صبه فيها.
فتركناها غير بعيد، ثم إنها أصدرتنا ما شئنا نحن وركابنا.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٤١٥٠).

13310 — Al-Barāʾ narrated:
“You consider the Conquest to be the conquest of Makkah. The conquest of Makkah was indeed a conquest, but we considered the true victory to be the Pledge of al-Riḍwān on the Day of al-Ḥudaybiyyah.”
We were with the Prophet ﷺ, fourteen hundred in number.
At al-Ḥudaybiyyah there was a well. We drew out all of its water until we did not leave a single drop in it.
When this reached the Prophet ﷺ, he came to the well and sat upon its edge. He asked for a vessel containing water, performed ablution, rinsed his mouth, supplicated, and then poured the water into the well.
We left it for a short while, and afterward it provided as much water as we and our riding animals desired.
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4150).

((أفلا أكون عبدًا شكورًا؟)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٨٣٦)، ومسلم (٢٨١٩: ٨٠)، واللفظ للبخاري، ولفظ مسلم نحوه.

13311 — Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ stood in prayer until his feet became swollen.
It was said to him:
“Allah has forgiven you what preceded of your sin and what will follow.”
He replied:
“Should I not then be a grateful servant?”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4836) and Muslim (2819:80). The wording is that of al-Bukhārī, while Muslim’s wording is similar.

13312 — ʿĀʾishah narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ used to stand in prayer at night until his feet became cracked and swollen.
ʿĀʾishah asked:
“Why do you do this, O Messenger of Allah, when Allah has already forgiven you what preceded of your sin and what will follow?”
He replied:
“Should I not love to be a grateful servant?”
Later, when his body became heavier, he would pray while seated. Then, when he intended to bow, he would stand, complete his recitation, and then bow.

١٣٣١٣ — عن البراء بن عازب قال: قرأ رجل الكهف، وفي الدار الدابة، فجعلت تنفر، فسلَّم، فإذا ضبابة أو سحابة غشيته، فذكره للنبي ﷺ فقال:
((اقرأ فلان، فإنها السكينة نزلت للقرآن، أو تنزلت للقرآن)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٦١٤)، ومسلم (٧٩٥: ٢٤١)، واللفظ للبخاري.

13313 — Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib narrated:
A man was reciting Sūrat al-Kahf while there was an animal in the house, and it began to startle and move about.
The man stopped reciting, and suddenly a mist or cloud had enveloped him.
He mentioned this to the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
“Continue reciting, so-and-so, for that was tranquility which descended because of the Qur’an—or descended for the Qur’an.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3614) and Muslim (795:241). The wording is that of al-Bukhārī.

١٣٣١٤ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري، أن أسيد بن حضير بينما هو ليلة يقرأ في مربده، إذ جالت فرسه، فقرأ، ثم جالت أخرى، فقرأ، ثم جالت أيضًا.
قال أسيد: فخشيت أن تطأ يحيى، فقمت إليها، فإذا مثل الظلة فوق رأسي، فيها أمثال السرج، عرجت في الجو حتى ما أراها.
قال: فغدوت على رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فقلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، بينما أنا البارحة من جوف الليل أقرأ في مربدي، إذ جالت فرسي.
قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((اقرأ، ابن حضير)).
قال: فقرأت، ثم جالت أيضًا.
فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((اقرأ، ابن حضير)).
قال: فقرأت، ثم جالت أيضًا.
فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((اقرأ، ابن حضير)).
قال: فانصرفت - وكان يحيى قريبًا منها، خشيت أن تطأه - فرأيت مثل الظلة، فيها أمثال السرج، عرجت في الجو حتى ما أراها.
فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((تلك الملائكة كانت تستمع لك، ولو قرأت لأصبحت يراها الناس ما تستتر منهم)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٧٩٦).

13314 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrated:
One night, Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr was reciting in his enclosure when his horse suddenly became agitated.
He continued reciting, and the horse became agitated again. He continued reciting, and it became agitated yet again.
Usayd said:
I feared that it might trample Yaḥyā, so I went toward it.
Then I saw something like a canopy above my head, containing objects resembling lamps. It rose upward into the sky until I could no longer see it.
The next morning I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, last night, in the middle of the night, I was reciting in my enclosure when my horse became agitated.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Recite, Ibn Ḥuḍayr.”
I said:
“I continued reciting, and it became agitated again.”
He said:
“Recite, Ibn Ḥuḍayr.”
I said:
“I continued reciting, and it became agitated again.”
He said:
“Recite, Ibn Ḥuḍayr.”
I said:
I stopped because Yaḥyā was close to the horse and I feared that it might trample him. Then I saw something like a canopy containing objects resembling lamps, which rose into the sky until I could no longer see it.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Those were the angels listening to your recitation. Had you continued reciting until morning, the people would have seen them, and they would not have hidden themselves from them.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (796).

١٣٣١٥ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمرو بن العاص أن هذه الآية التي في القرآن: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ شَاهِدًا وَمُبَشِّرًا وَنَذِيرًا﴾ قال: في التوراة:
«يا أيها النبي، إنا أرسلناك شاهدًا ومبشرًا وحرزًا للأميين، أنت عبدي ورسولي، سميتك المتوكل، ليس بفظ ولا غليظ، ولا سخاب بالأسواق، ولا يدفع السيئة بالسيئة، ولكن يعفو ويصفح، ولن يقبضه اللّٰه حتى يقيم به الملة العوجاء بأن يقولوا: لا إله إلا اللّٰه، يفتح بها أعينًا عميًا، وآذانًا صمًا، وقلوبًا غلفًا».
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٤٨٣٨).

“Indeed, We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of glad tidings, and a warner,”
that in the Torah it states:

Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4838).

١٣٣١٦ — عن جابر قال: كنا يوم الحديبية ألفًا وأربعمائة، فبايعناه، وعمر آخذ بيده تحت شجرة، وهي سمرة، وقال: بايعناه على أن لا نفر، ولم نبايعه على الموت.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٨٥٦).

13316 — Jābir narrated:
On the Day of al-Ḥudaybiyyah we were fourteen hundred.
We pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ while ʿUmar was holding his hand beneath a tree, which was a samurah tree.
Jābir said:
“We pledged allegiance to him that we would not flee. We did not pledge allegiance to him specifically upon death.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1856).

١٣٣١٧ — عن يزيد بن أبي عبيد قال: قلت لسلمة بن الأكوع: على أي شيء بايعتم رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يوم الحديبية؟
قال: على الموت.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤١٦٩)، ومسلم (١٨٦٠: ٨٠).
قوله: «على الموت» وجاء في بعض الروايات: «بايعوه على الصبر وألا يفروا»، فمن قال: «على الموت» أراد لازمها، ومن قال: «على الصبر» فقد حكى الحقيقة.

english_source:
13317 — Yazīd ibn Abī ʿUbayd narrated:
I asked Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ:
“Upon what did you pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Day of al-Ḥudaybiyyah?”
He replied:
“Upon death.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4169) and Muslim (1860:80).
Regarding the phrase:
“Upon death,”
other narrations state:
“They pledged to remain steadfast and not flee.”
Whoever described the pledge as being “upon death” intended what steadfastness necessarily entailed: remaining firm even if it resulted in death.
Whoever described it as “upon steadfastness” stated the literal wording and reality of the pledge.

arabic_source:
١٣٣١٨ — عن عثمان بن موهب قال: جاء رجل حج البيت، فرأى قومًا جلوسًا، فقال: من هؤلاء القعود؟
قالوا: هؤلاء قريش.
قال: من الشيخ؟
قالوا: ابن عمر.
فأتى فقال: إني سائلك عن شيء، أتحدثني؟
قال: أنشدك بحرمة هذا البيت، أتعلم أن عثمان فر يوم أحد؟
قال: نعم.
قال: فتعلم أنه تغيب عن بدر فلم يشهدها؟
قال: نعم.
قال: فتعلم أنه تخلف عن بيعة الرضوان فلم يشهدها؟
قال: نعم.
قال: فكبر.
قال ابن عمر: تعال لأخبرك ولأبين لك عما سألتني عنه: أما فراره يوم أحد فأشهد أن اللّٰه عفا عنه.
وأما تغيبه عن بدر، فإنه كان تحته بنت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وكانت مريضة، فقال له النبي ﷺ:
((إن لك أجر رجل ممن شهد بدرًا وسهمه)).
وأما تغيبه عن بيعة الرضوان، فإنه لو كان أحد أعز ببطن مكة من عثمان بن عفان لبعثه مكانه، فبعث عثمان.
وكانت بيعة الرضوان بعد ما ذهب عثمان إلى مكة، فقال النبي ﷺ بيده اليمنى:
((هذه يد عثمان)).
فضرب بها على يده، فقال:
((هذه لعثمان)).
اذهب بهذا الآن معك.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٤٠٦٦).

13318 — ʿUthmān ibn Mawhab narrated:
A man came to perform Ḥajj at the Sacred House and saw a group of people sitting together.
He asked:
“Who are these people sitting here?”
They replied:
“They are from Quraysh.”
He asked:
“Who is the elderly man?”
They replied:
“Ibn ʿUmar.”
So he approached Ibn ʿUmar and said:
“I want to ask you about something. Will you tell me?”
He said:
“I adjure you by the sanctity of this House: do you know that ʿUthmān fled on the Day of Uḥud?”
Ibn ʿUmar replied:
“Yes.”
He asked:
“Do you know that he was absent from Badr and did not attend it?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
He asked:
“Do you know that he was absent from the Pledge of al-Riḍwān and did not attend it?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
The man exclaimed, “Allāhu akbar!”
Ibn ʿUmar then said:
“Come here, and I will explain to you what you have asked me about.
As for his fleeing on the Day of Uḥud, I testify that Allah pardoned him for it.
As for his absence from Badr, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was his wife, and she was ill. The Prophet ﷺ said to him:
‘You will have the reward and the share of a man who attended Badr.’
As for his absence from the Pledge of al-Riḍwān, had there been anyone in the valley of Makkah more respected than ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, the Prophet ﷺ would have sent that person instead. But he sent ʿUthmān.
The Pledge of al-Riḍwān took place after ʿUthmān had gone to Makkah.
The Prophet ﷺ then said, indicating with his right hand:
‘This is the hand of ʿUthmān.’
He struck his right hand upon his other hand and said:
‘This pledge is on behalf of ʿUthmān.’
Then Ibn ʿUmar said:
“Now take this explanation with you.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4066).

قال: أنشدك بحرمة هذا البيت، أتعلم أن عثمان فر يوم أحد؟
قال: نعم.
قال: فتعلم أنه تغيب عن بدر فلم يشهدها؟
قال: نعم.
قال: فتعلم أنه تخلف عن بيعة الرضوان فلم يشهدها؟
قال: نعم.
قال: فكبر.
قال ابن عمر: تعال لأخبرك ولأبين لك عما سألتني عنه: أما فراره يوم أحد فأشهد أن اللّٰه عفا عنه.
وأما تغيبه عن بدر، فإنه كان تحته بنت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وكانت مريضة، فقال له النبي ﷺ:
((إن لك أجر رجل ممن شهد بدرًا وسهمه)).
وأما تغيبه عن بيعة الرضوان، فإنه لو كان أحد أعز ببطن مكة من عثمان بن عفان لبعثه مكانه، فبعث عثمان.
وكانت بيعة الرضوان بعد ما ذهب عثمان إلى مكة، فقال النبي ﷺ بيده اليمنى:
((هذه يد عثمان)).
فضرب بها على يده، فقال:
((هذه لعثمان)).
اذهب بهذا الآن معك.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٤٠٦٦).
13318 — ʿUthmān ibn Mawhab narrated:
A man came to perform Ḥajj at the Sacred House and saw a group of people sitting together.
He asked:
“Who are these people sitting here?”
They replied:
“They are from Quraysh.”
He asked:
“Who is the elderly man?”
They replied:
“Ibn ʿUmar.”
So he approached Ibn ʿUmar and said:
“I want to ask you about something. Will you tell me?”
He said:
“I adjure you by the sanctity of this House: do you know that ʿUthmān fled on the Day of Uḥud?”
Ibn ʿUmar replied:
“Yes.”
He asked:
“Do you know that he was absent from Badr and did not attend it?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
He asked:
“Do you know that he was absent from the Pledge of al-Riḍwān and did not attend it?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
The man exclaimed, “Allāhu akbar!”
Ibn ʿUmar then said:
“Come here, and I will explain to you what you have asked me about.
As for his fleeing on the Day of Uḥud, I testify that Allah pardoned him for it.
As for his absence from Badr, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was his wife, and she was ill. The Prophet ﷺ said to him:
‘You will have the reward and the share of a man who attended Badr.’
As for his absence from the Pledge of al-Riḍwān, had there been anyone in the valley of Makkah more respected than ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, the Prophet ﷺ would have sent that person instead. But he sent ʿUthmān.
The Pledge of al-Riḍwān took place after ʿUthmān had gone to Makkah.
The Prophet ﷺ then said, indicating with his right hand:
‘This is the hand of ʿUthmān.’
He struck his right hand upon his other hand and said:
‘This pledge is on behalf of ʿUthmān.’
Then Ibn ʿUmar said:
“Now take this explanation with you.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4066).

١٣٣٢١ — عن جابر قال: كنا يوم الحديبية ألفًا وأربعمائة، فقال لنا النبي ﷺ:
((أنتم اليوم خير أهل الأرض)).
وقال جابر: لو كنت أبصر لأريتكم موضع الشجرة.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٨٤٠)، ومسلم (١٨٥٦: ٧١)، واللفظ لمسلم، والبخاري اقتصر على ذكر العدد فقط.

13321 — Jābir narrated:
We were fourteen hundred on the Day of al-Ḥudaybiyyah.
The Prophet ﷺ said to us:
“Today you are the best people upon the earth.”
Jābir said:
“Had I still been able to see, I would have shown you the location of the tree.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4840) and Muslim (1856:71). The wording is that of Muslim; al-Bukhārī mentioned only the number.

١٣٣٢٢ — عن طارق بن عبد الرحمن قال: انطلقت حاجًّا، فمررت بقوم يصلون، قلت: ما هذه؟
قالوا: هذه الشجرة، حيث بايع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بيعة الرضوان.
فأتيت سعيد بن المسيب فأخبرته.
فقال سعيد: حدثني أبي أنه كان فيمن بايع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ تحت الشجرة، قال: فلما خرجنا من العام المقبل نسيناها، فلم نقدر عليها.
فقال سعيد: إن أصحاب محمد ﷺ لم يعلموها وعلمتموها أنتم، فأنتم أعلم.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤١٦٣)، ومسلم (١٨٥٩: ٧٧).

13322 — Ṭāriq ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated:
I set out to perform Ḥajj and passed by some people who were praying.
I asked:
“What is this place?”
They replied:
“This is the tree where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ received the Pledge of al-Riḍwān.”
I then went to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib and told him.
Saʿīd said:
“My father narrated to me that he was among those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ beneath the tree.
When we returned the following year, we had forgotten its exact location and were unable to find it.”
Saʿīd then said sarcastically:
“The Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ did not know where it was, yet you have discovered it? Then you must know better!”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4163) and Muslim (1859:77).

فقال سعيد: حدثني أبي أنه كان فيمن بايع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ تحت الشجرة، قال: فلما خرجنا من العام المقبل نسيناها، فلم نقدر عليها.
فقال سعيد: إن أصحاب محمد ﷺ لم يعلموها وعلمتموها أنتم، فأنتم أعلم.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤١٦٣)، ومسلم (١٨٥٩: ٧٧).
13322 — Ṭāriq ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated:
I set out to perform Ḥajj and passed by some people who were praying.
I asked:
“What is this place?”
They replied:
“This is the tree where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ received the Pledge of al-Riḍwān.”
I then went to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib and told him.
Saʿīd said:
“My father narrated to me that he was among those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ beneath the tree.
When we returned the following year, we had forgotten its exact location and were unable to find it.”
Saʿīd then said sarcastically:
“The Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ did not know where it was, yet you have discovered it? Then you must know better!”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4163) and Muslim (1859:77).

صحيح: رواه ابن سعد في طبقاته (٢/١٠٠).
فقول سعيد بن المسيب: «إن أصحاب محمد ﷺ لم يعلموها وعلمتموها أنتم، فأنتم أعلم»، فيه إنكار وتهكم، فإن الشجرة قد أمر بقطعها عمر بن الخطاب، فأين هي الآن؟ وأما مكان الشجرة فكان جابر بن عبد اللّٰه يضبطه، ولكنه عمي فلم يستطع أن يدل عليه.

People used to come to a tree that was said to be the Tree of al-Riḍwān and pray near it.

“The Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ did not know it, while you know it, so you must know better,”

arabic_source:
١٣٣٢٤ — عن جويرية، عن نافع قال: قال ابن عمر: رجعنا من العام المقبل، فما اجتمع منا اثنان على الشجرة التي بايعنا تحتها، كانت رحمة من اللّٰه.
فسألت نافعًا: على أي شيء بايعهم؟ على الموت؟
قال: لا، بل بايعهم على الصبر.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٩٥٨).
قوله: «كانت رحمة من اللّٰه» أي: كان خفاء هذه الشجرة رحمة لئلا يفتن بها الناس أن هذه الشجرة لها قوة نفع أو ضر.

english_source:
13324 — Juwayriyah narrated from Nāfiʿ that Ibn ʿUmar said:
“We returned the following year, yet no two of us could agree upon which tree it was beneath which we had pledged allegiance. That was a mercy from Allah.”
I asked Nāfiʿ:
“Upon what did the Prophet ﷺ take their pledge? Was it upon death?”
He replied:
“No. Rather, he took their pledge upon steadfastness.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2958).
Regarding Ibn ʿUmar’s words:
“That was a mercy from Allah,”
the meaning is that the disappearance and uncertainty surrounding the tree was a mercy, lest people become tested by it and begin believing that the tree itself possessed some power to benefit or harm.

١٣٣٢٥ — عن جابر بن عبد اللّٰه يقول: أخبرتني أم مبشر أنها سمعت النبي ﷺ يقول عند حفصة:
((لا يدخل النار - إن شاء اللّٰه - من أصحاب الشجرة أحد الذين بايعوا تحتها)).
قالت: بلى يا رسول اللّٰه. فانتهرها.
فقالت حفصة: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وَارِدُهَا﴾ [مريم: ٧١].
فقال النبي ﷺ:
((قد قال اللّٰه عز وجل: ﴿ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا وَنَذَرُ الظَّالِمِينَ فِيهَا جِثِيًّا﴾)) [مريم: ٧٢].
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٤٩٦).

13325 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated:
Umm Mubashshir informed me that she heard the Prophet ﷺ say in the presence of Ḥafṣah:
“None of those who pledged allegiance beneath the Tree will enter the Fire, if Allah wills.”
Ḥafṣah said:
“But yes, O Messenger of Allah.”
He rebuked her.
She then recited:
“There is none among you except that he will come to it.” [Sūrat Maryam 19:71]
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has also said: ‘Then We will save those who were mindful of Allah and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees.’” [Sūrat Maryam 19:72]
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2496).

١٣٣٢٦ — عن جابر أن عبدًا لحاطب جاء رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يشكو حاطبًا، فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، ليدخلن حاطب النار.
فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((كذبت، لا يدخلها؛ فإنه شهد بدرًا والحديبية)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٤٩٥).

13326 — Jābir narrated:
A slave belonging to Ḥāṭib came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ complaining about Ḥāṭib and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, Ḥāṭib will certainly enter the Fire.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied:
“You are wrong. He will not enter it, for he witnessed Badr and al-Ḥudaybiyyah.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2495).

A slave belonging to Ḥāṭib came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ complaining about Ḥāṭib and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, Ḥāṭib will certainly enter the Fire.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied:
“You are wrong. He will not enter it, for he witnessed Badr and al-Ḥudaybiyyah.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2495).

13327 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
Eighty armed men from Makkah descended upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the mountain of al-Tanʿīm, intending to take the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions by surprise.
The Muslims captured them, but the Prophet ﷺ spared their lives.
Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed:
“He is the One who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah, after He had given you victory over them.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1808).
Regarding the word “salan”, al-Nawawī said that it has been transmitted with two vocalizations: with both the sīn and lām open, and with the lām silent while the sīn is either kasrah or fatḥah.
Al-Ḥumaydī said that it means “peace” or “truce.”
Al-Qāḍī said that most scholars vocalized it in this way, though the first reading is clearer, meaning that they were captured.
Al-Khaṭṭābī decisively read it with both the sīn and lām open and said that it means submission and yielding, as in Allah’s words:
“And they offer you peace.” [Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:90]
meaning submission. It is a verbal noun that can apply to one person, two people, or a group.
Ibn al-Athīr said:
“This interpretation best fits the account, for they were not captured through a peace treaty. Rather, they were taken by force and surrendered themselves because they were unable to resist.”

١٣٣٢٨ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن مغفل المزني قال: كنا مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بالحديبية في أصل الشجرة التي قال اللّٰه تعالى في القرآن، وكان يقع من أغصان تلك الشجرة على ظهر رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، وعلي بن أبي طالب وسهيل بن عمرو بين يديه.
فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ لعلي:
((اكتب: بسم اللّٰه الرحمن الرحيم)).
فأخذ سهيل بن عمرو بيده، فقال: ما نعرف الرحمن الرحيم، اكتب في قضيتنا ما نعرف.
قال:
((اكتب: باسمك اللهم)).
فكتب: هذا ما صالح عليه محمد رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أهل مكة.
فأمسك سهيل بن عمرو بيده، وقال: لقد ظلمناك إن كنت رسوله، اكتب في قضيتنا ما نعرف.
فقال:
((اكتب: هذا ما صالح عليه محمد بن عبد اللّٰه بن عبد المطلب، وأنا رسول اللّٰه)).
فكتب.
فبينا نحن كذلك إذ خرج علينا ثلاثون شابًا عليهم السلاح، فثاروا في وجوهنا، فدعا عليهم رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فأخذ اللّٰه عز وجل بأبصارهم، فقدمنا إليهم فأخذناهم.
فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((هل جئتم في عهد أحد، أو هل جعل لكم أحد أمانًا؟)).
فقالوا: لا.
فخلى سبيلهم، فأنزل اللّٰه عز وجل: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي كَفَّ أَيْدِيَهُمْ عَنْكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ بِبَطْنِ مَكَّةَ مِنْ بَعْدِ أَنْ أَظْفَرَكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرًا﴾.
حسن: رواه أحمد (١٦٨٠٠)، والنسائي في الكبرى (١١٤٤٧)، وصححه الحاكم (٢/٤٦٠-٤٦١).

13328 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Mughaffal al-Muzanī narrated:
We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Ḥudaybiyyah beneath the tree mentioned by Allah in the Qur’an.
Some of its branches were hanging over the back of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and Suhayl ibn ʿAmr were before him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to ʿAlī:
“Write: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.”
Suhayl ibn ʿAmr took hold of his hand and said:
“We do not recognize ‘the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.’ Write in our agreement what we recognize.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Write: In Your name, O Allah.”
So he wrote:
“This is what Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, has agreed upon with the people of Makkah.”
Suhayl ibn ʿAmr again took hold of his hand and said:
“We would indeed have wronged you if you truly were His Messenger. Write in our agreement what we recognize.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Write: This is what Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib has agreed upon—and I am the Messenger of Allah.”
So he wrote it.
While we were in that situation, thirty armed young men suddenly came out against us and rushed toward us.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ supplicated against them, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, took away their sight.
We advanced toward them and captured them.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked:
“Have you come under anyone’s covenant, or has anyone granted you protection?”
They replied:
“No.”
So he released them.
Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed:
“He is the One who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah, after He had given you victory over them. And Allah sees all that you do.”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (16800), al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (11447), and authenticated by al-Ḥākim (2/460–461).

فبينا نحن كذلك إذ خرج علينا ثلاثون شابًا عليهم السلاح، فثاروا في وجوهنا، فدعا عليهم رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فأخذ اللّٰه عز وجل بأبصارهم، فقدمنا إليهم فأخذناهم.

13328 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Mughaffal al-Muzanī narrated:
We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Ḥudaybiyyah beneath the tree mentioned by Allah in the Qur’an.
Some of its branches were hanging over the back of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and Suhayl ibn ʿAmr were before him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to ʿAlī:
“Write: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.”
Suhayl ibn ʿAmr took hold of his hand and said:
“We do not recognize ‘the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.’ Write in our agreement what we recognize.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Write: In Your name, O Allah.”
So he wrote:
“This is what Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, has agreed upon with the people of Makkah.”
Suhayl ibn ʿAmr again took hold of his hand and said:
“We would indeed have wronged you if you truly were His Messenger. Write in our agreement what we recognize.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Write: This is what Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib has agreed upon—and I am the Messenger of Allah.”
So he wrote it.
While we were in that situation, thirty armed young men suddenly came out against us and rushed toward us.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ supplicated against them, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, took away their sight.
We advanced toward them and captured them.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked:
“Have you come under anyone’s covenant, or has anyone granted you protection?”
They replied:
“No.”
So he released them.
Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed:
“He is the One who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah, after He had given you victory over them. And Allah sees all that you do.”

((اكتب: باسمك اللهم)).

١٣٣٢٩ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
((أنزل اللّٰه تعالى في كتابه فذكر قومًا استكبروا، فقال: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا إِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ [الصافات: ٣٥]، وقال تعالى: ﴿إِذْ جَعَلَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْحَمِيَّةَ حَمِيَّةَ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِ وَعَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَأَلْزَمَهُمْ كَلِمَةَ التَّقْوَىٰ وَكَانُوا أَحَقَّ بِهَا وَأَهْلَهَا﴾، وهي: لا إله إلا اللّٰه، محمد رسول اللّٰه، استكبر عنها المشركون يوم الحديبية، يوم كاتبهم رسول اللّٰه ﷺ في قضية المدة)).

13329 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Allah, the Exalted, revealed in His Book concerning a people who behaved arrogantly:
‘Indeed, whenever it was said to them, “There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah,” they would act arrogantly.’ [Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt 37:35]
And Allah, the Exalted, said:
‘When those who disbelieved placed within their hearts the pride of ignorance, Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and bound them firmly to the word of God-consciousness, and they were more deserving of it and worthy of it.’
The word of God-consciousness is: ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah; Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah.’ The polytheists acted arrogantly toward it on the Day of al-Ḥudaybiyyah, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was writing the agreement with them concerning the truce.”
Authentic: Narrated by Ibn Abī Ḥātim, as cited by Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr (7/345), Ibn Ḥibbān (218), and al-Bayhaqī in al-Asmāʾ wa-al-Ṣifāt (195, 196).

١٣٣٣٠ — عن ابن عمر: أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ خرج معتمرًا، فحال كفار قريش بينه وبين البيت، فنحر هديه وحلق رأسه بالحديبية، وقاضاهم على أن يعتمر العام المقبل، ولا يحمل سلاحًا عليهم إلا سيوفًا، ولا يقيم بها إلا ما أحبوا.
فاعتمر من العام المقبل، فدخلها كما كان صالحهم، فلما أن أقام بها ثلاثًا أمروه أن يخرج، فخرج.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٤٢٥٢).

13330 — Ibn ʿUmar narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out intending to perform ʿUmrah, but the disbelievers of Quraysh prevented him from reaching the House.
So he slaughtered his sacrificial animals and shaved his head at al-Ḥudaybiyyah.
He made an agreement with them that he would perform ʿUmrah the following year, that he would not bring weapons against them except swords, and that he would remain in Makkah only for as long as they permitted.
The following year he performed ʿUmrah and entered Makkah in accordance with the agreement.
After remaining there for three days, they ordered him to leave, so he departed.
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4252).

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out intending to perform ʿUmrah, but the disbelievers of Quraysh prevented him from reaching the House.
So he slaughtered his sacrificial animals and shaved his head at al-Ḥudaybiyyah.
He made an agreement with them that he would perform ʿUmrah the following year, that he would not bring weapons against them except swords, and that he would remain in Makkah only for as long as they permitted.
The following year he performed ʿUmrah and entered Makkah in accordance with the agreement.
After remaining there for three days, they ordered him to leave, so he departed.
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4252).

13331 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions arrived in Makkah after the fever of Yathrib had weakened them.
The polytheists said:
“Tomorrow there will come to you a people who have been weakened by fever and have suffered greatly from it.”
So they sat on the side facing al-Ḥijr.
The Prophet ﷺ instructed his Companions to walk briskly with short, quick steps during the first three circuits of ṭawāf and to walk normally between the two corners, so that the polytheists could see their strength.
The polytheists said:
“Are these the people you claimed had been weakened by fever? These people are stronger than such-and-such!”
Ibn ʿAbbās said:
“Nothing prevented the Prophet ﷺ from ordering them to perform the brisk walk during all the circuits except his concern to spare them hardship.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4256) and Muslim (1266:240).

“With your heads shaved and your hair shortened”:

13333 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“O Allah, have mercy on those who shave their heads.”
They said:
“And those who shorten their hair, O Messenger of Allah?”
He said:
“O Allah, have mercy on those who shave their heads.”
They again said:
“And those who shorten their hair, O Messenger of Allah?”
He then said:
“And those who shorten their hair.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Mālik in Kitāb al-Ḥajj (184), al-Bukhārī (1727), and Muslim (1301:317).

“Do not insult my Companions. Do not insult my Companions. By the One in Whose hand is my soul, if one of you were to spend in charity an amount of gold equal to Mount Uḥud, he would not attain the reward of even one mudd given by one of them, nor even half of it.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2540).

١٣٣٣٥ — عن عائشة قالت: سأل رجل النبي ﷺ: أي الناس خير؟
قال:
((القرن الذي أنا فيه، ثم الثاني، ثم الثالث)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٥٣٦).
ومن عقيدة أهل السنة والجماعة أن الصحابة كلهم عدول، أي: لا يتعمدون الكذب على رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، لا أنهم لا يسهون ولا يخطئون، وكلهم من أهل الجنة، فإذا صدر من أحدهم الهفوات فيبادرون إلى التوبة والاستغفار.

english_source:
13335 — ʿĀʾishah narrated:
A man asked the Prophet ﷺ:
“Which people are the best?”
He replied:
“The generation in which I live, then the second, then the third.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2536).
Among the beliefs of Ahl al-Sunnah wa’l-Jamāʿah is that all of the Companions are upright and trustworthy.
This means that they did not deliberately lie about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; it does not mean that they were incapable of forgetfulness or error.
All of them are among the people of Paradise, and if any slips occurred from any of them, they hastened to repentance and seeking forgiveness.

Among the beliefs of Ahl al-Sunnah wa’l-Jamāʿah is that all of the Companions are upright and trustworthy.
This means that they did not deliberately lie about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; it does not mean that they were incapable of forgetfulness or error.
All of them are among the people of Paradise, and if any slips occurred from any of them, they hastened to repentance and seeking forgiveness.

قال نافع: لا أحفظ اسمه.
فقال أبو بكر لعمر: ما أردت إلا خلافي.
قال: ما أردت خلافك.
فارتفعت أصواتهما في ذلك، فأنزل اللّٰه: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَرْفَعُوا أَصْوَاتَكُمْ﴾ الآية.
قال ابن الزبير: فما كان عمر يسمع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بعد هذه الآية حتى يستفهمه. ولم يذكر ذلك عن أبيه، يعني أبا بكر.

13337 — Ibn Abī Mulaykah narrated:
The two best men, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, nearly brought ruin upon themselves when they raised their voices in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ after a delegation of Banū Tamīm came to him.
One of them suggested al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis, the brother of Banū Mujāshiʿ, while the other suggested another man.
Nāfiʿ said:
“I do not remember his name.”
Abū Bakr said to ʿUmar:
“You only intended to oppose me.”
ʿUmar replied:
“I did not intend to oppose you.”
Their voices rose during the disagreement.
Then Allah revealed:
“O you who believe, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet…”
Ibn al-Zubayr said:
“After this verse, ʿUmar would speak so softly to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that the Prophet ﷺ sometimes had to ask him to repeat himself.”
He did not mention the same concerning his father, Abū Bakr.
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4845).

((يا أبا عمرو، ما شأن ثابت؟ اشتكى؟)).

قال: فأتاه سعد، فذكر له قول رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فقال ثابت: أنزلت هذه الآية، ولقد علمتم أني من أرفعكم صوتًا على رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فأنا من أهل النار.
فذكر ذلك سعد للنبي ﷺ، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:

13338 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
When this verse was revealed:
“O you who believe, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet…”
to the end of the verse, Thābit ibn Qays remained inside his house and said:
“I am among the people of the Fire.”
He stayed away from the Prophet ﷺ.
The Prophet ﷺ asked Saʿd ibn Muʿādh:
“Abū ʿAmr, what is the matter with Thābit? Is he ill?”
Saʿd replied:
“He is my neighbor, and I do not know of him having any illness.”
Saʿd went to him and told him what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said.
Thābit replied:
“This verse has been revealed, and you know that I am among those with the loudest voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Therefore I am among the people of the Fire.”
Saʿd reported this to the Prophet ﷺ.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Rather, he is among the people of Paradise.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Muslim (119) and al-Bukhārī (4846).

متفق عليه: رواه مسلم (١١٩)، والبخاري (٤٨٤٦).
13338 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
When this verse was revealed:
“O you who believe, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet…”
to the end of the verse, Thābit ibn Qays remained inside his house and said:
“I am among the people of the Fire.”
He stayed away from the Prophet ﷺ.
The Prophet ﷺ asked Saʿd ibn Muʿādh:
“Abū ʿAmr, what is the matter with Thābit? Is he ill?”
Saʿd replied:
“He is my neighbor, and I do not know of him having any illness.”
Saʿd went to him and told him what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said.
Thābit replied:
“This verse has been revealed, and you know that I am among those with the loudest voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Therefore I am among the people of the Fire.”
Saʿd reported this to the Prophet ﷺ.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Rather, he is among the people of Paradise.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Muslim (119) and al-Bukhārī (4846).

13339 — Anas narrated:
When the verse was revealed:
“O you who believe, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet…”
until:
“…while you do not realize it,”
Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās was a man with a naturally loud voice.
He said:
“I am the one who used to raise my voice in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. My deeds have become worthless. I am among the people of the Fire.”
He remained with his family in sadness.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ noticed his absence, so some of the people went to him and said:
“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has noticed your absence. What is wrong with you?”
He replied:
“I am the one who raises his voice above the voice of the Prophet ﷺ and speaks loudly. My deeds have become worthless, and I am among the people of the Fire.”
They returned to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of what Thābit had said.
He replied:
“No. Rather, he is among the people of Paradise.”
Anas said:
“After that, we would see him walking among us while knowing that he was one of the people of Paradise.”
When the Day of al-Yamāmah came and there was some retreat among the Muslims, Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās came forward after having applied perfume used in preparation for death and put on his shroud.
He said:
“How evil is what you are accustoming your opponents to!”
Then he fought them until he was killed.
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (12399) and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (7168).
Al-Bukhārī narrated in the Book of Prayer (470), through his chain from al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd, who said:
I was standing in the mosque when a man threw a small pebble at me.
I looked and saw that it was ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.
He said:
“Go and bring those two men to me.”
So I brought them to him.
He asked:
“Who are you two?” or, “Where are you from?”
They replied:
“We are from al-Ṭāʾif.”
He said:
“Had you been from the people of this city, I would have punished you severely. You are raising your voices in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!”

13340 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
When the verse was revealed:
“Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah…”
Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq said:
“By the One who revealed the Book to you, O Messenger of Allah, I will speak to you only as one speaking privately and softly until I meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”
Good: Narrated by al-Ḥākim (2/461) and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-Īmān (1431).

١٣٣٤١ — عن البراء بن عازب في قوله تعالى: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُنَادُونَكَ مِنْ وَرَاءِ الْحُجُرَاتِ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ قال: قام رجل فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، إن حمدي زين، وإن ذمي شين.
فقال النبي ﷺ:
((ذاك اللّٰه عز وجل)).

١٣٣٤٢ — عن عبيد بن رفاعة الزرقي، عن أبيه قال: لما كان يوم أحد، وانكفأ المشركون، قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((استووا حتى أثني على ربي عز وجل)).
فصاروا خلفه صفوفًا، فقال:
((اللهم لك الحمد كله، اللهم لا قابض لما بسطت، ولا مقرب لما باعدت، ولا مباعد لما قربت، ولا معطي لما منعت، ولا مانع لما أعطيت. اللهم ابسط علينا من بركاتك ورحمتك وفضلك ورزقك، اللهم إني أسألك النعيم المقيم الذي لا يحول ولا يزول، اللهم إني أسألك النعيم يوم العيلة، والأمن يوم الحرب، اللهم عائذًا بك من سوء ما أعطيتنا، وشر ما منعت منا. اللهم حبب إلينا الإيمان وزينه في قلوبنا، وكره إلينا الكفر والفسوق والعصيان، واجعلنا من الراشدين، اللهم توفنا مسلمين، وأحينا مسلمين، وألحقنا بالصالحين، غير خزايا ولا مفتونين، اللهم قاتل الكفرة الذين يصدون عن سبيلك ويكذبون رسلك، واجعل عليهم رجزك وعذابك، اللهم قاتل الكفرة الذين أوتوا الكتاب، إله الحق)).
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٥٤٩٢)، والبخاري في الأدب المفرد (٦٩٩)، والبزار - كشف الأستار (١٨٠٠)، والحاكم (١/٥٠٦-٥٠٧).

english_source:
13342 — ʿUbayd ibn Rifāʿah al-Zuraqī narrated from his father:
On the Day of Uḥud, after the polytheists had withdrawn, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Form straight rows so that I may praise my Lord, Mighty and Majestic.”
They formed rows behind him, and he said:
“O Allah, all praise belongs to You. O Allah, none can withhold what You expand, none can bring near what You distance, none can distance what You bring near, none can give what You withhold, and none can withhold what You give.
O Allah, spread upon us Your blessings, Your mercy, Your bounty, and Your provision. O Allah, I ask You for lasting bliss that neither changes nor disappears. O Allah, I ask You for bliss on the day of poverty and security on the day of war.
O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of what You have given us and from the evil of what You have withheld from us. O Allah, make faith beloved to us and beautify it within our hearts, and make disbelief, sinfulness, and disobedience hateful to us, and make us among the rightly guided.
O Allah, cause us to die as Muslims, keep us alive as Muslims, and join us with the righteous, neither disgraced nor put to trial.
O Allah, fight the disbelievers who turn people away from Your path and reject Your messengers, and send upon them Your punishment and chastisement. O Allah, fight the disbelievers who were given the Book, O God of Truth.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (15492), al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (699), al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (1800), and al-Ḥākim (1/506–507).

١٣٣٤٣ — عن ابن عمر أن عمر بن الخطاب خطب بالجابية، فقال: قام فينا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ مقامي فيكم، فقال:
((…ومن سرته حسنته وساءته سيئته فهو مؤمن)).
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١١٤)، وابن حبان (٧٢٥٤)، والحاكم (١/١١٣).

13343 — Ibn ʿUmar narrated:
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb delivered a sermon at al-Jābiyah and said:
“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ once stood among us just as I am standing among you and said:
‘…Whoever is pleased by his good deed and saddened by his bad deed is a believer.’”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (114), Ibn Ḥibbān (7254), and al-Ḥākim (1/113).

١٣٣٤٤ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: قيل للنبي ﷺ: لو أتيت عبد اللّٰه بن أبي؟ قال: فانطلق إليه، وركب حمارًا، وانطلق المسلمون، وهي أرض سبخة، فلما أتاه النبي ﷺ قال: إليك عني، فواللّٰه لقد آذاني نتن حمارك.
قال: فقال رجل من الأنصار: واللّٰه لحمار رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أطيب ريحًا منك.
قال: فغضب لعبد اللّٰه رجل من قومه. قال: فغضب لكل واحد منهما أصحابه. قال: فكان بينهم ضرب بالجريد وبالأيدي وبالنعال.
قال: فبلغنا أنها نزلت فيهم: ﴿وَإِنْ طَائِفَتَانِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ اقْتَتَلُوا فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُمَا﴾.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٦٩١)، ومسلم (١٧٩٩).
قوله: ﴿وَإِنْ طَائِفَتَانِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ اقْتَتَلُوا فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُمَا﴾، في هذه الآية وما بعدها أن البغي لا يزيل اسم الإيمان؛ لأن اللّٰه سماهم إخوة مؤمنين مع كونهم باغين، والباغي هو الخارج عن الإمام العدل.
وقد عمل به الحسن بن علي بن أبي طالب، وأصلح بين فئتين عظيمتين من المسلمين كما جاء في الصحيح:

13344 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
It was said to the Prophet ﷺ:
“If only you would go to ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy.”
So the Prophet ﷺ went to him riding a donkey, and the Muslims accompanied him. The ground was saline and marshy.
When the Prophet ﷺ reached him, ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy said:
“Keep away from me. By Allah, the stench of your donkey has offended me.”
A man from the Anṣār replied:
“By Allah, the donkey of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ smells better than you.”
A man from ʿAbdullāh’s people became angry on his behalf, and the supporters of each man became angry for him. They began striking one another with palm branches, their hands, and sandals.
Anas said:
“It reached us that concerning them the verse was revealed:
‘If two groups of the believers fight one another, then make peace between them.’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2691) and Muslim (1799).
Regarding the words:
“If two groups of the believers fight one another, then make peace between them,”
this verse and what follows indicate that wrongful rebellion does not remove the name of faith from a person, because Allah still called them believing brothers despite the presence of transgression.
The bāghī is one who rebels against the just ruler.
Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib acted upon this principle and brought reconciliation between two great groups of Muslims, as stated in the authentic hadith:

١٣٣٤٥ — عن أبي موسى قال: سمعت الحسن يقول: استقبل واللّٰه الحسن بن علي معاوية كتائب أمثال الجبال، فقال عمرو بن العاص: إني لأرى كتائب لا تولي حتى تقتل أقرانها.
فقال له معاوية - وكان واللّٰه خير الرجلين -: أي عمرو، إن قتل هؤلاء هؤلاء، وهؤلاء هؤلاء، من لي بأمور الناس؟ من لي بنسائهم؟ من لي بضيعتهم؟
فبعث إليه رجلين من قريش من بني عبد شمس: عبد الرحمن بن سمرة وعبد اللّٰه بن عامر بن كريز، فقال: اذهبا إلى هذا الرجل، فاعرضا عليه، وقولا له، واطلبا إليه.
فأتياه، فدخلا عليه، فتكلما، وقالا له، فطلبا إليه.
فقال لهما الحسن بن علي: إنا بنو عبد المطلب، قد أصبنا من هذا المال، وإن هذه الأمة قد عاثت في دمائها.
قالا: فإنه يعرض عليك كذا وكذا، ويطلب إليك ويسألك.
قال: فمن لي بهذا؟
قالا: نحن لك به.
فما سألهما شيئًا إلا قالا: نحن لك به. فصالحه.
فقال الحسن: ولقد سمعت أبا بكرة يقول: رأيت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ على المنبر، والحسن بن علي إلى جنبه، وهو يقبل على الناس مرة وعليه أخرى، ويقول:
((إن ابني هذا سيد، ولعل اللّٰه أن يصلح به بين فئتين عظيمتين من المسلمين)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٧٠٤).
وقوله: ﴿فَإِنْ بَغَتْ إِحْدَاهُمَا عَلَى الْأُخْرَىٰ فَقَاتِلُوا الَّتِي تَبْغِي حَتَّىٰ تَفِيءَ إِلَىٰ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ﴾:

13345 — Abū Mūsā narrated:
I heard al-Ḥasan say:
By Allah, al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī confronted Muʿāwiyah with battalions resembling mountains.
ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said:
“I see battalions that will not retreat until they kill their counterparts.”
Muʿāwiyah—who, by Allah, was the better of the two men—said to him:
“ʿAmr, if these kill those and those kill these, who will take care of the affairs of the people? Who will take care of their women? Who will take care of their dependents and property?”
He sent two men from Quraysh, from Banū ʿAbd Shams, to al-Ḥasan: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samurah and ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿĀmir ibn Kurayz.
He said:
“Go to this man, make him an offer, speak to him, and ask him to accept.”
They went to al-Ḥasan, entered upon him, spoke to him, and made their request.
Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī said:
“We are Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, and we have acquired some of this wealth, while this Ummah has been spilling one another’s blood.”
They said:
“He offers you such-and-such and asks this of you.”
Al-Ḥasan asked:
“Who will guarantee this for me?”
They replied:
“We will guarantee it for you.”
Whatever he asked of them, they said:
“We guarantee it for you.”
So he made peace with Muʿāwiyah.
Al-Ḥasan then said:
I heard Abū Bakrah say:
I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the pulpit with al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī beside him. He would turn toward the people at one moment and toward al-Ḥasan at another, saying:
“This son of mine is a leader, and perhaps Allah will bring reconciliation through him between two great groups of Muslims.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2704).
Regarding the words:
“If one of them transgresses against the other, then fight the one that transgresses until it returns to the command of Allah”:

I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the pulpit with al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī beside him. He would turn toward the people at one moment and toward al-Ḥasan at another, saying:
“This son of mine is a leader, and perhaps Allah will bring reconciliation through him between two great groups of Muslims.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2704).
Regarding the words:
“If one of them transgresses against the other, then fight the one that transgresses until it returns to the command of Allah”:

١٣٣٤٥ — عن أبي موسى قال: سمعت الحسن يقول: استقبل واللّٰه الحسن بن علي معاوية كتائب أمثال الجبال، فقال عمرو بن العاص: إني لأرى كتائب لا تولي حتى تقتل أقرانها.
فقال له معاوية - وكان واللّٰه خير الرجلين -: أي عمرو، إن قتل هؤلاء هؤلاء، وهؤلاء هؤلاء، من لي بأمور الناس؟ من لي بنسائهم؟ من لي بضيعتهم؟
فبعث إليه رجلين من قريش من بني عبد شمس: عبد الرحمن بن سمرة وعبد اللّٰه بن عامر بن كريز، فقال: اذهبا إلى هذا الرجل، فاعرضا عليه، وقولا له، واطلبا إليه.
فأتياه، فدخلا عليه، فتكلما، وقالا له، فطلبا إليه.
فقال لهما الحسن بن علي: إنا بنو عبد المطلب، قد أصبنا من هذا المال، وإن هذه الأمة قد عاثت في دمائها.
قالا: فإنه يعرض عليك كذا وكذا، ويطلب إليك ويسألك.
قال: فمن لي بهذا؟
قالا: نحن لك به.
فما سألهما شيئًا إلا قالا: نحن لك به. فصالحه.
فقال الحسن: ولقد سمعت أبا بكرة يقول: رأيت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ على المنبر، والحسن بن علي إلى جنبه، وهو يقبل على الناس مرة وعليه أخرى، ويقول:
((إن ابني هذا سيد، ولعل اللّٰه أن يصلح به بين فئتين عظيمتين من المسلمين)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٧٠٤).
وقوله: ﴿فَإِنْ بَغَتْ إِحْدَاهُمَا عَلَى الْأُخْرَىٰ فَقَاتِلُوا الَّتِي تَبْغِي حَتَّىٰ تَفِيءَ إِلَىٰ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ﴾:
13345 — Abū Mūsā narrated:
I heard al-Ḥasan say:
By Allah, al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī confronted Muʿāwiyah with battalions resembling mountains.
ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said:
“I see battalions that will not retreat until they kill their counterparts.”
Muʿāwiyah—who, by Allah, was the better of the two men—said to him:
“ʿAmr, if these kill those and those kill these, who will take care of the affairs of the people? Who will take care of their women? Who will take care of their dependents and property?”
He sent two men from Quraysh, from Banū ʿAbd Shams, to al-Ḥasan: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samurah and ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿĀmir ibn Kurayz.
He said:
“Go to this man, make him an offer, speak to him, and ask him to accept.”
They went to al-Ḥasan, entered upon him, spoke to him, and made their request.
Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī said:
“We are Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, and we have acquired some of this wealth, while this Ummah has been spilling one another’s blood.”
They said:
“He offers you such-and-such and asks this of you.”
Al-Ḥasan asked:
“Who will guarantee this for me?”
They replied:
“We will guarantee it for you.”
Whatever he asked of them, they said:
“We guarantee it for you.”
So he made peace with Muʿāwiyah.
Al-Ḥasan then said:
I heard Abū Bakrah say:
I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the pulpit with al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī beside him. He would turn toward the people at one moment and toward al-Ḥasan at another, saying:
“This son of mine is a leader, and perhaps Allah will bring reconciliation through him between two great groups of Muslims.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2704).
Regarding the words:
“If one of them transgresses against the other, then fight the one that transgresses until it returns to the command of Allah”:

“Support your brother whether he is an oppressor or oppressed.”
They asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, we understand supporting him when he is oppressed, but how do we support him when he is an oppressor?”
He replied:
“You restrain his hands from oppression.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2444).

“And act justly. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly”:

١٣٣٤٧ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمرو قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((إن المقسطين عند اللّٰه على منابر من نور، عن يمين الرحمن عز وجل، وكلتا يديه يمين، الذين يعدلون في حكمهم وأهليهم وما ولوا)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٨٢٧).
وقوله: ﴿إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ إِخْوَةٌ﴾، وهذه الأخوة حقوق ومتطلبات ومقتضيات ينبغي لكل مؤمن أن يقوم بها على أحسن وجه.

13347 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Indeed, those who act justly will be with Allah upon pulpits of light, at the right hand of the Most Merciful, Mighty and Majestic—and both of His hands are right—those who are just in their judgments, toward their families, and in whatever they are entrusted with.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1827).
Regarding the words:
“The believers are but brothers,”
this brotherhood entails rights, responsibilities, and duties that every believer should fulfill in the best possible manner.

١٣٣٤٨ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمر أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال:
((المسلم أخو المسلم، لا يظلمه ولا يسلمه، ومن كان في حاجة أخيه كان اللّٰه في حاجته، ومن فرج عن مسلم كربة فرج اللّٰه عنه كربة من كربات يوم القيامة، ومن ستر مسلمًا ستره اللّٰه يوم القيامة)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٤٤٢)، ومسلم (٢٥٨٠).

13348 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim. He does not wrong him nor abandon him. Whoever attends to the need of his brother, Allah will attend to his need. Whoever relieves a Muslim of a hardship, Allah will relieve him of one of the hardships of the Day of Resurrection. And whoever conceals the faults of a Muslim, Allah will conceal his faults on the Day of Resurrection.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2442) and Muslim (2580).

13350 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever relieves a believer of one of the hardships of this world, Allah will relieve him of one of the hardships of the Day of Resurrection. Whoever makes things easy for someone in difficulty, Allah will make things easy for him in this world and the Hereafter. Whoever conceals the faults of a Muslim, Allah will conceal his faults in this world and the Hereafter. Allah continues to help the servant for as long as the servant continues to help his brother…”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2699).

١٣٣٥٠ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((من نفس عن مؤمن كربة من كرب الدنيا نفس اللّٰه عنه كربة من كرب يوم القيامة، ومن يسر على معسر يسر اللّٰه عليه في الدنيا والآخرة، ومن ستر مسلمًا ستره اللّٰه في الدنيا والآخرة، واللّٰه في عون العبد ما كان العبد في عون أخيه…)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٦٩٩).
13350 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever relieves a believer of one of the hardships of this world, Allah will relieve him of one of the hardships of the Day of Resurrection. Whoever makes things easy for someone in difficulty, Allah will make things easy for him in this world and the Hereafter. Whoever conceals the faults of a Muslim, Allah will conceal his faults in this world and the Hereafter. Allah continues to help the servant for as long as the servant continues to help his brother…”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2699).

((المؤمن للمؤمن كالبنيان يشد بعضه بعضًا)).
وشبك بين أصابعه.

“The believer in relation to another believer is like a building, each part strengthening the other.”
He then interlaced his fingers.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2446) and Muslim (2585).

١٣٣٥٢ — عن النعمان بن بشير قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((مثل المؤمنين في توادهم وتراحمهم وتعاطفهم مثل الجسد، إذا اشتكى منه عضو تداعى له سائر الجسد بالسهر والحمى)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٠١١)، ومسلم (٢٥٨٦).

13352 — Al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The example of the believers in their mutual love, mercy, and compassion is like that of a single body. When one limb suffers, the rest of the body responds with sleeplessness and fever.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6011) and Muslim (2586).

١٣٣٥٣ — عن سهل بن سعد الساعدي، عن النبي ﷺ قال:
((إن المؤمن من أهل الإيمان بمنزلة الرأس من الجسد، يألم المؤمن لأهل الإيمان كما يألم الجسد لما في الرأس)).
حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٢٨٧٧) واللفظ له، والطبراني في الكبير (٦/١٦٠-١٦١)، والطبراني في الأوسط (٤٦٩٣).

13353 — Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Sāʿidī narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“A believer among the people of faith is like the head in relation to the body. The believer feels pain for the people of faith just as the body feels pain because of what afflicts the head.”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (22877), whose wording is given here, al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (6/160–161), and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ (4693).

١٣٣٥٤ — عن أبي جبيرة بن الضحاك قال: فينا نزلت الآية، قدم رسول اللّٰه ﷺ المدينة وما منا رجل إلا له اسمان أو ثلاثة، كان إذا دعا الرجل بالاسم قلنا: يا رسول اللّٰه، إنه يغضب من هذا، فأنزلت: ﴿وَلَا تَنَابَزُوا بِالْأَلْقَابِ بِئْسَ الِاسْمُ الْفُسُوقُ بَعْدَ الْإِيمَانِ وَمَنْ لَمْ يَتُبْ فَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾.
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٤٩٦٢)، والترمذي (٣٢٦٨)، وابن ماجه (٣٧٤١)، وصححه ابن حبان (٥٧٠٩)، والحاكم (٢/٤٦٣).

english_source:
13354 — Abū Jubayrah ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk narrated:
This verse was revealed concerning us.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in Madinah, every man among us had two or three names.
When the Prophet ﷺ called a man by one of those names, we would say:
“O Messenger of Allah, he becomes angry when he is called by that name.”
Then Allah revealed:
“Do not call one another by offensive nicknames. Evil indeed is the name of wickedness after faith, and whoever does not repent—it is they who are the wrongdoers.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4962), al-Tirmidhī (3268), Ibn Mājah (3741), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (5709) and al-Ḥākim (2/463).

١٣٣٥٥ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال:
((إياكم والظن، فإن الظن أكذب الحديث، ولا تجسسوا، ولا تحسسوا، ولا تنافسوا، ولا تحاسدوا، ولا تباغضوا، ولا تدابروا، وكونوا عباد اللّٰه إخوانًا)).
متفق عليه: رواه مالك في حسن الخلق (١٥)، والبخاري (٦٠٦٦)، ومسلم (٢٥٦٣).

13355 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the falsest of speech. Do not spy, do not seek out one another’s faults, do not compete against one another in a blameworthy way, do not envy one another, do not hate one another, and do not turn your backs on one another. Rather, be servants of Allah as brothers.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Mālik in Ḥusn al-Khuluq (15), al-Bukhārī (6066), and Muslim (2563).

Do not spy, do not seek out one another’s faults, do not compete against one another in a blameworthy way, do not envy one another, do not hate one another, and do not turn your backs on one another. Rather, be servants of Allah as brothers.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Mālik in Ḥusn al-Khuluq (15), al-Bukhārī (6066), and Muslim (2563).

١٣٣٥٦ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((لا تحاسدوا، ولا تناجشوا، ولا تباغضوا، ولا تدابروا، ولا يبع بعضكم على بيع بعض، وكونوا عباد اللّٰه إخوانًا، المسلم أخو المسلم، لا يظلمه، ولا يخذله، ولا يحقره، التقوى هاهنا)).
ويشير إلى صدره ثلاث مرات:
((بحسب امرئ من الشر أن يحقر أخاه المسلم، كل المسلم على المسلم حرام: دمه وماله وعرضه)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٥٦٤).

13356 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Do not envy one another, do not artificially inflate prices against one another, do not hate one another, do not turn your backs on one another, and do not enter into a sale after another has already concluded a sale. Rather, be servants of Allah as brothers.
The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim: he does not wrong him, abandon him, or look down upon him. God-consciousness is here.”
He pointed to his chest three times.
Then he said:
“It is sufficient evil for a person to look down upon his Muslim brother. Everything belonging to a Muslim is inviolable to another Muslim: his blood, his wealth, and his honor.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2564).

“Do not hate one another, do not envy one another, do not turn your backs on one another, and be servants of Allah as brothers. It is not lawful for a Muslim to abandon his brother for more than three nights.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Mālik in Ḥusn al-Khuluq (14), al-Bukhārī (6076), and Muslim (2559).

١٣٣٥٨ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال:
((أتدرون ما الغيبة؟)).
قالوا: اللّٰه ورسوله أعلم.
قال:
((ذكرك أخاك بما يكره)).
قيل: أفرأيت إن كان في أخي ما أقول؟
قال:
((إن كان فيه ما تقول فقد اغتبته، وإن لم يكن فيه فقد بهته)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٥٨٩).

english_source:
13358 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Do you know what backbiting is?”
They replied:
“Allah and His Messenger know best.”
He said:
“It is mentioning your brother in a way that he dislikes.”
Someone asked:
“What if what I say about my brother is actually true?”
He replied:
“If what you say is true, then you have backbitten him; and if it is not true, then you have slandered him.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2589).

١٣٣٥٩ — عن عائشة قالت: حكيت للنبي ﷺ رجلًا، فقال:
((ما يسرني أني حكيت رجلًا وأن لي كذا وكذا)).
قالت: فقلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، إن صفية امرأة - وقال بيده، كأنه يعني قصيرة - فقال:
((لقد مزجت بكلمة لو مزج بها ماء البحر لمزجته)).
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٤٨٧٥)، والترمذي (٢٥٠٢، ٢٥٠٣)، وأحمد (٢٥٥٦٠).

13359 — ʿĀʾishah narrated:
I imitated a man in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ.
He said:
“I would not like to imitate a person, even if I were given such-and-such in return.”
She said:
I then said:
“O Messenger of Allah, Ṣafiyyah is a woman who is…”
and she gestured with her hand, apparently meaning that she was short.
He said:
“You have uttered a word which, if it were mixed with the water of the sea, would corrupt it.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4875), al-Tirmidhī (2502, 2503), and Aḥmad (25560).

١٣٣٦٠ — عن أبي برزة الأسلمي قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((يا معشر من آمن بلسانه ولم يدخل الإيمان قلبه، لا تغتابوا المسلمين، ولا تتبعوا عوراتهم، فإنه من اتبع عوراتهم يتبع اللّٰه عورته، ومن يتبع اللّٰه عورته يفضحه في بيته)).
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٤٨٨٠)، وأحمد (١٩٧٧٦)، وأبو يعلى (٧٤٢٣)، والبيهقي في الكبرى (١٠/٢٤٧).

13360 — Abū Barzah al-Aslamī narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“O people who have believed with their tongues while faith has not entered their hearts, do not backbite the Muslims and do not pursue their private faults. Whoever pursues their faults, Allah will pursue his faults; and whoever Allah pursues for his faults, He will disgrace him even within his own home.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4880), Aḥmad (19776), Abū Yaʿlā (7423), and al-Bayhaqī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (10/247).

Whoever pursues their faults, Allah will pursue his faults; and whoever Allah pursues for his faults, He will disgrace him even within his own home.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4880), Aḥmad (19776), Abū Yaʿlā (7423), and al-Bayhaqī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (10/247).

((يا معشر من آمن بلسانه، لا تغتابوا المسلمين، ولا تتبعوا عوراتهم، فإنه من تتبع عورة أخيه تتبع اللّٰه عورته، ومن تتبع اللّٰه عورته يفضحه في جوف بيته)).
حسن: رواه أبو يعلى (١٦٧٥).

١٣٣٦٢ — عن ابن عمر قال: صعد رسول اللّٰه ﷺ المنبر فنادى بصوت رفيع فقال:
((يا معشر من قد أسلم بلسانه ولم يفض الإيمان إلى قلبه، لا تؤذوا المسلمين، ولا تعيروهم، ولا تتبعوا عوراتهم، فإنه من تتبع عورة أخيه المسلم تتبع اللّٰه عورته، ومن تتبع اللّٰه عورته يفضحه ولو في جوف رحله)).
قال: ونظر ابن عمر يومًا إلى البيت - أو إلى الكعبة - فقال: ما أعظمك، وأعظم حرمتك، والمؤمن أعظم حرمة عند اللّٰه منك.
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٢٠٣٢)، وابن حبان (٥٧٦٣).

13362 — Ibn ʿUmar narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ascended the pulpit and called out in a loud voice:
“O people who have submitted with their tongues while faith has not reached their hearts, do not harm the Muslims, do not shame them, and do not pursue their private faults. Whoever pursues the fault of his Muslim brother, Allah will pursue his fault; and whoever Allah pursues for his fault, He will disgrace him even inside his own dwelling.”
Ibn ʿUmar once looked at the House—or the Kaʿbah—and said:
“How magnificent you are, and how great your sanctity! Yet the believer is even more sacred to Allah than you.”
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (2032) and Ibn Ḥibbān (5763).

١٣٣٦٣ — عن جابر قال: هاجت ريح منتنة على عهد رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((إن ناسًا من المنافقين اغتابوا أناسًا من المسلمين، فبعثت هذه الريح لذلك)).
وفي رواية عنه قال: كنا مع النبي ﷺ، فارتفعت ريح جيفة منتنة، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
((أتدرون ما هذه الريح؟ هذه ريح الذين يغتابون المؤمنين)).
صحيح: رواه عبد بن حميد (١٠٢٨)، والبخاري في الأدب المفرد (٧٣٣)، والخرائطي في مساوئ الأخلاق (١٨٧).
والرواية الثانية: رواها أحمد (١٤٧٨٤)، والبخاري في الأدب المفرد (٧٣٢).

13363 — Jābir narrated:
A foul-smelling wind arose during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Some of the hypocrites have been backbiting some of the Muslims, and this wind has been sent because of that.”
In another narration from him:
We were with the Prophet ﷺ when the stench of a decaying carcass arose.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Do you know what this smell is? This is the smell of those who backbite the believers.”
Authentic: The first narration was narrated by ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd (1028), al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (733), and al-Kharāʾiṭī in Masāwiʾ al-Akhlāq (187).
The second narration: Narrated by Aḥmad (14784) and al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (732).

((لما عرج بي مررت بقوم لهم أظفار من نحاس يخمشون بها وجوههم وصدورهم، فقلت: من هؤلاء يا جبريل؟ قال: هؤلاء الذين يأكلون لحوم الناس، ويقعون في أعراضهم)).

13364 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“When I was taken up through the heavens, I passed by people who had fingernails of copper with which they were scratching their faces and chests.
I asked: ‘Who are these, O Jibrīl?’
He replied: ‘These are the people who used to eat the flesh of others and attack their honor.’”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4878) and Aḥmad (13340).

١٣٣٦٥ — عن أنس قال: كانت العرب تخدم بعضها بعضًا في الأسفار، وكان مع أبي بكر وعمر رجل يخدمهما، فنام، فاستيقظا ولم يهيئ طعامًا، فقال: إن هذا لنؤوم بينكم، فأيقظاه، فقالا: ائت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقل له: إن أبا بكر وعمر يقرئانك السلام، وهما يستأدمانك.
فأتاه فقال، فقال:
((أخبرهما أنهما قد ائتدما)).
ففزعا، فجاءا إلى النبي ﷺ، فقالا: يا رسول اللّٰه، بعثنا نستأدمك، فقلت: ائتدما، فبأي شيء ائتدمنا؟
فقال:
((بأكلكما لحم أخيكما، إني لأرى لحمه بين ثناياكما)).
فقالا: يا رسول اللّٰه، فاستغفر لنا.
قال:
((هو فليستغفر لكما)).
حسن: رواه الخرائطي في مساوئ الأخلاق (١٨٦)، والضياء المقدسي في المختارة (١٦٩٦، ١٦٩٧).
